Recording a deed in Alcona County

Deeds and mortgages for Alcona County property are filed with the Register of Deeds in Harrisville. Call 989-724-9450 (fax 989-724-9459). The office is the official recording point for papers that touch real estate, and it works under a uniform state system.

It accepts warranty and quitclaim deeds, mortgages with their assignments and discharges, land contracts, liens and releases, easements, rights of way, oil and gas leases, plats, surveys, land corners and court orders. It also takes passport applications.

Counter staff cannot draft your deed or answer legal questions, so lean on a lawyer or the closing agent for that. The county closes on holidays such as Columbus Day, Thanksgiving and the Friday after, so phone ahead before you carry a signed original to the courthouse.

Fees at the Alcona County counter

Recording costs $30.00 per paper regardless of length, a figure fixed in MCL 600.2567. A few add-ons exist:

  • $3.00 extra for every further instrument when one document assigns or discharges several.
  • $1.00 a page for photocopies of the record, with $5.00 on top to certify.
  • $5.00 for the treasurer's tax certificate, which spans up to five property descriptions, then 20 cents per added description.

Mailing a deed in has quirks. Enclose a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. If your check overshoots the fee by $10.00 or less, the county keeps the difference, so total the charges before you send anything.

Which papers need the treasurer's certificate first?

Warranty deeds, land contracts and their assignments, condominium master deeds, subdivision plats and any deed that conveys with a warranty must arrive with a certificate from the Treasurer's Office, 989-724-9420.

Make this stop first on your errand list, since the certificate travels with the deed to the register. Holding a different form, such as a quitclaim? Ask the register whether the same rule reaches it.

The same counter can tell you whether any tax is still unpaid on the parcel. Knowing that number before you pick a closing date avoids a last-minute surprise.

Michigan transfer tax on an Alcona County sale

Two levies fall on the seller. The county charges $0.55 for each $500 of value (MCL 207.504) and the state charges $3.75 for each $500 (MCL 207.525). Any leftover amount is rounded up to a full $500.

Transfer tax rates on an Alcona County sale
LevelRate per $500Who pays
County$0.55Seller
State$3.75Seller
Both levels$4.30Seller

The county treasurer collects within 15 days of delivery (MCL 207.523). Put the full price on the face of the deed, or file a value affidavit with it. Ask the closing agent to total the tax on your settlement statement so you see the figure before you sign.

Can a family transfer avoid the transfer tax?

Often yes. MCL 207.526 carves out gifts inside a family, which is the usual case for heirs and aging owners.

  • Parent to child, including a stepchild or adopted child.
  • Grandparent to grandchild, including step and adopted grandchildren.
  • Spouses creating or ending a tenancy by the entireties.
  • Any instrument carrying consideration under $100.
  • A corrective deed that confirms title the grantee already holds.

If you paid and then learn an exemption applied, the state Treasury Department takes refund requests.

Why might Alcona County turn a deed away?

Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, gives a register grounds to refuse papers that break its layout rules. Four checks cover most trouble:

  • Leave a clear top margin of 2 1/2 inches on page one.
  • Open with a single line that names the event, such as "Warranty Deed."
  • Use 10-point or larger type in black ink on white 20-pound stock.
  • Print the drafter's name and business address on the paper.

Keep one event per sheet. A first line claiming two recordable events, such as a deed plus a release, bars recording. Ask your title agent to review the deed before signing, since a rejected paper can push back a closing.

Other Alcona County offices that touch a sale

Several county desks can matter when a house sells, and the directory on the county home page gives each one's line.

  • Treasurer, 989-724-9420: tax certificates and balances.
  • Equalization, 989-724-9430: assessed and taxable values.
  • Building Department, 989-724-9440: permits.
  • County Clerk, 989-724-9410, and Probate Court, 989-724-9490: records and estate matters when the owner has died.

Alcona County sits in Michigan's 23rd Circuit, shared with Arenac, Iosco and Oscoda counties. An heir selling an inherited house should ask Probate Court what paperwork the deed needs before anything goes to the register.

Zoning, permits and assessments sit with townships and the county, not with the register. Call Equalization or the Building Department if a permit or valuation question could hold up your sale.

About Alcona County

Harrisville is the sole city and the county seat, and Lincoln is the village. The county has about 10,556 residents spread over 1,791 square miles, 62 percent of which is water, mostly Lake Huron and inland lakes such as Hubbard Lake. Many properties are lakefront, seasonal or inherited, and about 89.6 percent of housing is occupied by its owner.

That mix affects a sale. A seasonal or inherited house may have an old survey, a septic system and a tax history spread across several years, so gather the deed, the tax certificate and any permit records before you list. If the owner has died, start with Probate Court so the right person signs the deed, and ask the Treasurer whether any tax is outstanding before a closing date is set.

Selling an Alcona County house: a short checklist

Here is the usual order of steps for a seller who needs the deed recorded without delay:

  1. Call the Treasurer at 989-724-9420 for the tax balance and the certificate, if the deed is a warranty deed.
  2. Have a lawyer or title agent draft the deed to the layout rules above.
  3. Confirm the price on the deed, or prepare a value affidavit.
  4. Pay the $30.00 recording fee, plus any add-ons, and the transfer tax within 15 days.
  5. Keep copies. The register can furnish certified copies at $1.00 a page plus $5.00 to certify.

If the house is vacant, inherited or behind on tax, a cash as-is sale can shorten the list, since you do not have to wait on a buyer's lender. You are free to decline any offer. Whichever way you sell, confirm with the register before you mail anything, since the office can tell you the exact total to include with the paper.

Frequently asked questions

What is the filing price for a deed in Alcona County?

It is $30.00 a document. A paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3.00 for each extra, and copies of records cost $1.00 a page.

Who must pay the transfer tax in an Alcona County sale?

The seller must, since MCL 207.523 puts the liability on the grantor. The county treasurer expects payment inside 15 days from delivery of the deed.

Is a treasurer's certificate required before an Alcona County warranty deed is recorded?

Yes. The Treasurer's Office issues it at 989-724-9420 for $5.00 per document with up to five descriptions.

Can a deed go to the Alcona County register by mail?

Yes, if you add a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself. Any mailed overpayment of $10.00 or under becomes county revenue.

Is there an online search for Alcona County land records?

Yes, two fee-based tools: Laredo, which works by subscription, and Tapestry. Ask the register at 989-724-9450 how to sign up for Laredo.

Filing a deed with Allegan County

Paper and electronic filing both work. The register's page lists three e-recording vendors with direct lines: CSC (866-652-0111), Simplifile (800-460-5657) and ePN, the E-Recording Partners Network (888-325-3365). Title companies normally use one of these, which spares most sellers any contact with them. The register's phone is 269-673-0390.

The same page links a land records search portal and the state recording requirements. After filing, the register enters the paper in a book called a liber and stamps that reference on the document. An image becomes the permanent record, and the office does not keep the original deed or mortgage.

Counter staff do not prepare documents or answer legal questions, and they refer people to an attorney or title company. One protection for senders comes from MCL 565.201: a register may not refuse a compliant paper over its wording, and a paper already recorded is presumed to comply. The format rules are the real hurdle, so let the title agent look over the deed before signing.

Recording and copy fees

One flat $30 covers a recording of any length, as MCL 600.2567 provides. The remaining items on the statutory list are short.

  • $3 on top for every further instrument that a single paper assigns or discharges.
  • $1 per page of copies, and a $5 certification charge.
  • Grantor and grantee searches at 50 cents per year examined, minimum $5.
  • $1 for filing or looking up any other paper.

Fees are due when the paper is left. For electronic filings the fee can follow electronically, up to one business day after receipt. For copy purposes, a "page" is one side of a sheet measuring 8 1/2 by 11 up to 14 inches, in paper of 20 pound weight or more.

How much transfer tax is due on an Allegan County sale?

The seller pays two taxes that together come to $4.30 for each $500 of value, rounding a partial $500 upward.

Transfer tax rates on an Allegan County sale
LevelRate per $500Paid by
County$0.55Seller
State$3.75Seller
Combined$4.30Seller

The seller carries liability under MCL 207.523, although a buyer may pay on the seller's behalf. Payment reaches the county treasurer no later than 15 days after the instrument is delivered. Ask the title agent to show the tax on your settlement statement before you sign.

Which transfers can skip the tax?

MCL 207.526 exempts a list of transfers, and a few come up often with houses in a lake or farm county like this one.

  • A deed that only straightens a boundary line when no money changes hands.
  • A quitclaim deed given to confirm a title the grantee already holds, such as one that corrects a flaw.
  • A transfer between a limited liability company and its members when ownership shares are unchanged.
  • A transfer between a partnership and its partners on the same terms.
  • A deed in which the grantor is a government body or officer acting officially.

Anyone relying on one of these should say so to the title agent before closing. A refund request goes to the Department of Treasury.

Other services from the register

The office runs a free Property Fraud Alert. An owner or business enters a name and gets a notice whenever a recorded document matches it, which gives early warning of a forged deed or a lien filed against you.

The register also posts Plat Board public notices, which matter to anyone splitting a parcel before a sale. A related treasurer form covers tax certification for land divisions and lot line adjustments, with its own instructions.

U.S. passport applications are taken at the office by appointment only, between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays.

What does the Allegan County Treasurer handle in a sale?

The Treasurer's Office certifies deeds, keeps tax histories, and collects delinquent real estate tax for the 35 townships, cities and villages in the county. The county runs the whole tax reversion process in-house, including title searches, court hearings, foreclosure and sale.

A seller with delinquent tax should talk to the treasurer's staff first, because the office advances delinquent amounts to the local units through its revolving fund. The treasurer's pages link to pay delinquent taxes, search tax records and view foreclosure sales.

Former owners can also claim leftover foreclosure proceeds. A person with title or equity files Form 5743 with the county treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county replies by January 31 after the auctions with Form 5744, and a court motion may follow between February 1 and May 15. These steps come from MCL 211.78t.

Who sets and bills property tax?

Assessing happens at the township or city level. The county Equalization Department publishes property records, a list of township and city assessors, equalization reports and a tax levies and millages page.

Because 24 townships, 9 cities and 2 villages each act as their own unit, the correct office depends on the parcel. The county directory lists addresses and phone lines for all of them, such as Allegan Township at 269-673-5051, Otsego City Hall at 269-692-3391 and Holland City Hall at 616-355-1300.

Ask your township or city for the current tax balance before you list the house.

Allegan County at a glance

The county seat is the city of Allegan, and Holland is the largest city. The Lake Michigan shore draws vacation homes, especially around Saugatuck and Douglas, and much of the inland area is farmland. The 2025 population estimate is 123,188, and owners live in 87.4 percent of homes.

Many sellers here own lakeshore cottages, second homes or farm parcels. Those often involve a survey, a land division or an old tax history, so check with the township about splits before you list, and ask the treasurer about tax certification when a parcel is divided.

Steps for an Allegan County seller

  1. Ask your township or city for the current tax balance.
  2. Have the title agent review the deed against the state format rules.
  3. Choose paper or e-recording. Most title companies use CSC, Simplifile or ePN.
  4. Pay the $30 recording fee and any add-ons, then the transfer tax within 15 days.
  5. Turn on the free Property Fraud Alert so you hear about any later filing in your name.

If the house has delinquent tax, call the treasurer before you set a closing date. A cash as-is sale can fit when you need a firm date, and any offer is yours to decline. Keep your recorded deed image and the liber reference, since the office does not hold the original paper.

Frequently asked questions

Which e-recording services does Allegan County accept?

It accepts CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Their phone lines are 866-652-0111, 800-460-5657 and 888-325-3365.

How much does a deed cost to record in Allegan County?

A recording costs $30 per document. Add $3 per further instrument assigned or discharged, $1 a page for copies and $5 for certification.

Who pays the transfer tax on an Allegan County sale?

The seller is liable, at $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state. A buyer may pay on the seller's behalf, and payment goes to the county treasurer within 15 days.

Will the Allegan County register prepare my deed?

No. The office neither drafts documents nor answers legal questions, so an attorney or title company must do that.

How does a former owner claim surplus from an Allegan County foreclosure sale?

Send Form 5743 to the county treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county replies by January 31 with Form 5744, and a court motion may follow.

Hours and cutoffs at the Alpena County recording desk

The register works out of 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, and answers at 989-354-9547 (fax 989-354-9646). Hours run 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

Recording cutoffs come sooner than closing time. An e-filing must land by 3:30 p.m. to count that day, and paper has until 4:00 p.m. at the window. Anything later joins the next business day's pile, so a Friday 4:15 delivery waits for Monday.

The register insists on originals. Once indexed, the original is returned to the sender, normally inside seven days of recording. No blank deeds are given out, and staff cannot coach you through completing one. Visit an office supply store, a lawyer or a title company for that.

A deed that is ready early saves trouble. Sellers who sign on a Friday afternoon often find the paper waits until Monday, so plan the signing and the delivery for earlier in the day and earlier in the week.

Recording and copy fees

Most Michigan counties follow MCL 600.2567, which prices a recording at one flat sum no matter the number of pages. A charter county can override that by ordinance, so phone the register for the exact total before a check goes in the mail.

  • $30 for every recorded paper, and $3 more for each extra instrument it assigns or discharges.
  • Copies at $1 per page and certification at $5.
  • Index searches at 50 cents a year for grantor and grantee names, never less than $5.
  • A tax certification fee on certain deeds. Ask the Alpena County treasurer whether yours qualifies.

The county office page links to a fee sheet, a recording requirements sheet and e-recording instructions.

Search and alert tools

Researchers can choose Laredo or Tapestry. Tapestry fits someone who needs a copy or two, and Laredo suits title companies and frequent searchers.

Two free services cover Alpena County only: a property fraud alert and a notary fraud alert. Each sends a call, text or email when a recorded paper carries your name.

The same office is a certified passport agent and takes passport photos, so some visitors are there for a passport. If you want to watch for fraud, sign up for the property alert at no cost, and add the notary alert if you often use a notary.

What will state and county transfer tax cost on an Alpena County house?

On each $500 of value, the seller pays 55 cents to the county (MCL 207.504) and $3.75 to the state (MCL 207.525). A partial $500 counts as a full one.

Transfer tax rates on an Alpena County sale
LevelRate per $500Paid to
County$0.55County treasurer
State$3.75County treasurer, for the state
Both$4.30County treasurer

Remit it to the Alpena County treasurer inside 15 days after delivery. When furniture or equipment rides along, only the real estate is taxed, as long as the deed or an attached affidavit lists the values separately. The county treasurer is also the person to ask about any tax still owed on the parcel, so call before you pick a closing date.

Distress and court transfers that escape the tax

Distressed owners and heirs should read MCL 207.526, because several exemptions fit their situations.

  • A deed handed to a lender in foreclosure or in place of it. The lender's own resale is still taxed.
  • A court of record's order moving title, when no price is set.
  • An installment land contract, while legal title sits with the seller.
  • Husband and wife moving property into or out of a tenancy by the entireties.

Paid in error? Treasury takes refund requests.

What details on a deed trip up a recording?

Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, lets a register refuse a paper that skips basic identification steps. Returns usually trace to one of these:

  • A signer's printed name that differs from the name in the notary's certificate.
  • Ink that is not black or dark blue.
  • No notary name printed next to the notary's signature.
  • No street address for the buyer, or no drafter name and address.
  • A full Social Security number left visible.
  • Foreign-language text without an English version attached.

Once a paper satisfies the act, the register has no right to refuse it over what it says.

Timing a deed against the cutoffs

Start the e-record by early afternoon, because the 3:30 p.m. cutoff arrives half an hour before the counter's 4:00. Before signing, run through a short list:

  • The buyer's mailing address appears on the deed.
  • The notary's name is printed beside the signature.
  • The full sale value is stated, or a value affidavit is attached.
  • The original, not a copy, goes to the register.
  • Any tax certification step has been cleared with the county treasurer.

Miss the cutoff and your record date moves to the next business day. On a closing that depends on recording, that can mean a weekend wait, so plan the signing for the morning.

Alpena County for a home seller

Alpena County sits in the northeast of Michigan's Lower Peninsula, fronting Lake Huron and Thunder Bay. Alpena is the county seat and its only city, and Hillman is a village that straddles the county line. U.S. 23 hugs the shoreline, M-32 ends in downtown Alpena, and M-65 offers a quicker way south. About 28,853 people live here, and four of every five homes are lived in by their owners.

Assessments are a local matter, so a seller with a parcel question should call the city or township assessor, not the register. Many properties are lakefront or inherited, so expect a buyer to ask about survey, access and tax history. The county recorded 72 building permits in 2025, and permit questions go to the local building office.

Selling an Alpena County house: a short plan

  1. Ask the county treasurer about the tax balance and whether a tax certification applies to your deed.
  2. Have a lawyer or title company prepare the deed, since the register cannot.
  3. Check the deed against the list above: names, ink, notary, buyer address and sale value.
  4. Pick e-recording or paper, and send it before the cutoff.
  5. Watch for the returned original within about seven days of recording.

If the house is inherited, behind on tax or in poor shape, a cash as-is sale can shorten the wait for a buyer's loan. Treat any offer as one option and compare it with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and months of carrying costs. Whichever route you take, keep a copy of the recorded deed.

Frequently asked questions

What is the last time of day to record a deed in Alpena County?

Paper filings are taken until 4:00 p.m. and e-recordings until 3:30 p.m. A deed that arrives later is recorded on the next business day.

How can I contact the Alpena County Register of Deeds?

Phone 989-354-9547 or fax 989-354-9646, or visit 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, in Alpena.

Will my original deed come back from the Alpena County register?

Yes. The office indexes the paper and then returns the original, usually within a week of the recording date.

How much transfer tax applies to an Alpena County sale?

The seller pays $0.55 per $500 to the county and $3.75 per $500 to the state, which is $4.30 together. Each rate applies to every $500 or fraction thereof.

Can Alpena County staff write or advise on my deed?

No. They do not complete documents, give legal advice or provide blank deeds. A title company, an attorney or an office supply store can help instead.

Where Antrim County property records are kept

Deeds, mortgages and liens on Antrim County land are filed with the Register of Deeds at the county building in Bellaire. The office keeps a grantor and grantee index and serves weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00. The register also chairs the County Plat Board, the body that reviews new subdivisions before they can be sold off in lots.

Bring the original signed deed, the fee and a return address for the recorded copy. Staff index the grantor and grantee names so later title searches can find the deed.

Filings reach back to 1856. Computer images start in January 1990, and older entries sit in bound books. The name index covering the whole life of the county can be searched at no charge at a public terminal, though you reserve a slot by appointment.

Timing matters. Michigan runs a race-notice system, so a recorded deed puts every later buyer on notice, and the office stamps and numbers each paper in the order it lands on the counter. A lake cottage that changes hands in July should have its deed filed the day the money moves.

Recording fees

Antrim charges a flat $30.00 for each document it records, whether the deed runs one page or twelve. A few other items matter at a sale.

  • When one paper handles more than one assignment or discharge, add $3.00 for every instrument past the first.
  • Warranty deeds, any deed carrying a covenant of warranty, and land contracts (plus assignments or amendments that touch the legal description) need a $5.00 treasurer's certificate.
  • Photocopies cost $1.00 a page, plat copies $2.00 a page, and a certified copy costs $5.00 for its first page.

The office accepts a check, cash or a credit card. Make checks out to the Antrim County Register of Deeds, and expect the certificate to be handled through the treasurer's window.

Antrim County recording and copy fees
ServiceAmount
Record a deed, mortgage or lien$30.00
Each added instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
Tax certificate (County Treasurer)$5.00

Transfer tax on an Antrim County sale

The tax is charged per $500 of the price, with any leftover fraction counted as a full block, and it is paid at recording. Michigan register offices post a state share of $3.75 per block plus a county share of $0.55, which adds up to $4.30. Ask the Antrim office to confirm its county share before closing. Your bill follows the real sale price on the deed.

The state act lists transfers that owe nothing. The exempt group in MCL 207.526 includes:

  • a gift deed running to a son, daughter, stepchild or grandchild;
  • transfers by foreclosure or by a deed in lieu of foreclosure;
  • court orders that move title without naming a money amount;
  • a quitclaim that repairs a title flaw by confirming what the grantee already holds;
  • any instrument where the price is below $100.

The deed text itself must name the exemption claimed, or the office will collect the tax.

Filing electronically or by drop-off

You can do either. The register recommends e-recording through Simplifile or EPN, and still accepts the post office, FedEx, UPS and similar carriers. A drop box at the southeast corner of the county building takes hand deliveries, but it is only checked periodically, so a deed on a closing deadline should go another way.

Slip a return envelope with postage into anything you mail, and the original comes back once it is indexed. Staff can say what a filing needs, yet drafting a deed or picking a form is outside their role.

At a normal sale none of this lands on the seller. The closing agent signs the deed with you, adds the transfer tax and the treasurer's $5.00 certificate, and sends the package in electronically. Owners handling an inherited cabin by hand should call the office before they file.

Property tax bills and old balances

Your village or township bills the year in progress. The County Treasurer takes only earlier years and delinquent accounts. Summer bills go out in July and are due to the village or township on September 14. Township winter tax is billed in December and due February 14.

To pay a past-year balance, send a check to the treasurer at PO Box 544, Bellaire, MI 49615, pay by card online or by phone at 231-533-6720, or use the secure drop box outside the public entrance. Card payments add 2.95 percent, with a $3.99 minimum. People who may qualify for help can ask the treasurer about the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services.

Selling with taxes owed

If the parcel carries an unpaid balance, call the treasurer for a payoff figure before the house goes on the market. The closing agent deducts that sum from what you receive, so knowing it early lets you judge your net.

For a standard sale, expect this sequence. The buyer's title company orders a tax search, you sign the deed, the agent collects transfer tax and the $5.00 certificate where one is required, and the package is recorded in Bellaire the same day or close to it. A payoff for an old balance is settled at the same table. If you sell for cash and as-is, the same recording steps apply, but there is usually no lender appraisal or repair request to wait on.

Antrim County housing at a glance

Antrim covers 602 square miles of northwest lower Michigan, and 126 of them are water, with Torch Lake and much of the Chain of Lakes inside the county. Bellaire is the seat. Population is estimated at 24,698 for 2025, and owners occupy 86.4 percent of 11,100 households. Median gross rent is $902 a month and median owner cost with a mortgage is $1,462. A shoreline lot at Elk Rapids and a woodland house near Mancelona sit in different markets, so get comparable sales from the immediate area.

Many houses in the county are seasonal or came through an estate. A place closed up through several winters can need roof, plumbing or septic work before a financed buyer will go ahead. A buyer who takes the house in its current condition skips that repair list, which draws some owners to a cash sale.

Frequently asked questions

What is the filing fee for an Antrim County deed?

The fee is $30.00 for a document of any length. Each extra assignment or discharge on the same paper adds $3.00, and warranty deeds and land contracts also need the $5.00 treasurer's certificate.

Does the Antrim County office take deeds by e-recording?

Yes, through Simplifile or EPN, which the register encourages. Paper still works by mail, by carrier, or through the box at the building's southeast corner.

Which office collects this year's tax on an Antrim County house?

The village or township holds the current year's tax roll. The county treasurer steps in for prior years and delinquent bills, and the due dates for summer and winter township tax are September 14 and February 14.

Will the register's staff prepare my deed?

No. They can describe what the office needs, but writing the deed is left to a preparer you hire. Heirs and sellers working without a closing agent should line one up first.

Is a deed to my daughter taxed as a sale in Antrim County?

MCL 207.526 exempts a parent's conveyance to a child from the state tax, provided the deed names the exemption in its text. Confirm the exact language for the county side with the register before you sign.

What the Arenac County Register of Deeds does

Standish is home to the office that records Arenac County land papers: deeds, mortgages, discharges and any other instrument that transfers or encumbers property. A signed deed only becomes public record here, and this counter also collects the state and county transfer taxes. The phone number is (989) 846-9201.

The office runs a land notification service that emails you whenever a new document is recorded against your property. Heirs, and owners of seasonal places that sit empty, may want it turned on before listing.

The office also stamps and indexes each instrument, which is what lets a later buyer or lender find it by name. If you plan to list a house that came through an estate, check that every earlier deed or death certificate needed to show your authority is already on file.

Recording charges

Every document filed in Arenac County pays $30.00, however many pages it has. The flat fee rests on MCL 600.2657 and took effect on October 1, 2016.

When one document assigns or discharges more than a single instrument, the office adds $3.00 for each instrument beyond the first. A payoff release that clears two recorded mortgages, for example, takes one extra $3.00.

Arenac County recording and transfer tax rates
ChargeRate
Recording any document$30.00 flat
Each added instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
County transfer tax$0.55 per $500 or fraction
State transfer tax$3.75 per $500 or fraction
Transfer tax applies when the value is$100 or more

Pay when you file. A mailed deed should come with a check for the full recording fee and transfer tax, and an address for the return of the recorded original. Call (989) 846-9201 to confirm the total if the deed covers several instruments or parcels, because extra instruments are charged separately.

Transfer tax on an Arenac County house

Add the county's 55 cents to the state's $3.75 and a sale pays $4.30 per $500 of price, with a leftover partial $500 counted as a whole one. Your sale is taxed on its own price, so ask the closing agent for the figure before signing.

The deed should show the property's value. A real estate valuation affidavit can be filed in its place at no charge, provided the deed says an affidavit is being filed. The statutes for this are MCL 207.511 and 207.525.

  • The office collects the tax unless the deed qualifies for a state exemption, a county exemption, or both.
  • The deed has to name the exemption, with the statute behind it (MCL 207.505 for the county, MCL 207.526 for the state).
  • State exemptions include a gift to a child or grandchild, a foreclosure transfer, and a deed that merely confirms title the buyer already has.

Searching Arenac County deeds online

Two separate tools cover the records. The county's online records site covers documents from February 11, 1991 forward, and it lets you search and buy copies of filings from 1992 to the present. Older index books are handled differently.

For anything before 1992, the office points researchers to RECORDhub. You make an account, pick one of the subscription plans Arenac County offers, and then view and print pages from deed books 1 through 214. That archive is how a family finds the chain of ownership on a farm or a lakeshore lot that has not changed hands for decades.

Online searching shows what is on file, but it does not replace a title search. If a seller spots an old easement, a lien or a name that differs from the deed, a title company can explain what it means before a buyer's lender asks.

Start with the owner's name exactly as the last deed spells it, the legal description if you have one, and the year of purchase. Work backward from the newest deed to see who holds title and whether any mortgage or lien remains open. Print what you find for your closing agent, who runs the formal search.

Who handles property tax bills

Ask the treasurer of the city, village or township where the parcel sits for the current tax bill, and ask the Arenac County Treasurer about any amount that has fallen behind. Each can give you a written figure to hand the closing agent.

The register does not handle tax collection, so questions about assessments or exemptions go to the local assessor or treasurer rather than to the deeds counter.

Take your recent tax bills to the first meeting with the closing agent. They show which local unit collects, and a past-due amount will be listed as owed to the county. Paying an old balance before listing is not required, but it removes a question from the buyer's side.

Selling with taxes owed

At a sale, an unpaid tax balance is normally paid from the seller's side of the closing statement. On an older or inherited house, request the payoff early, so the number you plan around matches the one the closing agent sees.

Closings here tend to run in a set order. A title search comes first, then you sign, then the closing agent totals transfer tax and any tax owed. The deed travels to Standish by mail or electronically and gets stamped and indexed. Any exemption must be written into the deed before you sign it. When a buyer pays cash and takes the house in its present state, no lender repair list slows things down, yet recording works the same way.

Find out early who carries each cost. Your purchase contract decides whether the seller or the buyer pays transfer tax and recording, and the settlement statement lists every Register of Deeds charge beside any tax payoff. Review that statement a day ahead if you can, and call the deeds office at (989) 846-9201 if a recording charge looks off.

Arenac County housing at a glance

Saginaw Bay on Lake Huron takes up 47 percent of Arenac County's 681 square miles, and Standish is the county seat. The county was created in 1831, folded into Bay County in 1857 and re-established on April 21, 1883, so anyone tracing an old farm deed should expect the records to reflect that history.

The 2025 population estimate is 15,068. There are 6,552 households, with 86.2 percent in owner-occupied homes, and median gross rent is $761. Median household income is $58,811. With homes valued near $150,600 at the median, a repair bill can swallow much of a seller's margin. A house that needs a roof, a furnace or a full cleanout may fit a cash buyer better.

Frequently asked questions

How do I contact the Arenac County deeds office by phone?

Call (989) 846-9201. Use that line with questions about recording, transfer tax or the online records subscription.

What does a deed filing cost at the Arenac office?

A deed pays $30.00 whatever its length. A paper that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3.00 for each one beyond the first.

What are the Arenac County transfer tax rates?

The county takes 55 cents per $500 and the state takes $3.75 per $500, rounded up for a partial block. A transfer worth $100 or more owes both unless the deed states an exemption.

Do I have to put the sale price on the deed?

Not if you file a real estate valuation affidavit instead. There is no fee for the affidavit, and the deed must say that one is being filed.

Where can I look at old Arenac County deed books?

Deed books 1 through 214 can be viewed on RECORDhub with a subscription plan from the county. Documents from 1992 forward are on the county's online records site.

Where to take a deed in Barry County

Go to Room 102 at the Barry County Courthouse, 220 W State Street, Hastings, MI 49058. The office is open Monday to Friday from 8:15 to 4:45, shuts for the noon hour, and answers at 269-945-1289 or bcrod@barrycounty.org. A recorded deed becomes public, but recording does not certify that the deed is legal.

Clerks record, index and preserve what arrives. They do not search titles, hand out blank forms or coach anyone on wording, so the deed itself comes from your closing agent or a lawyer. Nothing already on file can be altered, and a name added to or dropped from ownership means a brand-new deed gets signed and filed.

People sometimes ask for the "title" to a house. Most homes have none, since the recorded deed covers whatever is permanently fixed to the land. Certain mobile homes are the exception and may keep a separate title with the Secretary of State.

Before you go, call 269-945-1289 and ask what the packet needs. Bring the original deed, a check that covers the recording fee and the transfer tax, a second check for the treasurer's $5.00 certificate if the deed carries a warranty, and a stamped return envelope if you will not wait. Walk-in filers leave with the recorded copy the same day.

Recording charges

A flat $30.00 covers any document, and each added instrument number that a paper assigns or discharges brings another $3.00. Sale deeds and similar transfers owe state and county transfer tax on top, collected during recording. One payment to the Register of Deeds can cover the fee and the tax together.

One item travels separately. Land contracts, their assignments, warranty deeds and any deed with a warranty covenant require a Tax Certification from the Barry County Treasurer, priced at $5.00, written as its own check to the treasurer.

Barry County recording and copy charges
Service or taxAmount

The counter takes cash, checks, and debit or credit cards; cards add a small service fee.

Transfer tax on a Barry County sale

The seller carries the tax, set at $4.30 for every $500 of consideration, with any partial block rounded up. It is due the moment the deed is recorded.

Some transfers escape the tax, though staff will not choose an exemption on your behalf. A deed claiming one must show MCL 207.505 (county) or MCL 207.526 (state) plus the exemption's letter, and the county posts separate lists for each. Have your closing agent make that call.

  • A gift deed to your child or grandchild is on the state's exempt list.
  • The state tax also skips foreclosure transfers and deeds given in place of foreclosure.
  • A corrective deed that only confirms what the grantee already owns is exempt, as is any paper priced under $100.

The full state list sits in MCL 207.526.

What a Barry County deed must include

State statutes set recording standards, and Barry posts a checklist drawn from them. Run through it before filing.

  • Ink signatures in black or dark blue, original rather than copied, with each name typed or printed under it.
  • An acknowledgment taken by a judge, a court clerk or a notary in Michigan, with the notary's name typed on the signature page.
  • A street or post office address for each grantee, and the drafter's name and address.
  • A blank 2.5 inch strip at the top of page one, and half an inch of white space around the rest.
  • Readable black print no smaller than 10 point, on white 20 pound paper sized from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • The property's full value stated in the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit attached.
  • A certified death certificate recorded alongside, or ahead of, any deed that conveys by survivorship.

Photocopies are rejected. Court orders must carry the clerk's seal, and all other documents need original signatures.

Ways to file and when the paper comes back

You can carry the deed in, post it, or send it through an e-recording company. Barry names five: Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, Nationwide Title Clearing, EPN and CSC. A document sent by ordinary email is not recorded.

A paper that meets the standards is recorded the day it is received, and walk-in filers take the recorded copy home. Mail and drop-offs usually return in 2 to 4 business days. Enclose a stamped return envelope, or the office keeps the original for 90 days at least. Digital PDF returns through Swift are free and arranged with staff.

The treasurer issues electronic tax certifications only via Simplifile and CSC. Confirm that your closing agent's provider fits before signing day.

For an out-of-town seller, e-recording is usually the least trouble. The closing agent submits the signed deed, the provider forwards it to Hastings, and a PDF can come back by Swift at no charge. If you mail it instead, allow the 2 to 4 business days for return plus the time in the post.

Property tax and foreclosure questions

Property tax is outside the register's job. Ask the city or township for current bills and the Barry County Treasurer for delinquent amounts. If the parcel has back tax, get a payoff figure from the treasurer first, so the closing agent can pay it from your proceeds.

Foreclosures reach the office only after the sale occurs, so staff cannot say whether a house is set for sheriff's sale. After a sheriff's deed is recorded, the office takes the redemption payment but does not compute it. Open liens show up in a title search, run at the public workstations or through a title firm.

For ownership questions, start with the county's GIS property map. It follows the tax roll and shows the listed taxpayer, while the recorded deed settles who actually owns the parcel.

Barry County housing at a glance

Barry County's only city, Hastings, is also its seat. About 63,991 people lived here in 2025, in 24,480 households and 28,284 housing units. Owners occupy 87.3 percent of homes. Median value is $264,100 and median rent is $972. With a 27.7 minute average commute, drive time and condition both shape what buyers offer. Deferred repairs can block a mortgage, so some sellers turn to a cash buyer who will close as-is.

Frequently asked questions

When is the Barry County deeds counter open?

Monday through Friday, 8:15 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., closed at noon for an hour. Phone 269-945-1289 before a long drive in case hours change.

Can I email a deed to Barry County for recording?

No. Plain email cannot be recorded. Send it through an approved provider such as Simplifile, EPN or CSC, or deliver the signed original.

Who is responsible for transfer tax in a Barry County sale?

The seller, and payment falls due at recording. The rate is $4.30 per $500, split as $3.75 to the state and $0.55 to the county.

Can Barry County staff tell me who owns a parcel?

Not directly. Staff can only retrieve the latest deed under a given name. Check the GIS property map for the listed taxpayer, then search that name at a public workstation.

How can I order a copy of a recorded Barry County deed?

The office will mail or email a copy at $1.00 a page, with a $5.00 search charge when you lack the document number. A check has to reach them first, because payment is not taken by email or phone.

What the Bay County Register of Deeds does

Think of this office as the county's land filing cabinet. Deeds, mortgages, notices of pending suits and certified copies all land here to be indexed, and the resulting public record is what every title company reads before a Bay County closing.

The counter opens Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. through 5:00 p.m. Hands on research with staff wraps up a half hour sooner, and nobody locks the door at midday. Beginning January 1, 2018, each instrument receives a single Document Number in place of the old Liber and Page pair.

Sellers and heirs also find handy links on the office page, including a Bay County cemetery directory, contact details for local city and township officials, and state forms from Michigan.gov. Tax certifications carry their own $5 charge, paid to the Treasurer.

  • Doxpop offers search any hour of the day. Its help line, 1-866-369-7671, assists with account sign up.
  • Doxpop Property Watch emails you free of charge whenever someone attempts to transfer title to your land.
  • Approved eRecording partners are listed on the office page for electronic delivery.
  • A package sent by USPS, UPS or FedEx should include postage paid return packaging addressed to you.

Recording fees

The fee schedule sets a single price, $30.00 per document, for a deed, mortgage, lis pendens or any similar instrument. Out of each $30, four dollars move on to the state's survey and remonumentation program. Liens held by the state or federal government, fixture filings, plats, state deeds and tax reversion papers are not charged that four dollar share.

Bay County recording fees and transfer tax rates
Document or taxAmount
A deed, mortgage or comparable instrument$30.00 apiece
Assignment or discharge naming several instrumentsAdd $3.00 per extra instrument

The certificate comes from MCL 211.135 and covers deeds with a warranty clause, land contracts, land contract assignments that carry a warranty, and condominium master deeds.

Why a deed might be rejected

The office publishes sixteen rules taken from Michigan recording statutes. If a paper fails any of them it is sent back, and several lost days can upset a closing schedule. These are the flaws that catch sellers most.

  • Signatures must be live originals, with each signer's name typed or printed beneath the line and matching the notary's certificate exactly.
  • A deed has to give the grantee's street or post office address, and it also needs the name and address of the person who prepared it.
  • Any paper that conveys or burdens land needs an acknowledgment from a Michigan notary, judge or court clerk.
  • Page one needs a 2.5 inch empty band along the top, with half an inch of margin on all remaining sides. Print in black ink, 10 point or bigger, on white paper.
  • Paper size runs from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches, and the first line should say what kind of instrument it is.
  • If a deed refers to a surviving owner, pair it with a certified death certificate unless one is already of record.
  • A court order must be certified and sealed by the clerk, and any Social Security number has to have its first five digits removed.

Another rule asks conveyances to give the marital status of male grantors, citing MCLA 565.221.

Transfer tax on a Bay County sale

Two levies arise at recording, one county (MCL 207.505) and one state (MCL 207.526). Either the deed states the total price on its front, or the filer hands in a Real Estate Transfer Affidavit with that number. Both taxes are due unless an exemption applies, and the instrument itself has to claim it.

The two exemption lists overlap but are not identical. Each excludes consideration below $100, security instruments, leases, court orders that set no price, land contracts whose title has not passed, and foreclosure transfers involving government backed loans. Only the state act goes on to name gifts from a parent or grandparent to a child or grandchild. Ask the title agent or the office which section covers your paper.

Other fees set by state law

The Revised Judicature Act, at MCL 600.2567, governs what a register may charge. The statute also prices the services that sellers and heirs request most often.

  • Copies run $1.00 per page. Certifying a recorded paper adds $5.00.
  • Index searches by grantor and grantee cost 50 cents per year covered, with a $5.00 minimum.
  • Filing a miscellaneous paper costs $1.00.
  • Fees are paid on delivery of the paper, with exceptions for electronic filers and for government filers that have a payment agreement.

A charter county can pass its own schedule by ordinance, so confirm any copy or search fee with Bay County staff before you write a check.

Recording step by step

Work in this order and you save a trip. Settle who must sign and whether a survivor appears on the deed, so the death certificate is on hand. If the deed has a warranty clause, request the tax certificate from the County Treasurer. Have the deed drafted with the full price written in, or complete the transfer affidavit. Have it notarized in Michigan, then hand the original to the title agent or post it with a return envelope.

Once the paper is recorded, you receive a Document Number, which is how the instrument turns up in the online index. File it with your closing papers. Anyone who holds other land in the county should also enroll in Property Watch.

When a paper bounces, the cause usually sits on the sixteen item list: a mismatched name, a narrow margin, an unsealed court order or an exposed Social Security number. Correct that single defect and resubmit instead of redrafting everything. If the deed is already signed, ask the notary whether a corrected acknowledgment is possible before you start over.

Other Bay County offices a deed touches

A sale crosses several counters. The Treasurer, upstairs at 515 Center Ave., writes the tax certificate and collects late tax. Equalization answers parcel and description questions. The assessor in your city or township keeps the value record, while the Register preserves the chain of title.

Bay County sits on Saginaw Bay. The median owned home is worth $152,200, owners occupy 77.0 percent of homes, and median household income is $61,763. New construction is slight: 67 building permits were counted for 2025. A house needing repairs before a mortgage will fund may fit a cash buyer, who can close without a lender's inspection list.

Frequently asked questions

What does a Bay County recording cost?

It is $30.00 per document, with $4.00 of the total sent to the state survey fund. A paper that assigns or discharges multiple instruments adds $3.00 for each additional one.

Are Bay County land records searchable on the web?

Yes. Doxpop offers searching at any hour, and the office suggests its free Property Watch alert so you learn of any attempt to move your title.

Is eRecording available in Bay County?

It is. The office page names the approved partners that deliver title documents electronically to the county.

What does the Bay County tax certificate cost on a warranty deed?

Five dollars, on its own check, payable to the Bay County Treasurer instead of the Register.

What transfer tax rates does Bay County list?

content:
Benzie County, MI Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Michigan
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Benzie County, MI Register of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Benzie County, MI Register of Deeds sale

Selling in Benzie County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Benzie County?

Where to find the Benzie County Register of Deeds

Go to Suite 202 of the Government Center, 448 Court Place, Beulah, MI 49617. The counter is staffed weekdays from half past eight in the morning to five in the afternoon, and the phone number is 231-882-0016.

Every deed, mortgage and easement for land in Benzie's townships and in the city of Frankfort lands in the same index at this one counter.

  • Clerks cannot supply blank forms or weigh in on legal questions. People who need a deed written are told to see an attorney or a title company.
  • A filing can arrive over the counter, by post, via UPS or FedEx, or by electronic submission.
  • If you request copies by mail, enclose your own return envelope with postage.

Recording fees

The charge is $30.00 per filing however many pages it runs. Michigan's MCL 600.2567 sets that same $30 and includes the survey fee inside it. If one paper assigns or discharges multiple instruments, each instrument after the first brings a $3.00 surcharge.

Benzie County recording office charges
ServicePrice
File one document$30.00
Each additional instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
Copy of a recorded real estate record$1.00 a page
Certification of a document$5.00 extra
Tax certificate covering up to five descriptions$5.00 per instrument
Every description beyond five20 cents

Certain papers need a County Treasurer certificate first: warranty deeds, any deed that promises warranty, land contracts and assignments of them, and condominium master deeds. Under MCL 211.135 the proof covers five years of taxes before the instrument date.

Plan the budget in two parts. The recording fee and any $3.00 surcharges go to the Register. The tax certificate goes to the County Treasurer on its own check, and vendor fees for electronic filing are billed by the vendor.

Recording electronically

Four vendors handle electronic submissions: Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm. Each sets its own price, and the Register adds nothing more, so the vendor's charge is the only extra cost to budget for.

If your deed also calls for county tax certification, the office recommends ePN because a document router links the two. A single electronic package can then serve both offices.

Searching is its own service. Names are indexed by seller and buyer, and scans reach back to the mid 1800s. The public Tapestry link charges for use, and title professionals may take a Laredo subscription arranged by phone.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Benzie County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax on a Benzie County deed

The office collects state transfer tax as the deed goes on record, and its website links the county act (MCL 207.505) and the state act (MCL 207.526). The state charge is $3.75 on each $500 of price, a partial block rounding up, or $7.50 per $1,000. Call the office to learn the county amount for your instrument. Lakefront prices run high, so the tax deserves a line in any shoreline seller's net sheet.

Some transfers escape the state tax, and the instrument has to say which exemption it claims.

  • A price below $100, loan security papers, leases and mineral interests.
  • A deed passing from a person to a son, daughter, stepchild or grandchild.
  • A court order that sets no dollar price, a boundary adjustment, or a corrective quitclaim.
  • A land contract in which the seller still holds title, and foreclosure deeds, including deeds given to avoid foreclosure.

Documents the office records

The office records land related paper, and the list is broad. A seller or an heir will meet several of these during a sale or estate settlement.

  • Warranty, quit claim and mineral deeds, as well as administrator, tax and sheriff's deeds.
  • Mortgages, along with assignments and discharges of them.
  • Liens for state and federal tax, circuit court orders, and probate orders.
  • Certificates of trust, master deeds, rights of way, restrictions and subdivision plats.
  • Surveys, land corner records and remonumentation records.

Payoff paperwork matters most with an older loan. A lender files a discharge once a mortgage is satisfied, and the buyer's closer checks this index for it before title is cleared.

Steps before filing a deed

Sequence matters at a small counter. Begin with the title commitment, so you know which liens need a discharge. If the deed has a warranty clause, request the Treasurer's certificate next, or send the deed through ePN so certification travels with it. After that, check that the deed states the complete price, because transfer tax follows the stated price.

Last, choose how it gets there. Carry it in on a weekday, post it with a return envelope, or let the closing agent send it through one of the four vendors. A family transfer should name its exemption right on the instrument, so the tax is not collected in error.

What to bring if you file in person: the signed original deed, a check for the recording fee and transfer tax made out to the Register of Deeds, and a separate check to the County Treasurer if a tax certificate is needed. Ask the clerk to confirm the total before you pay. If the property is an inherited cabin or a family lake house, bring the earlier deed or probate paperwork too, so the index entry can be matched to the right owner.

When the closing is handled by a title company, none of this is your job, but you should still ask which of the four vendors they use and when the recorded deed is expected back. Recording is the point where the sale becomes part of the public record, so a buyer's lender will want proof that it happened.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Benzie County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Other county offices a seller may call

Upstairs in the same building is the Treasurer, at 231-882-0011, on the same weekday schedule. That office administers delinquent tax under Public Act 206 and keeps the tax rolls. Online payments of delinquent tax cost 2.49 percent by card (minimum $1.50) or $1.00 by e-check.

Downstairs, Equalization works from Suite 130 at 231-882-0015. It supplies parcel maps, descriptions, values, sales data, tax maps and millage rates, and it links a parcel search and FEMA map change forms, handy for lakefront owners.

A free Property Fraud Alert service from the Register emails you when any document is recorded under your name, which helps an owner who lives elsewhere catch a forged deed early. The Register also collects the state remonumentation fee as part of each filing, leads the county Plat Board that reviews new subdivisions, and processes U.S. passport applications.

Benzie County housing at a glance

Benzie is small and growing, with 18,568 people in 2025, up 3.3 percent from 2020. The county counts 12,682 housing units against only 7,708 households, and 87.8 percent of occupied homes belong to their occupants. The 2020 to 2024 median home value is $285,700. Median gross rent is $1,026 a month, a useful benchmark if the house you are selling has a tenant. Because units outnumber households so widely, ask the title agent early whether any owner or heir lives out of the area, since that changes where papers are signed and mailed.

Frequently asked questions

What is Benzie County's fee for filing a deed?

Thirty dollars a document, no matter how long it is. A paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds three dollars for each one after the first.

Does the Benzie County Register of Deeds add a surcharge for electronic filing?

No. Only the vendor you pick bills a fee, and the approved list is Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm.

When is a tax certificate required in Benzie County?

Warranty deeds, land contracts and condominium master deeds need one. Up to five descriptions cost $5.00, and each further description is 20 cents.

Will Benzie County staff write my deed for me?

No. Staff do not prepare blank documents or give legal advice, so engage an attorney or a title company.

When can I visit the Benzie County Register of Deeds?

Weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon, in Suite 202 of the Government Center in Beulah. Phone 231-882-0016 first if you have a question.

Where to take a deed in Berrien County

The office occupies the Berrien County Administration Center, 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085. Staff are present on weekdays that are not county holidays, with doors open from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The window for taking in documents is shorter, ending at 4:30 p.m., and the public search computers go dark at 4:45 p.m.

Questions go to 269-983-7111, extension 8562. Paper reaches this one counter from every city, village and township in the county, from Benton Harbor and New Buffalo to Niles and Three Oaks.

  • Deliver the original in person, by courier, or by USPS, UPS or FedEx to 701 Main Street.
  • Slip in a self addressed return envelope, since the recorded paper travels back to whoever you name on it.
  • Photocopies get turned away because the office only records originals with live signatures.
  • Pay the whole amount up front. Checks should name the Register of Deeds, because a check meant for another county department will bounce the whole packet back.

Recording fees

The county charges $30 for any document, however long, the flat Michigan charge per recordable event. Certification and transfer tax can be added when the paper is a deed.

Berrien County Register of Deeds fees
ServiceCharge
Record a single document of any size$30
Extra instrument named in an assignment or discharge$3 each
Tax certification covering up to 25 parcel descriptions$5
Each further parcel description20 cents
Ordinary copy$1 per page
Oversize copy, larger than tabloid paper$3 per page
Certifying a recorded document$5 plus $1 per page
Search of the indexes50 cents per year, $5 minimum

The treasurer's certificate has to accompany a warranty deed, any deed with a warranty covenant, a land contract or its assignment, and a master deed for a condominium.

Transfer tax on a Berrien County sale

Two taxes apply to a non exempt deed of $100 or more. The county levy is 55 cents for each $500 of the price and the state levy is $3.75 for each $500, and a leftover fraction counts as a whole block. Added up, that is $4.30 per block. The county posts a rate chart that turns sale prices into dollar amounts.

State the whole price on the deed or attach a real estate valuation affidavit. Name any exemption on the instrument itself. The purchase contract assigns who pays, so confirm with the title agent.

The two statutes differ on exemptions. MCL 207.526, the state act, excuses a gift of a home to a child or grandchild, court orders with no stated price, and a transfer made through a mortgage foreclosure. MCL 207.505, the county act, shares many exemptions but has no family transfer item, so settle which tax applies before anyone signs.

What a deed needs before staff will accept it

These items show up most with house sales and estates.

  • Bring a certified death certificate, sealed by the clerk, to record that a joint owner has died (MCL 565.48). Recording it does not change the earlier deed, which stays the most current deed of record until someone files a new one.
  • A court paper must show the court's certification and seal.
  • For a notary, try the County Clerk by appointment on the main number, extension 8233, or a bank, municipal office or title company, some of which charge a fee.
  • Employees do not write deeds for the public. Ask a lawyer or title insurer, or find a template online or in an office supply store.
  • Mortgage survey reports do not go on file here. Only a certified survey that was actually recorded appears in the index.

Every recorded paper turns into a public record, and any member of the public may buy a copy for $1 per page. Once a loan is repaid, the lender files a discharge of mortgage at this office, and a buyer's closer checks for it.

A short checklist before you leave home: the original deed with live signatures, an acknowledgment from a notary or court officer, payment in full on a check that names the Register of Deeds, and a self addressed return envelope. If a co-owner has died, bring the certified death certificate. If a court order moved the title, make sure it carries the court's certification and seal. Staff cannot fix a defective deed at the counter, so a rejected packet means another trip or another mailing.

Searching Berrien County records online

The county website has a Land Records Search page for lookups and an e-Recording page for electronic filing. The property and taxes page also links to online Register of Deeds services, the transfer tax chart and a flowchart on splitting or combining parcels.

Ahead of a closing, search by name for the chain of title, open mortgages and recorded liens. Counter searches by staff run 50 cents per year covered. Owners who intend to hold back a piece of their lot should read the split and combine flowchart first, since that process runs through other offices.

An heir preparing to list should pull the earlier deed and any recorded death certificate before the listing goes live, so the title agent can tell exactly who holds the interest.

Which county office handles what

Keep the departments straight when you chase a payoff. The Register of Deeds is an elected office that reviews and records papers moving or burdening land. The County Treasurer is a separate elected office with a four year term, and the Equalization Department prepares the report that sets the equalized tax base for the Board of Commissioners.

Tax payoff questions belong with the treasurer, not the Register. In a normal sale the closing agent requests the payoff, collects the transfer tax and sends the deed for recording, so most sellers only sign. If you sell for cash and as-is, the recording steps are the same, but there is usually no lender appraisal to wait on.

For an estate sale, plan the order. First record the death certificate if a joint owner died, then record the new deed, then let the closing agent clear any mortgage discharge still pending. Each paper becomes a separate recording, and each recording carries its own $30 fee, so ask the title agent for a total before you write the check.

Berrien County housing at a glance

The July 2025 population estimate is 152,444, which is 1.3 percent under the 2020 base. Housing stock totals 78,132 units and 63,999 households, and owner occupancy sits at 72.8 percent. The typical owned home was worth $224,300 over the 2020 to 2024 period. Monthly costs for owners paying a mortgage had a median of $1,462, and gross rent had a median of $942. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 372.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Berrien County recording fee?

Thirty dollars flat per recordable document, regardless of how many pages it has. When a paper assigns or discharges several instruments, each one past the first adds $3.

What are Berrien's transfer tax numbers?

The county tax is 55 cents per $500 and the state tax is $3.75 per $500, with each block rounded up. That adds to $4.30 per block, unless the deed is exempt.

Can I mail a deed to Berrien County?

Yes. Send the signed original to 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085, along with complete payment and a return envelope that carries postage. A photocopy cannot be recorded.

What is the cutoff for recording in Berrien County?

Documents are taken until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, even though the office itself stays open to 5:00 p.m. and the public search computers close at 4:45 p.m.

Does the Berrien County recording office offer a notary?

No. Book a notary at the County Clerk through 269-983-7111, extension 8233, or visit a bank, municipal office or title company. Some of them charge a fee.

Cash Home Buyers in Michigan

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Branch County, MI Register of Deeds sale

Selling in Branch County? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Branch County?
We buy Branch County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Where Branch County records deeds and mortgages

Branch County land records are kept in the Courthouse Annex, 23 East Pearl Street, Coldwater. Weekday counter hours are 7:30 to 4:30, lunch hour included, and the office phone is 517-279-4320.

A document that arrives after the 4:30 close still gets that day's date stamp, and the clerks record it first thing the following morning. E-recording is accepted, which suits lenders and title agents closing a Coldwater, Bronson or Quincy sale from a distance. Frequent researchers can pay monthly for remote access, and occasional ones pay per search.

An owner checking for back taxes before listing can use the treasurer's free delinquent tax search at bsaonline.com. Under Online Services choose Delinquent Tax Search, then enter a surname, a parcel number or a street address.

Recording fees

Each recording costs $30 flat. The county forwards $4 of every fee to the state survey and remonumentation fund, with carve-outs for fixture filings, liens filed by the state or federal government, state deeds, plats and tax reversion documents. The governing fee statute is MCL 600.2567.

  • $30 each for a deed, a mortgage, a lien notice or release, and a UCC fixture filing.
  • $3 for every instrument past the first on a combined assignment or discharge.
  • $1 per page for copies of recorded real estate documents, and $5 to certify a document.
  • Name searches at 50 cents per year searched, never less than $5, and $3 per name for a lien search.
  • $5 to have a document faxed or emailed.

Mailed submissions must include a stamped envelope addressed to you, since that is how the recorded original comes back.

Why a deed gets rejected

Returned paper usually fails one of the formatting tests in MCL 565.201. Check these points first.

  • A typed or printed name beneath each signature, which should be dark ink and must spell the name the way the notary block does.
  • The notary's printed name sitting near the notary signature on the same sheet.
  • Grantee mailing addresses, plus who drafted the paper and where to reach them.
  • An unprinted strip of 2 1/2 inches on top of page one, and 1/2 inch along all remaining edges.
  • A heading line that states the single recordable event, for example warranty deed.
  • Dark print of at least 10 points on white stock weighing 20 pounds, no smaller than letter and no longer than legal.
  • Social Security numbers cut to their last four digits, and a written English translation for foreign-language text.

Once a document meets these tests, the register cannot refuse it over what it says.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Branch County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Tax certificate before recording

That turns on the kind of deed. Warranty deeds, deeds with a warranty covenant, land contracts and land contract memoranda with a warranty clause all go through the Branch County Treasurer first. MCL 211.135 is the source, and the certificate has to show that the parcel carries no tax liens or tax titles and that five years of taxes before the deed date are settled.

The treasurer charges $5 a document for as many as five descriptions and 20 cents for each one beyond five. That money goes on its own check made out to the Treasurer's Office.

A quitclaim with no warranty covenant sits outside the rule, so family transfers and title fixes tend to move quickly. If you owe back taxes, expect a warranty deed to sit until the balance is paid.

Transfer tax on a Branch County sale

A sale draws two levies. The county takes 55 cents for every $500 of value or fraction (MCL 207.504), and the state takes $3.75 on the same unit (MCL 207.525). Added together, that is $4.30 per $500 and $8.60 per $1,000. The deed should state the full value on its face, or an affidavit of value goes with it.

Branch County transfer tax rates
TaxRate per $500 of value or fraction
County$0.55
State$3.75
Combined$4.30

The Register of Deeds collects the tax on any transfer of $100 or more and publishes a rate schedule on its resources page. Who pays is settled in the purchase agreement.

Transfers that escape transfer tax

County and state exemptions overlap without matching exactly. Both let through nominal deals under $100, mortgages and other security papers, leases, court orders that name no price, boundary corrections, title-confirming quitclaims, and land contracts whose legal title has not yet passed.

  • A parent or grandparent deeding to a descendant, including step and adopted relations, is exempt only in the state act, MCL 207.526.
  • Foreclosure is treated differently too. The state exempts any mortgage foreclosure or deed in lieu, while MCL 207.505 reaches only government-made, guaranteed or insured loans.
  • The county list carries no gift-to-child entry, so ask in Coldwater whether the county's 55 cents still hits a family deed.

Towns the Coldwater office serves

The Coldwater office records land for every parcel in the county, wherever it sits. The two cities are Bronson and Coldwater. Quincy, Sherwood and Union City are villages. The sixteen townships are Algansee, Batavia, Bethel, Bronson, Butler, California, Coldwater, Gilead, Girard, Kinderhook, Matteson, Noble, Ovid, Quincy, Sherwood and Union.

Unincorporated places on the county's list include Canada Shores, Crystal Beach, East Gilead, Girard, Hatmaker, Hodunk, Lockwood, Pearl Beach, Ray and Sans Souci Beach. A deed for a lot in any of them goes to the same counter in Coldwater.

Branch County housing at a glance

Coldwater is the seat and biggest city, and farming is still the base of the local economy. The 2025 population estimate is 45,993, with 21,287 housing units and 16,906 households. Owners occupy 77.7% of units, the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $162,500, and gross rent in the middle of the range is $959. Because the recording fee, the tax certificate and the transfer tax all come out at closing, ask your title agent for the totals before you sign.

Typical sequence for a sale: check for back taxes, get the treasurer's certificate if the deed carries a warranty, sign a deed that meets the format rules, and have the title agent record it, electronically if you are out of town. A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can shorten the repair and lender steps, but the recording requirements stay the same.

Frequently asked questions

How much will I pay to put a deed on record in Branch County?

Budget $30 for the recording itself, no matter how many pages the deed has. Add $3 per extra instrument if one document assigns or discharges several, and at least $5 for the treasurer's certificate when the deed carries a warranty.

What are the street address and hours of the Branch County recorder?

Go to the Courthouse Annex at 23 East Pearl Street in Coldwater between 7:30 and 4:30 on a weekday. The number to call is 517-279-4320.

Does Branch County take electronic filings?

It does. Electronic submissions are accepted, and whatever lands after 4:30 in the afternoon is date stamped that day and entered in the books the next morning.

Is a tax certificate needed to record a quitclaim in Branch County?

Usually not. The tax certificate statute, MCL 211.135, carves out a quitclaim or any deed lacking a covenant of warranty. Warranty deeds and land contracts still need the county treasurer's sign-off.

What happens with transfer tax when I deed the house to my son or daughter?

The state tax does not apply, because MCL 207.526(j) and (k) exempt a transfer to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild. The county statute lists no such exemption, so ask the Register of Deeds about the county's 55 cents per $500 before you record.

Where to file a deed in Calhoun County

Calhoun County accepts land documents at one office only: the Marshall County Building, 315 West Green Street, home of the Clerk and Register of Deeds. The second county office, at 161 East Michigan Avenue in Battle Creek, handles circuit court filings and personal protection orders, so a deed taken there goes nowhere. Call the Marshall counter at 269-781-0718 if you are unsure.

The research room, used by title searchers and genealogists, is open on business days and closes at 4:45 p.m., a quarter hour before the office itself. The Marshall building also issues marriage licenses, vital records and notary commissions, so expect a mixed crowd at the counter. A drop box at the west edge of the parking lot behind the County Building takes completed documents with payment enclosed. The county also runs an online land record search and a property alert tool.

Clerks cannot give legal advice about completing a land record form, and the office stocks no blank forms. Questions go to a lawyer. The State Bar of Michigan referral line is 1-800-968-0738, and Michigan Legal Help is another free place to start.

Recording fees

A flat $30 buys the recording of any document, long or short. That covers deeds, mortgages, certified copies, lis pendens, timber, oil and gas leases, UCC filings, Land Division Act filings, discharges and terminations, and federal, state and employment security liens. Land record payments are taken as cash or check, nothing else.

  • Add $3 for each additional liber and page referenced on a discharge or assignment.
  • Pay $5 to the treasurer for the tax certification a warranty deed or land contract requires.
  • Copies cost $1 a page for real estate records, $2 for UCC filings, and at least $2 a page for plats.
  • Certification of a recorded instrument is $5.

The base fee comes from MCL 600.2567: $30 to enter and record a document, with $3 added for each further instrument assigned or discharged.

Can I record a Calhoun County deed electronically?

Yes, with one carve-out. Every document type can be e-recorded except those that require a real estate transfer tax valuation affidavit. Those have to be mailed or brought to the Marshall counter. E-recording runs through a vendor: you scan and upload, the register reviews, and anything with errors comes back for correction before it is stamped and returned by electronic delivery.

Four vendors work with the county: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. Sign up as a customer with one of them; each offers demonstrations and training. When a document needs tax certification, the system routes it to the County Treasurer's Office, so you make no separate trip for the certificate.
