What the Marshall office checks on a deed

The county's posted checklist rests on MCL 565.201 and adds items that catch people who draft their own deeds.

  • Signatures in original ink, each with a typed or printed name below it that agrees with the notary block.
  • Street or post office addresses for grantees, and the drafter's name and address.
  • A Michigan acknowledgment taken by a judge, a court clerk or a notary.
  • For any deed that names a survivor, a certified death certificate that was recorded earlier and is cited by liber and page.
  • Court orders bearing the court clerk's certification and seal.
  • A first line stating one recordable event, black type of 10 points or more on white 20-pound paper, and a 2 1/2 inch blank band above the first line of page one and 1/2 inch on the other edges.
  • The land's total value shown on the deed or in an attached valuation affidavit. The county bars the stock phrase "and other good and valuable consideration."
  • Any transfer tax exemption spelled out on the instrument, and a trust document recorded as a separate paper.

If you are selling, your closing attorney or title company normally handles this list. If you are drafting a deed yourself, run through it line by line before you drive to Marshall.

Treasurer tax certification

The Calhoun County Treasurer signs off. A warranty deed, a land contract, an assignment of a land contract or any deed with a warranty covenant must carry the treasurer's certification before the register accepts it, and the fee is $5. Call 269-781-0807 with questions about deed certification. When you e-record, the system forwards the paper to the treasurer for you.

The rule comes from MCL 211.135: the parcel must be free of tax liens and tax titles, and the five years of taxes before the deed date must be paid. A plain quitclaim without a warranty covenant is outside it.

An owner who has fallen behind will run into the balance at this step. Pay it off before the closing date so the recording stays on schedule. On a cash sale to a buyer who wants to close quickly, this is the one errand that can hold things up, so ask the treasurer about any balance early.

Transfer tax on a Calhoun County sale

Stack the county's 55 cents (MCL 207.504) on the state's $3.75 (MCL 207.525) and you get $4.30 for each $500 of value, with any remainder counted as one more block. A fraction of a block counts as a whole one, so a $162,800 home, the typical owner-occupied value here, becomes 326 blocks instead of 325.6.

$275,000$302.50$2,062.50$2,365.00

Owners selling a troubled property care most about three exemptions. A deed in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure on any mortgage is exempt under the state act, while the county act covers only government-backed loans. A court order that sets no price escapes both taxes. A transfer to a child or grandchild appears on the state list in MCL 207.526. Whatever you claim should be written on the instrument.

Calhoun County housing at a glance

Calhoun County has about 133,408 residents and 59,808 housing units, centered on Battle Creek, the largest city, and Marshall, the county seat. Owners live in 72.7% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is worth $162,800, typical gross rent is $968, and the county's 53,333 households earn a median $63,177. At that typical value a sale triggers roughly $1,400 of transfer tax, and the rates are the same in every Michigan county.

Frequently asked questions

What will I owe the Calhoun County recorder for a deed?

Thirty dollars per document, paid in cash or by check. A discharge or assignment adds $3 per additional liber and page it references, and a warranty deed needs the $5 treasurer tax certification as well.

Will the Battle Creek office record my deed?

No. Land documents are filed only at the Marshall office, 315 West Green Street. Battle Creek handles circuit court filings and personal protection orders.

Is e-recording available for Calhoun County deeds?

Yes, through CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. A document with a transfer tax valuation affidavit is the exception and must be mailed or delivered to Marshall.

What commonly gets a Calhoun County deed returned?

Typical reasons are a missing grantee address, no drafter name, signer names that disagree with the acknowledgment, no stated property value, and margins or type size outside the statute. The office returns rejected paper with the reasons checked off.

Who pays the Calhoun County transfer tax in a sale?

The statutes tax the written instrument and leave payment to the parties, so the purchase agreement governs. A $162,800 sale carries $1,401.80 in combined county and state tax.

Which office handles Cass County land records?

In Cass County one elected official, on a four-year term, fills both the Clerk and Register of Deeds roles. Besides land records, that office serves as clerk to the circuit court, the board of commissioners, the plat board and the jury board, as registrar of vital records, and as the county's chief election officer. The same counter handles marriage licenses, concealed pistol permits, assumed business names and notary commissions.

Find the office at 120 North Broadway, Suite 200, Cassopolis. The phone is 269-445-4464 and the fax is 269-445-4406. Call to confirm counter hours before you drive in with an original deed.

For occasional users, the county runs a basic deed search by name, date range, liber and page, document number or parcel number. The index search costs nothing. Looking at, printing or saving an image runs $1 a page plus a processing fee. Staff searches are done as time permits, so allow extra days. Clerks will pull a single document you identify, but they cannot search real property records or draw up a list of recorded instruments for you.

Recording charges

The price of a recording has been $30 since October 1, 2016, however many pages the document runs. Where one paper assigns or discharges several instruments, each additional instrument costs $3. MCL 600.2567 is the state basis. Keep staples away from checks.

  • A treasurer's tax certification, $5, is required for warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of them, and may be added to the recording check.
  • UCC terminations and fixture filings: $30 each. Financing statements go to the State of Michigan only.
  • Copies: $1 a page, $5 for a plat of record, $5 by fax; certifying a copy is $5.
  • Staff searches: half a dollar for each year covered with a $5 floor, $3 per name for state or federal tax lien certificates, and $6 for a financing statement certificate on one debtor name.

What the Cass County checklist requires of a deed

The county posts twenty requirements. Many echo MCL 565.201, and several are more explicit than the statute itself.

  • The land's complete legal description.
  • A notary block giving the notary's signature, commission expiration date, the county and state of certification, the names of those acknowledging, and where the paper was signed.
  • A notary seal if the notary is out of state.
  • Social Security numbers cut to the last four digits, unless a law or court order calls for more.
  • An affidavit explaining the correction whenever an original is recorded a second time.
  • A recorded death certificate, attached or cited by liber and page, wherever a grantor is described as survivor.
  • The consideration stated on the deed itself. Wording such as "other good and valuable consideration" is accepted only with an affidavit.

Layout follows the statewide rule: a blank 2 1/2 inches above the first line of page one, half an inch on other edges, black print of at least 10 points on white 20-pound paper, and a sheet no smaller than letter or larger than legal.

What a Cass County tax certification covers

MCL 211.135 sets up a two-part certificate. First, the county or state treasurer says whether any tax liens or tax titles are held on the parcel and whether taxes are paid for the five years preceding the instrument's date. Second, the treasurer of the city, village or township where the land lies reports on tax titles and tax sale certificates, and on whether those titles, certificates and sold special assessments were redeemed over the same five years.

Timing can matter. Paper presented from March 1 on, before the local treasurer has filed the year's delinquent return, receives a county treasurer notation that the return could not be checked. That gap is not a reason for the register to turn the deed away.

If a tax certificate or special assessment has been sold against your parcel, redeem it through the village or township and collect written proof ahead of closing, because the statute requires evidence of redemption.

How is transfer tax figured on a Cass County closing?

The same rates apply here as elsewhere in Michigan: 55 cents for the county per MCL 207.504 and $3.75 for the state per MCL 207.525, each applied to every $500 of price or any leftover part of $500, so a price of $218,001 would count as 437 blocks. The typical owner-occupied value in Cass County is $218,000, which divides into 436 blocks.

Cass County transfer tax by sale price
Sale priceCounty (0.55)State (3.75)Combined
$120,000$132.00$900.00$1,032.00

$350,000$385.00$2,625.00$3,010.00

When a deal includes personal property, only the real estate is taxed, as long as the deed or an affidavit states the two values apart.

Transfers exempt from transfer tax

MCL 207.505 and MCL 207.526 share most of their exemptions. The ones most likely to matter in Cass County are below.

  • Land contracts, while legal title waits for the final payment.
  • Quitclaims that only confirm a title the grantee already holds.
  • Boundary-line deeds with no payment attached.
  • A joint tenancy among people when at least one already owned the land.
  • A husband's or wife's deed that creates or dissolves a tenancy by the entireties.
  • On the state list alone: deeds from a parent or grandparent to a descendant, including step and adopted relations, and a dissolving company's transfer to its owners.

An exempt deed still has to meet every format rule, so ask the Clerk/Register how to word the exemption before you sign.

Which Cass County communities record in Cassopolis?

Every parcel in the county records in Cassopolis, whether the house sits in a city, a village or open country. The cities and villages are Dowagiac, Cassopolis, Edwardsburg, Marcellus and Vandalia, and unincorporated places include Adamsville, Calvin Center, Glenwood, Jones, La Grange, Penn, Pokagon, Sumnerville, Union and Wakelee. Library districts give a handy map of the townships: Cass District Library serves Calvin, Howard, Jefferson, LaGrange, Mason, Milton, Newberg, Ontwa, Penn, Pokagon, Porter and Volinia, Dowagiac District Library serves the city of Dowagiac and Wayne Township plus parts of three others, and Marcellus runs its own.

Cass County housing at a glance

Cass County is part of the South Bend-Mishawaka metropolitan area, in the Michiana corner of southwest Michigan. Cassopolis is the county seat and Dowagiac is the largest city.

The county has about 51,677 residents, 26,087 housing units and 21,207 households. Owners occupy 81.6% of homes. The typical owner-occupied value is $218,000, typical gross rent is $916, and half of households earn more than $70,443. Because values run at that level, a typical sale carries a sizable transfer tax bill.

Frequently asked questions

What will a deed cost to record in Cass County?

Thirty dollars per document, whatever its length, plus $3 for each extra instrument on a combined assignment or discharge. A warranty deed also needs the $5 treasurer tax certification, which the county lets you include in the same check as the recording fee.

What is the address of the Cass County Register of Deeds?

The Clerk/Register office is at 120 North Broadway, Suite 200, Cassopolis, MI 49031. Call 269-445-4464, and do not staple your check to the document.

Is searching Cass County deeds free?

The index is free to search by name, date range, liber and page, document number or parcel number. Viewing, printing or saving a document image costs $1 a page plus a processing fee.

What does the transfer tax come to on a $218,000 sale in Cass County?

The total is $1,874.80, made up of $239.80 for the county and $1,635.00 for the state, using 55 cents and $3.75 per $500.

Do I need a treasurer's certificate to record a Cass County quitclaim?

Generally not. The county asks for one on warranty deeds, land contracts and deeds with a covenant of warranty, and MCL 211.135 excludes conveyances without a warranty covenant.

Where to find the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds

The city of Charlevoix is the county seat, while Boyne City is the largest city. Whether you are selling a Lake Charlevoix cottage, a place in East Jordan or a home on Beaver Island, the transfer finishes at this one office. It is a constitutional office created in 1835 that records, indexes and preserves land documents.

What happens to your deed after it arrives

Staff stamp the time on it, give it a liber and page, scan it and add it to the searchable index. That sequence puts the buyer's name on the public record for the property.

Recording does not make a document legal; it makes the document public. Counter staff have no blank deed forms to hand out and cannot draft or coach, because MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from giving legal advice. The deed itself comes from your closing attorney or the title agent, and the register of deeds only checks it against the recording rules.

  • Deeds, mortgages, land contracts and discharges are recorded here.
  • The computer image index reaches back to January 1984, and older records are still being indexed.
  • Documents can be walked in or mailed with the fee and a prepaid return envelope.

For a mailed package, send the signed original deed, one check for the fee and any tax, the treasurer's certificate if the deed needs one, and a prepaid return envelope. Staff cannot record a deed that is missing a required piece, so a complete package saves a second round of mail before your closing.

Recording charges

Filing one document costs $30.00 whatever its length. That amount follows MCL 600.2567, and $4.00 of it is sent to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund.

What transfer tax comes due at a Charlevoix County closing?

Most sales carry two taxes, both counted in $500 slices of the price with any leftover treated as a full slice. MCL 207.504 sets the county rate at 55 cents a slice for counties under 2,000,000 people. MCL 207.525 puts the state rate at $3.75 a slice.

The full value has to appear on the deed itself, or an affidavit stating it travels with the deed. For a sale at $276,800, the typical owner-occupied value here, that is 554 slices.

Some transfers escape the county tax. MCL 207.505 lists instruments with consideration under $100, security instruments such as mortgages, leases, and deeds that only fix a title flaw. Ask the office how your own deed is treated well before the closing date.

Layout rules that can bounce a deed

A deed must satisfy the page rules in MCL 565.201, and the office may not take one that misses them. Formatting causes most returns, so inspect the sheet before it goes in the mail.

  • Margin: 2.5 inches of clear space at the head of page one and half an inch around the rest of every page.
  • Print: 10-point type or bigger, black ink, white paper of 20-pound stock or heavier.
  • Size: letter or legal sheets only, from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • First line: one statement naming the recordable event, such as warranty deed.
  • Only one recordable event per instrument.

The statute also wants a legible printed name under every signature that matches the acknowledgment, and the name and workplace address of whoever drafted anything signed after 1964.

Why do I need a tax certificate before a warranty deed is recorded?

Michigan law makes the office ask for proof that no tax liens attach to the parcel. Under MCL 211.135 the county treasurer certifies that taxes for the five years leading up to the deed date are paid, and Charlevoix charges $5.00 for that certification.

The deeds that trigger this step are warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, and trustee, fiduciary or personal representative deeds with a warranty clause. It reaches master deeds for condominiums as well. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excluded by MCL 211.135(6)(e), so it moves through without the certificate.

Start at the County Treasurer's Office, then bring the certificate with the deed. If you owe back taxes, settle them before the closing date so the certificate can be issued.

Searching records and guarding your title

The county offers three search routes and a free fraud alert. Webtecs is the free portal for taxpayers and occasional users, and images can be bought document by document. Laredo Anywhere is a subscription service for people who run title searches regularly; email rod@charlevoixcounty.org to request an agreement. Tapestry is a web search that needs no subscription.

Homeowners can also enroll in Property Fraud Alert, which sends the owner an alert whenever a filing appears under their name. That helps after a sale too, since a seller can watch for a deed or lien appearing against a property they believed they had cleared.

Charlevoix County housing at a glance

Charlevoix County is one of the pricier corners of northern Michigan. It has about 26,036 residents and 18,026 housing units. Owners live in 83.5% of occupied homes, median rent is $949, and the typical household brings in $76,531.

In the 2020 count, 35.4% of housing units sat vacant, which points to plenty of seasonal and second homes. Water covers 70% of the county's 1,390 square miles, so waterfront parcels and island properties often carry details that the deed and title search have to capture accurately.

Frequently asked questions

What is the filing charge for one deed in Charlevoix County?

One document costs $30.00 whatever its length. A tax certification adds $5.00 when the deed type calls for one, and a mailed document with no prepaid return envelope adds $3.00 for postage. Transfer tax is separate and follows the sale price.

Can the Charlevoix County office prepare my deed for me?

No. Staff cannot draft papers or give legal advice, since MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from it, and the office keeps no blank deed forms. Have an attorney or the title agent prepare the deed first.

Do I need a tax certificate for a quitclaim deed in Charlevoix County?

Usually not. MCL 211.135(6)(e) exempts a quitclaim deed or other conveyance with no covenants of warranty from the certificate rule. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts and certain fiduciary deeds do need the County Treasurer's certification first.

How do I pay the transfer tax on a Charlevoix County sale?

Pay when you hand in the deed. Make transfer tax and tax certification checks out to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds; one check can cover them together with the recording fee. Rates are 55 cents (county) and $3.75 (state) per $500 slice.

Where can I buy a copy of a recorded Charlevoix deed?

Search the free Webtecs portal and buy the image, or ask the office. Plain copies are $1.00 a page and certified copies are $5.00, so request the exact total on a long document.

Which Cheboygan County office takes my deed?

In Cheboygan County the clerk and the register of deeds are the same office, so the same counter handles court filings, marriage licenses and land records.

The Register of Deeds side keeps weekday hours that open at 8:30 in the morning and close at half past four, half an hour after the rest of the clerk's office starts. The county closes on a fixed list of holidays that includes Good Friday, the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve, so a closing planned near those dates needs an earlier recording plan.

What the Register of Deeds does

The office keeps the official real property records for Cheboygan County. Any document that affects real property is recorded there, including warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, wills, mortgages and divorces. After your sale, this is where the chain of title for the house continues.

The county website offers recording packets: a general recording requirements sheet, a warranty deed with recording requirements, a land contract form and a quit claim deed with recording requirements. Pull those sheets before a drafter starts work, because they show the layout the office expects.

  • Payment is accepted by cash, check and debit or credit card.
  • Coins above $5.00 are not accepted.

In a typical sale, the title agent or closing attorney delivers the deed, the fee and any certificate in one package. If you handle the recording yourself, call 231-627-8808 first so you know the exact total and can pay it the day you file.

What to bring when you take a deed to the office

Carry the signed original deed, payment for the fee and transfer tax, and any tax certificate the deed type needs. For a mailed package, add a return envelope and a note with a daytime phone number so staff can reach you about a problem.

  • The original deed with every signature and notary block complete.
  • A stated total value on the deed or an attached affidavit of value.
  • A check, cash or a card for the recording fee and the transfer tax.
  • The treasurer's certification if the deed carries warranty covenants.

Most other local matters, from building permits to zoning, sit with the city, village or township rather than the county recording office, so a question about those goes to the local hall.

Recording fee

State law puts the usual price of entering and recording a document at $30.00, with no extra charge for length. MCL 600.2567 also lists $3.00 for each added instrument on a multi-instrument assignment or discharge, $1.00 a page for copies and $5.00 to certify a recorded document.

A charter county may adopt its own schedule by ordinance, so confirm the total with the Cheboygan office before you write the check. Payment is expected on the day the document is left at the counter, with narrow exceptions for electronic filings and government agencies. A short call to 231-627-8808 gets the exact amount.

State and county transfer tax

Both taxes run on the full sale price, counted in $500 steps with a partial step counted whole. MCL 207.504 sets the county rate at 55 cents a step and MCL 207.525 sets the state rate at $3.75 a step.

Which deeds need a tax certificate?

A deed carrying warranty promises needs county treasurer certification first. MCL 211.135 asks for proof that the parcel's taxes are paid for the five years ahead of the deed date, plus a statement of any tax liens or titles.

Subsection (6)(e) excuses a quitclaim deed that has no warranty covenants, and subsection (6)(c) excuses a sheriff's deed from a court proceeding. If a deed is presented after March 1 and before the local treasurer has filed the current delinquent tax return, the certificate carries a note that the return was not available, and the register of deeds may not refuse the deed for that reason alone.

If taxes are owed on your parcel, pay them before closing. The certificate cannot be issued clean while a lien or unpaid balance sits on the record.

Formatting mistakes that get a deed rejected

Mismatched names, missing addresses and cramped signature blocks cause most trouble. MCL 565.201 sets the rules that every Michigan register of deeds applies.

  • Each signer's name is printed beneath the signature, in black or dark blue ink, and matches the name in the acknowledgment.
  • A notary's name is printed or stamped on the same page near the notary signature.
  • Every grantee's address appears on the deed, using the street number where street numbers are in common use.
  • The person who drafted it is named, with a workplace address.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number are removed or obscured.

A deed written in another language needs an English translation attached. A returned deed goes back to your drafter for repair.

Cheboygan County housing at a glance

Cheboygan County is large, thinly settled and full of seasonal homes. It has about 25,793 residents and 17,631 housing units, and 36.0% of those units sat vacant in the 2020 count. Owners hold 85.6% of homes, the middle rent is $773, and the typical household earns $62,875.

How do I protect my property from deed fraud?

Sign up for Property Activity Alert, a service that watches for recordings under your name. The office cannot stop fraud, but the alert warns an owner early so they can act. Call 231-627-8866 and the staff will enter your name and email address.

This is useful for sellers who keep another parcel in the county, and for anyone who inherited land and has not yet recorded a transfer into their own name.

Frequently asked questions

When can I reach the Cheboygan register of deeds counter?

The Register of Deeds window runs weekdays, opening at 8:30 and closing at half past four. Other clerk services start at 8:00. Closures follow the county holiday list, which includes Good Friday and the day after Thanksgiving.

Can I pay recording fees by card in Cheboygan County?

Yes. Cash, checks and debit or credit cards all work at the office, and most services can be paid by card over the phone. Coin payments above $5.00 are refused.

Is a quitclaim deed taxed differently in Cheboygan County?

A quitclaim deed does not need the treasurer's tax certificate, but transfer tax can still apply if money changes hands. MCL 207.505 exempts deeds that only confirm a title already held, and deeds with consideration under $100.

How is the county transfer tax calculated in Cheboygan County?

Divide the price by $500, round up, and multiply by $0.55. The state tax rounds the same way at $3.75. A $200,000 sale gives 400 steps, so $220 county tax and $1,500 state tax.

Does the Cheboygan office help me write a deed?

No. Hire an attorney or the title agent to draft it. The county posts a general recording requirements sheet and sample warranty and quit claim deed layouts that show what the register of deeds expects.

Where is the Chippewa County Register of Deeds?

The office is at 319 Court Street in Sault Ste. Marie, MI 49783. The phone is 906-635-6312, the fax is 906-635-6855 and the email is rod@chippewacountymi.gov. Call ahead for counter hours, since none are posted online.

Chippewa County is in the eastern Upper Peninsula, and Sault Ste. Marie is the county seat. A seller on Drummond Island, in the Sault, or anywhere along the St. Marys River records the deed here. Mail works as well as a visit, as long as the document, the fee and the return envelope go in together.

Who answers which questions

The county keeps the deed and mortgage records. Police, fire, building and zoning, tax assessment and street maintenance belong to the cities and townships. A seller with a question about an assessed value or a building permit therefore calls the local township or city office, not the register of deeds. The register of deeds answers questions about what has been recorded against the parcel, and it can tell you whether an older mortgage was ever discharged on the record before your buyer's lender asks.

  • Recording, indexing and copies: the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street.
  • Assessment and local zoning: the city or township where the house sits.
  • Tax certificates for warranty-type deeds: the treasurer offices named in MCL 211.135.

Why does a Chippewa County house sale end at the Register of Deeds?

Only a recording here puts the new deed into the county's land record. The office also holds the mortgages, discharges and liens that a title agent hunts for when clearing your title.

The online land records system goes back to May 16, 1865, which gives a title examiner well over a century of names to search. Sellers who inherited a Chippewa County house can use that index to find the deed that put the family on title.

  • Guests search the index free of charge.
  • Members log in with a group, user ID and password, and login charges may apply.
  • PDF copies are bought by credit card after the search.

The order of events at closing is simple. Your title agent or attorney prepares the deed, you sign before a notary, and the closing agent sends the original to Sault Ste. Marie with the fee and any tax certificate. The office records it, indexes it and returns it to the address on the return envelope. If you are mailing it yourself, send everything in one package and keep a copy of what you sent.

Recording and copy charges

Under MCL 600.2567 the recording fee is $30.00 a document unless a charter county has adopted a different schedule. The same section prices copies at a dollar a page and certifying a recorded document at $5.00.

Chippewa County land record charges
ServiceFee
Recording a document$30.00, any page count
Extra instrument on an assignment or discharge$3.00 each
Certifying a recorded document$5.00
Online PDF copy$1.00 per page
Online order fee$5.00 per order

Five dollars of the $30.00 is set aside for the register of deeds' automation fund. Send payment together with the deed, because the office wants it at the time of filing.

Which deeds escape transfer tax?

MCL 207.505 carves out a list of instruments, and a few of them come up often here. A mortgage or other security instrument is carved out. So is a lease, and so is a deed whose stated consideration is under $100.

  • A deed where the grantor is the federal government, the state or a local government.
  • A deed given to settle, or in place of foreclosing, a government-backed or insured loan.
  • A corrective deed that repairs a defect in title the buyer already holds.
  • A boundary-straightening deed when no money changes hands.
  • A transfer between husband and wife that sets up or dissolves an entireties tenancy.

Everything else owes the county 55 cents and the state $3.75 for each $500 slice, with a partial slice counted as a whole one. Phone the office to learn which exemption, if any, fits your deed.

On a cash sale with an unrepresented buyer, agree in writing who pays the transfer tax. The statute taxes the paper, and the purchase agreement decides which side writes the check.

For a taxable sale, work out the tax on paper before closing. The deed has to show the full consideration, or an affidavit with the value goes with it, so the clerk can check your arithmetic.

What else a deed must carry besides the legal description

MCL 565.201 requires details about the people named in the deed, and one missing item stops the recording. Every grantee's address must be printed, using the street number where street numbers are normal and a post office address where they are not.

Any Social Security number must have its first five digits removed or blacked out. A deed in a foreign language needs an English translation stapled on. Anything signed after January 1, 1964 must show who drafted it, with a business address. A notary's printed name belongs on the same page as the notary's signature.

Do I need a tax certificate to record a deed?

For most warranty-type deeds, yes. MCL 211.135 directs the office to demand certification that no taxes are unpaid for the five years preceding the deed, together with a statement of any liens or tax titles on the parcel.

Certificates come from the county treasurer and from the treasurer of the local city, village or township. Quitclaim deeds without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds and state tax deeds are among the exceptions. Skipping the step is a misdemeanor for a register of deeds, with a fine up to $100, so the office holds firm on it.

If you owe back taxes, pay them before the closing date. The certificate cannot show clean until the balance is cleared, and a buyer's lender will want it.

Chippewa County housing at a glance

By land area Chippewa is Michigan's second largest county, and it touches both Lake Huron and Lake Superior. It has about 36,081 residents and 20,556 housing units. Three of every four homes are owner-held (75.0%), and the middle rent is $797. A typical home is valued at $161,900, and a typical household takes in $62,217. In the 2020 count, 31.7% of units stood vacant.

Frequently asked questions

What does it cost to record one deed in Chippewa County?

The state fee under MCL 600.2567 is $30.00 a document whatever the page count. Add transfer tax where it applies and any certification charge the treasurer sets. The office at 906-635-6312 can quote the final total.

Can I search Chippewa County land records for free?

Yes. Guests can search the online index at no charge. A PDF of a document is $1.00 a page plus a $5.00 online fee per order, paid by credit card.

How far back do the Chippewa County records go?

The online indexes begin May 16, 1865. The system's welcome screen shows the index range and upload date, so you can see how current it is before you search.

Is a mortgage subject to transfer tax in Chippewa County?

No. MCL 207.505 exempts instruments given as security, and an assignment or discharge of them. You pay the recording fee, but not the transfer tax, when you record a mortgage.

Who handles a recording problem with a Chippewa County deed?

Reach the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street in Sault Ste. Marie, phone 906-635-6312, email rod@chippewacountymi.gov. A question about what the deed should say belongs with an attorney or the title agent.

Who handles what in a home sale

The county records deeds and mortgages, while cities and townships handle tax assessment, building and zoning, and street maintenance. Ask the township or city office about assessments, and ask the Harrison office about what is on the record.

The office records the deed that moves ownership to your buyer and the mortgage that goes with it. It also holds earlier deeds, land contracts, discharges and liens, so a title search on a Clare County house begins and ends in these books. The clerk is also the county's official abstractor, which helps when a seller needs a title history on an older parcel. If you own an older wooded parcel, ask for the deed history early so closing is not held up.

  • Bring the original signed deed, not a photocopy.
  • Include the fee, a return envelope and any certificate the deed type requires.
  • Keep a copy of the recording stamp for your closing file.

Wooded acreage and lake cottages make up much of the housing stock around Harrison and Farwell, and many owners live elsewhere part of the year. When a deed has several co-owners who sign in different states, each signer's printed name must match the acknowledgment, so gather every signature page before the package goes to the recorder.

What Clare County charges to record a deed

The base charge set by Michigan is $30.00 a document, with page count irrelevant. MCL 600.2567 sends $5.00 of that fee into the register of deeds' automation fund and adds $3.00 for each additional instrument an assignment or discharge covers.

Copies run a dollar a page and a certification is $5.00. A requested records search costs 50 cents per year searched with a $5.00 floor, and filing some other paper is $1.00. Charter counties may use a different schedule, so verify the total with the Clare office by phone.

How transfer tax shows up on a Clare County deed

The deed must print the total value of the real property, or an affidavit of value goes with it. Both the county act (MCL 207.504) and the state act (MCL 207.525) require this.

With the value printed, the arithmetic is short. The county takes 55 cents and the state takes $3.75 on every $500 slice of price, partial slices counted whole. A $133,800 sale, which matches the typical home value in Clare County, spans 268 slices: $147.40 for the county and $1,005 for the state. If real and personal property sell together, naming each value separately confines the tax to the real property. Ask the office how it collects the tax so payment arrives with the deed.

What belongs on page one of a deed

The first printed line must name the recordable event in a single statement, such as warranty deed or quit claim deed. MCL 565.201 bars recording an instrument signed after April 1, 1997 when that statement points to more than one event.

  • Keep 2.5 inches clear at the head of page one.
  • Keep half an inch clear on every other side, on every page.
  • Print in 10-point type or larger, black ink, on white stock of 20-pound weight or more.
  • Attach nothing that falls outside letter or legal dimensions.

Once an instrument is received and recorded, the statute presumes it complies, so a clean first page protects you later.

When does a deed need treasurer certification?

A deed that conveys title with warranty covenants, and a land contract, needs county treasurer certification under MCL 211.135. The certificate says whether tax liens or tax titles exist and confirms payment of the taxes for the five years that precede the deed.

If the register of deeds refuses to receive a deed for lack of certificates, the office notes that fact on the instrument, and the person presenting it must obtain the certificate before trying again. Recording a sale, step by step

A cash sale to a buyer without a lender skips the mortgage recording, so only the deed and its fees are in play. The deed still has to meet every format rule on page one, and the tax certificate still applies if the deed carries warranty covenants. Frequently asked questions

Is the Clare County Register of Deeds a separate office from the clerk?

No. The County Clerk and Register of Deeds offices are combined in Clare County, and both operate from 255 W. Main Street in Harrison.

How do I phone the Clare County office?

Where in Clinton County are deeds filed?

Head for the courthouse at the county seat. The land records for Clinton County are kept by an office that combines the county clerk and the register of deeds, found at 100 E State Street, Suite 2500, with a phone line at 989-224-5270.

The doors are open on weekdays from eight until noon, then again from one until five. Staff ask that you walk in by 4:30 so a transaction is not rushed at closing time, and holiday schedules can shift. Passport services run from the same office by appointment only.

Do not expect the counter to help you write anything. Employees do not prepare or alter documents, do not give legal advice, and keep no blank deeds in stock. For a sale, a title company or attorney writes the deed and sends it over.

What recording a Clinton County deed costs

Thirty dollars flat, whatever the page count. The same figure covers a mortgage or a lis pendens, and the county's recording fees page lists it next to the add-ons below.

Charges the Clinton County office may add to a closing package
Document or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage or other instrument$30 each
Release or assignment naming extra instruments$3 per extra instrument named
Stamp certifying a recorded paper$5
Photocopy$1 a page

If you ask staff to search the index for you, the statutory rate is fifty cents per year covered, never less than $5.

Formatting mistakes that get a deed sent back

The county posts a sixteen-point checklist drawn from Michigan's recording statutes, and the office will look over a draft before you file it. Common reasons for rejection are an incorrect fee, no drafter named, names not typed under the signatures, a male grantor's marital status left out, and an unfinished notary block.

  • Page one needs a blank band 2.5 inches deep along its top, and a half-inch gutter elsewhere.
  • Use black ink, type at 10 points or larger, and white paper of at least 20-pound weight cut to letter or legal dimensions.
  • Open the first printed line with a statement naming the single event the paper records, such as a warranty deed. A paper that combines two events is refused.
  • List every party's street address, and put the drafter's name and address on the instrument.
  • Truncate any Social Security number to its final four digits.
  • Lift the legal description from the previous deed or a fresh survey instead of the abbreviated wording on an assessment notice.

A survivor deed must come with a certified death certificate, unless the certificate is already recorded and the deed cites its liber and page. A court order has to arrive as a certified copy bearing the court clerk's seal.

Who owes transfer tax on a Clinton County sale, and how much?

The seller does, in two layers. State layer: $3.75. County layer: 55 cents. Each is charged on every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts as a whole one (MCL 207.504 and 207.523). Typically the title company deducts the tax from the seller's proceeds. Fifteen days after the deed is delivered is the statutory deadline, and the county treasurer is the collector.

  • Outside both taxes: any deed carrying less than $100 of value, and deeds that only fix a defect in title.
  • Outside the state tax only: foreclosure transfers and deeds in lieu, plus conveyances down a family line to a child or grandchild (MCL 207.526).
  • The county statute lists no family exemption of its own, so ask the register how the county layer is treated on a family transfer.

Print any exemption claim on the deed itself. If none appears, the clerk charges the tax at the window.

When a deed needs the treasurer's certificate

Any time the instrument is a warranty deed, a land contract, or a land contract assignment with a warranty clause. Under MCL 211.135 the register may not record those papers until the county treasurer has certified the parcel's tax status.

It looks back five years from the date on the instrument and flags tax liens or tax titles. A quitclaim without warranty covenants skips the step. For a seller who is behind on taxes, request a payoff letter from the Clinton County Treasurer early, so the balance can be paid at closing and the certificate comes back without a lien. Your title company can usually arrange the payoff from the seller's proceeds.

Clinton County housing at a glance

This is Lansing's northern commuter belt, with the cities of St. Johns and DeWitt and parts of Ovid, Lansing, East Lansing and Grand Ledge inside its lines. The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $259,500, with $88,210 as the typical household income. Owners live in 82.2% of occupied homes, and renters pay $1,092 at the median.

The county has about 80,432 residents. Many stay put: 89.7% lived at the same address a year earlier, so a house for sale often draws buyers from outside the neighborhood rather than from next door. A house on a rural parcel may involve a private well and septic system, a legal description that spans acreage, and a survey, while a city lot usually comes with a short platted description. Either way, the register of deeds only needs the recorded instrument to meet the format list above.

What happens at closing when a Clinton County owner sells for cash?

The paperwork matches a financed sale. The closing agent submits the signed deed to the register with the $30 fee, adds a treasurer's certificate if the deed warrants title, and attaches either the transfer tax or the exemption wording.

Before you sign, ask who is ordering the certificate, whether the deed recites the full price or relies on a valuation affidavit, and what exemption, if any, is claimed. If you mail originals yourself, enclose a stamped return envelope so the recorded deed comes back to you.

One more errand sits outside the register's counter. Within 45 days, the buyer sends the assessor a Property Transfer Affidavit. A seller who claimed the principal residence exemption files to end it effective on the closing date.

A short checklist helps. Confirm the fee, confirm whether the treasurer's certificate is needed, check the exemption wording if the deed qualifies for one, and make sure every signer's printed name matches the notary block. If the office is closed for lunch or a holiday when your closing agent plans to file, move the filing to another day rather than rushing the package. A rushed filing is how a missing signature or wrong fee slips through and sends the deed back.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Clinton County filing fee for a deed?

Thirty dollars, charged per document. Expect an extra $5 for the treasurer's certificate on a warranty deed, which covers up to 25 legal descriptions.

Who is liable for transfer tax when a house in St. Johns or DeWitt sells?

The seller. The statutes name the grantor as the liable party, and the title company usually withholds the tax from what the seller receives.

Will courthouse staff prepare my deed?

No. They review drafts against the recording rules but leave the writing to an attorney, a lender or a title company.

Can I drop off a deed over the lunch hour?

Not in person. The office shuts from noon to one on weekdays. Phone 989-224-5270 to check holiday schedules.

Why did the register send my deed back?

The usual culprits are a wrong fee, a missing drafter name, signatures with no typed names beneath, a half-finished notary block, thin margins, or two recordable events on one paper.

Certifying a recorded copy$5.00
Paper copies$1.00 a page
Tapestry online search$8.95 each name or legal description

Pay the $5 certification in the same payment as the recording fee. No second check goes to the treasurer.

How is transfer tax calculated for a Crawford County sale?

Count how many $500 slices the price holds, treating any leftover as a full slice. Each slice carries $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county. The county rate rests on MCL 207.504, which applies to counties under 2,000,000 people.

  • The seller pays, and the stamps have to be bought here in Crawford County.
  • Land that straddles a county line needs the price allocated between the counties, with each one taxed on its share.
  • The deed has to show the full price. Otherwise attach a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit, which is free to file.
  • Spell out any exemption on the deed itself. Examples include value under $100, foreclosure transfers, and quitclaims that merely repair a title defect.

Michigan's state act, MCL 207.526, also exempts gifts to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild. The county act's list holds no such item, so ask Grayling how the county portion is handled.

When the Crawford County Treasurer has to certify a deed

The certificate is required for warranty deeds, for any other deed with a warranty covenant, for land contracts, and for assignments of land contracts that use warranty wording. MCL 211.135 tells the register to hold such papers until the certificate arrives.

The treasurer works from 200 W. Michigan Ave, keeps the same weekday hours, and can be reached at (989) 344-3231. The certificate lists any liens and tax titles and confirms that the last five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim with no warranty covenants does not need one.

Delinquent taxes can be paid online, by text-to-pay, with digital wallets, by ACH or on autopay, all with fees. Get a payoff figure before you settle on a closing date.

How a Crawford County home sale reaches the register

Begin with the deed itself. A closing attorney or title company drafts it, and you sign in front of a notary. If it carries warranty wording, the Crawford County Treasurer certifies the taxes next. Ask for a payoff figure early so any delinquent balance is cleared from your proceeds rather than found at the last minute.

Then comes payment. The closing agent buys the transfer tax stamps in Crawford County and writes one check for the recording fee and the $5 certification. The package goes to Grayling in person, by mail with a prepaid return envelope, or through Simplifile.

After recording, the deed gets a liber number and an image goes into the files. Expect the recorded original back in the mail, and file it with your closing papers. If you sold for cash to a buyer with no lender, the steps are the same minus the mortgage paperwork, which is why these sales can close quickly when the taxes are already paid.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Crawford County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Crawford County housing at a glance

Land ownership shapes this market. Of roughly 360,000 acres, over three quarters belong to the State of Michigan, the U.S. Forest Service or the Department of Military Affairs. The county has six townships and one city, Grayling, which is its only incorporated community.

About 13,722 people live here, and only 23.3 live on each square mile. Owners occupy 79.6% of occupied homes, rent is $862 at the median, the median household income is $60,392, and builders took out 27 permits in 2025. Rural and wooded parcels are common, so be ready to describe water, septic and internet service at the property when a buyer asks.

Guarding against deed fraud

The register runs a free alert service. Enroll and you get an email or phone message whenever a filing appears under your name, so a forged deed against your property would not sit unnoticed.

The office's files reach back to 1879. It keeps an image of each document rather than the original deed, which is stamped with a liber number after recording. Visitors can search on public computers at the counter, and Tapestry (occasional users) and Laredo (subscribers) offer remote search.

Counter staff will not draft anything or answer legal questions. They refer owners to a real property attorney, a title company, or a blank deed from an office supply store, and caution that forms found online may fall short of Michigan's format rules.

Pre-closing checklist

Before the deed goes to Grayling, work through these questions with whoever is handling your closing.

  • Does the deed warrant title? If so, order the treasurer's certification.
  • Who buys the transfer tax stamps, and for what amount?
  • Was the legal description copied from the previous deed, and is the drafter named with an address?
  • Are delinquent taxes outstanding, and will proceeds clear them?
  • Is the transfer paperwork headed to the local assessor, along with a rescission of any principal residence exemption effective on closing day?

Rural parcels raise extra questions about wells, septic systems and private roads. Take those to the county's health and road authorities. The register only handles the recorded paper, so it cannot answer them. Settling them before you list avoids surprises when a buyer's inspector arrives.

Frequently asked questions

What does it cost to file a Crawford County deed?

Thirty dollars flat. A warranty deed also needs the treasurer's $5 certification, and a release that names several instruments adds $3 for each additional one.

What transfer tax rates apply in Crawford County?

The seller pays $3.75 to the state and 55 cents to the county for each $500 slice of price, with stamps bought in Crawford County itself.

Does the Grayling register close for lunch?

Yes, daily from 12:00 to 1:00. Otherwise the counter serves walk-ins on weekdays until 4:30, no appointment needed.

Can a deed be e-recorded in Crawford County?

Yes, through CSC, Indecomm or Simplifile. Simplifile is the one the county names for papers needing tax certification.

Is a tax certificate needed for a quitclaim?

Not when the quitclaim has no warranty covenants. Warranty deeds and land contracts do need it under MCL 211.135.

Where in Delta County are deeds recorded?

Every deed in the county is recorded in Escanaba. The Register of Deeds works from the county building at 310 Ludington Street, open from eight to four, and the county line is (906) 789-5100, with a fax at (906) 789-5179.

That holds whether the house stands in Escanaba, in Gladstone, in the village of Garden, or out in a township near Rapid River or Rock. Call ahead about anything unusual. Bring the original signed deed and the fee, and ask whether the counter takes cards.

Delta County recording fees

The office follows the statewide schedule in MCL 600.2567, which applies unless a charter county sets its own. Under it a deed is $30 to record whatever the page count.

Recording fees for an Escanaba closing
ServiceFee
Recording one document$30.00
Each additional instrument in an assignment or discharge$3.00
Photocopies$1.00 a page
Certifying a recorded paper$5.00
Records search on request$0.50 for each year, minimum $5
Filing another paper$1.00

Payment is due when you hand the paper to the clerk. An electronic filing that is also paid electronically can settle within one business day under the statute. Ask the office whether it accepts e-recording and through which vendors. Bring along a list of everything being recorded so the clerk can quote one total.

What transfer tax comes out of a Delta County seller's proceeds?

Expect a deduction at closing. Delta County sellers owe a state tax of $3.75 plus a county tax of $0.55, and both are counted per $500 of price. Round any remainder up to a whole $500. The county rate is in MCL 207.504. Liability sits with the seller under MCL 207.523. Checks go to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed reaches the buyer.

Several kinds of transfer owe no state tax:

  • anything under $100;
  • security instruments;
  • land contracts that hold back title until paid;
  • conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.

MCL 207.505 gives the county a shorter list of exemptions. Deeding a house to your daughter, say, can skip the state portion yet still draw the county portion. Check with the register about your own deed before signing.

Print the sale value on the deed, or attach an affidavit stating it. Did tax get paid on a sale that turned out to be exempt? The seller, or a buyer who paid for the seller, may apply to the Department of Treasury for a refund.

Which deeds need a treasurer's certificate?

Most sale deeds do. Under MCL 211.135 the register must hold a deed, plat or land contract until the treasurer certifies tax liens and tax titles and confirms that five years of taxes are paid.

Excused from certification: quitclaims and other conveyances without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds, and some state tax deeds. The same treasurer holds county funds, collects delinquent property taxes and runs the yearly tax sale for the State Treasury.

Before you pick a closing date, ask the treasurer what the certificate costs and how fast it is issued.

Equalization office reports

The Delta County Equalization office serves title agents and appraisers. Its price list shows a $5 Equalization Report, a $15 Apportionment Report listing millage rates, and $15 for taxable value broken out by school district or township. Database copies run $1 a page and simple maps $2.

A single house is different. For its assessed and taxable value, contact the assessor in the city or township where it sits. A buyer estimating the first tax bill will want those two numbers and the millage rate. If you are a seller, having them ready when you list answers the first question an interested buyer is likely to ask about carrying costs.

Recording a Delta County sale, start to finish

Five steps carry a sale through. An attorney or title company drafts the deed and every seller signs, printing a name beneath the signature. A notary, judge or court clerk then acknowledges those signatures. If the deed warrants title, the treasurer's certificate comes next. The closing agent calculates the transfer tax on the full price and sets aside the recording fee. Last, the package reaches 310 Ludington Street in Escanaba, and the register records it.

What arrives at the counter should be the signed original, never a photocopy, plus the fee and any certificate. A buyer paying cash has no lender, so no mortgage gets recorded and the deed with its fees is the entire package. That keeps the visit brief.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Delta County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Unpaid property tax is what most often holds up a deed. No certificate issues while a lien or balance is outstanding, and a warranty deed sits at the register until one arrives. Ask for a written payoff figure before you fix a closing date, and let the closing agent pay it from what you receive at the sale. The certificate then comes back clean, with no second trip to the office.

Raise the tax question with your closing agent the day you accept an offer. A cash buyer will want these loose ends tied up well before closing, and a clear certificate is one less thing to negotiate.

Delta County housing at a glance

A typical owner-occupied house here is valued at $157,100. Median rent is $692 and median household income is $57,809. Owners live in 82.0% of occupied homes. The county has about 36,582 residents spread over 1,171 square miles of land, so parcels range from city lots in Escanaba and Gladstone to farms and forest acreage. Prices and what a buyer expects will differ across that range, and the recording steps above stay the same for all of it.

For a seller the practical upshot is variety. A lakeside cottage near Escanaba, a house in Gladstone and forty acres near Garden call for different disclosures, surveys and legal descriptions, but all three travel to the same counter on Ludington Street for recording.

What formatting does a Delta County deed need?

One recording format applies across Michigan under MCL 565.201, and the Escanaba office enforces these items.

  • Signatures in ink, each followed by a printed name, with the same spelling used in the deed body and the notary block.
  • A street address for every party, and the drafter's name with a way to reach them.
  • For a deed signed in Michigan, an acknowledgment taken by a notary, judge or court clerk.
  • 2.5 inches left blank at the top of page one for the recorder's stamp.
  • A Social Security number, if shown, cut down to its last four digits.

Clerks do not draft deeds or offer legal advice. Inherited a house? Your title company can tell you whether a death certificate or court order must be recorded first, and finding out early keeps an estate sale moving.

Frequently asked questions

How much does the Delta County register charge to record a deed?

Thirty dollars a document, per MCL 600.2567. A release naming several instruments adds $3 for each extra, and certifying a recorded paper costs $5.

Who pays transfer tax on a Delta County house sale?

The seller does. The state rate is $3.75 and the county rate 55 cents for every $500 slice, payable to the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery.

Do deeds for Gladstone and Garden homes go to Escanaba?

Yes. The register at 310 Ludington Street records for the entire county, including both cities and the village.

Is a quitclaim deed exempt from the treasurer's certificate in Delta County?

Yes, when it has no warranty covenants. A warranty deed or land contract must carry the certificate before the register will accept it.

What are the register's hours in Escanaba?

Eight to four. Telephone (906) 789-5100 to confirm holiday closures.

What the Eaton County Register of Deeds does

Eaton County's register keeps the county's land title file: deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and any other paper that touches real estate between Charlotte, Grand Ledge, Eaton Rapids and the townships around them. Each filing is checked against Michigan's recording rules and then stored as a digital image.

Counter staff won't draft a deed, and they can't advise you on what a deed should say. Whoever prepared the paper answers for what it says and why, and legal advice has to come from a lawyer. Need a deed written? Hire a title company or real estate attorney, then bring the signed original here.

Weekday counter hours run 8:30 to 4:30, minus a lunch break from noon to 1:00. Courthouse holidays interrupt that schedule, so check the register's page before a holiday week. Anything sent by mail should include a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, since the office won't return documents without one.

Recording fees

Most recordings cost a flat $30 apiece, whether the paper is a deed, a mortgage, a lis pendens or a certified real estate copy. The extras are itemized on the county's fees page.

Eaton County register charges
ServiceCharge
Filing one deed, mortgage or similar paper$30
Each further instrument that one paper assigns or discharges$3 each
Tax certificate, first 25 legal descriptions$5
Each description past that$0.20
Ordinary copy of a land record$1 a page
Copy of a recorded plat$2 a page
Certified copy of a recorded document$1 a page plus $5 for the seal

The website does not sell certified copies. Ask at the counter or write to the office.

When does a deed need the treasurer's certificate?

Before the register will accept a warranty deed, land contract or land contract assignment, the county treasurer has to certify the parcel. MCL 211.135 sets the test: no tax lien or tax title on the land, and the prior five years of taxes paid.

Exempt from the requirement: quitclaim deeds and similar conveyances lacking warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds, and state tax deeds. The closer normally orders the certificate while escrow is open, so most sellers never request it directly.

What a complete package holds:

  • The treasurer's certificate stapled to a warranty deed or land contract.
  • The full price printed on the deed, or a value affidavit attached.
  • An addressed envelope with postage when the package travels by mail.
  • The $30 filing charge plus $5 for the certificate where one is required.

Filing by mail without a closer? Work through it in this order:

  1. Get the treasurer certificate first if the deed carries warranty language.
  2. Check that the price or value affidavit is on the deed.
  3. Add a check for the $30 charge, plus $5 for the certificate.
  4. Enclose a stamped envelope addressed to yourself.
  5. Send it to the register in Charlotte and watch for the recorded copy.

A package with a missing piece is returned, and the closing can slip a few days. Unpaid taxes on the parcel block a clean certificate until the balance is paid.

Michigan transfer tax for sellers

Selling a house here brings two transfer charges. The state's share is $3.75 for each $500 of the price (MCL 207.525), and the county's is 55 cents for each $500 (MCL 207.504, the rate for smaller counties). A partial $500 still counts in full.

Both are the grantor's to pay (MCL 207.502 and 207.523), and the treasurer needs the state part within 15 days after delivery of the deed. A contract clause may hand the bill to the buyer, yet by statute the seller carries it.

Seller proceeds shrink by both amounts, so build them into your net estimate. Have the closer print both amounts on the settlement statement ahead of time.

Transfers that owe nothing

Plenty of deeds owe no transfer tax, provided the document itself names the exemption it relies on. The county exemptions sit in MCL 207.505 and the state ones in MCL 207.526. The two lists agree except for the last family item below.

  • A price under $100.
  • Mortgages and other security instruments, plus their assignments and discharges.
  • Leases and leasehold transfers.
  • Court orders passing title with no price stated.
  • Quitclaim deeds that cure a defect in title the grantee already owns.
  • Land contracts, until legal title changes hands.
  • State tax only: a gift deed running from parent to child or stepchild, or grandparent to grandchild.

Tax paid on a deal that qualified can be recovered under MCL 207.523(4). The seller, or a buyer who paid in the seller's place, applies to the state Department of Treasury.

Searching Eaton County land records online

Before you list, pull your own deed from the online index and read the legal description, so you know the instrument that will be recorded matches what you plan to convey. The search link on the register's page reaches every record from 1836 up to the most recent proof date, which lets you follow the full chain of title without leaving home. A link for electronic filing sits beside it.

With electronic filing, a title company can send the signed deed in on the same day and skip the courier. Ask your closer whether the file goes in that way and when the recorded copy will reach you. Taxes owed on a parcel are a different search, run through the county treasurer.

Eaton County housing and where the courthouse is

The county counts 109,581 residents as of July 2025 and 48,090 housing units. Owners live in 74.2% of homes. The median owner-occupied value is $216,900, while the median renter pays $1,092 a month. Charlotte holds the courthouse, and the register's counter is there. Other cities include Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet and Potterville, and part of Lansing lies within the county.

What happens when Eaton County taxes go unpaid?

Delinquent bills are the county treasurer's job, and the same office is the foreclosing unit for parcels that stay behind. Its page says over 2,000 foreclosures have been prevented since 2016 and links a chart of Michigan's foreclosure deadlines.

Pay online after looking up the parcel number and amount in the county's tax search. A 2.49% fee applies to cards, and parcels inside Lansing use their own link. A county land bank deals with vacant and foreclosed property.

You can still sell with a balance due. The closer pays it from your proceeds, guided by what the treasurer's certificate says must clear. Get a payoff figure from the treasurer before listing and confirm it again near closing. Cash buyers skip lender appraisal and underwriting, though a warranty deed still needs the certificate before recording.

Frequently asked questions

Where is a deed filed in Eaton County?

Go to the Register of Deeds in Charlotte, the county seat. Find the counter location on the register's page at eatoncounty.org. It is open weekdays 8:30 to 4:30, closed for lunch at noon.

How much does Eaton County charge for a filing?

Each document is $30. When one assignment or discharge covers several instruments, add $3 for each extra one. A tax certificate costs $5 for up to 25 descriptions.

Can an Eaton County deed be filed online?

Yes, through the e-record link on the register's page. Paper filings by mail need a stamped envelope addressed back to the sender.

Who pays the transfer tax on an Eaton County sale?

The seller, under state law. The purchase agreement can pass the cost to the buyer. The state share is due within 15 days after delivery.

How old are the records online?

They go back to 1836 and run through the latest proof date. For certified copies, contact the register's office directly.

Where Emmet County deeds are recorded

Emmet County's Register of Deeds works from 200 Division Street, Suite 150, in Petoskey, MI 49770, and answers at 231-348-1761. Every deed for land in the county, from Harbor Springs to Pellston, ends up in this one office.

It handles more than 240 kinds of paper, including deeds, mortgages with their assignments and discharges, land contracts, leases, liens, probate orders, condominium documents and plats. The register also chairs the county plat board, which reviews new subdivisions.

Land records start in 1852. Images exist from that year forward, yet the name index only runs from 1922 on, with earlier years being added a little at a time. For older searches the county invites people in to use the index books at the counter.

Recording fees at the Petoskey counter

Recording starts at $30 per document, collected at the counter by cash or check only.

Emmet County register fee schedule
ServiceFee
Entering and recording any document$30
Warranty deeds, land contracts, covenant deeds and similar$35
Document assigning or discharging more than one instrument$3 per instrument
Certification of a document$5
Tax certification, up to 5 descriptions$5
Each added description20 cents
Copies$1.00 a page in the office, $1.05 online

The $35 line applies to any deed carrying a warrant or covenant clause, and the $5 tax certification has to be added to that payment. By mail, write the check to the Emmet County Register of Deeds.

Why filings get returned

Every filing is measured against Michigan's recording statutes, and anything short is mailed back. These entries cause the most returns.

  • Signatures have to be originals with typed names under them, and the notary block must repeat those names exactly.
  • Keep a clear band of 2.5 inches across the top of page one and half an inch along every other edge.
  • Type in black ink, 10-point or bigger, on white stock of at least 20 pounds, cut anywhere from letter size to 8.5 by 14.
  • Put the name and address of whoever drafted the paper on anything signed in Michigan.
  • Show nothing beyond the final four digits of a Social Security number.
  • One instrument may cover only one recordable event.
  • Court orders come certified with the clerk's seal. A survivorship deed needs a certified death certificate recorded already.

Pack a return envelope with the filing. A paper is usually recorded the day it arrives, held for a day and mailed back the next business day, unless the title company or lender asked for something else.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Emmet County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How Emmet County transfer tax works

Michigan layers two taxes on the price. The state takes $3.75 for every $500 or part of $500 (MCL 207.525), and a county with under two million residents takes 55 cents on the same measure (MCL 207.504). The deed has to show the whole price, or carry an attached affidavit of value.

The register's downloads include a transfer tax table, a list of exemptions and a state refund application. Under MCL 207.502 and 207.523 the seller carries the bill.

Gifts running from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild escape the state tax under MCL 207.526, so long as the instrument states it. Ask the closer to show both taxes on the settlement statement so you can see what comes out of your proceeds.

Why the recording order matters

Michigan uses a race-notice system. A recorded deed warns every later buyer, and papers rank in the order they were first handed in. First in time, first in line.

After closing, the deed and the buyer's mortgage should go straight to the register, since a delay lets a later filing cut ahead. Title companies know this and typically file the same day. In a private sale you would carry the deed in yourself or use an e-recording provider the county names: CSC, EPN or Simplifile.

The county page carries a ROD Alert about outside companies that offer certified copies of a deed for $50 or more. Copies cost as little as $1 a page at the register, and the office asks residents to call 231-348-1761 before paying a third party.

Searching Emmet County records for free

The online index is the quickest way to check your own chain of title before a sale. Searching works after a free registration. You can search by liber and page, by name or by document type, and a low-resolution preview shows before you pay $1.05 a page by card for a copy. The county also runs Fraud Notify, which sends an email each time a paper is recorded in your name.

Tax details sit in a separate property search on the county website that accepts a name, an address or a parcel number. Anyone buying or inheriting a house here should run both searches. If something on the record looks wrong, such as a mortgage that was paid off but never discharged, raise it with your title company early, since a clean record is what lets a closing go on schedule.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Emmet County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Emmet County at a glance

Emmet County sits at the tip of the Lower Peninsula, with Lake Michigan to the west and the Straits of Mackinac to the north. Petoskey holds the county seat and is the biggest city. Harbor Springs is the second city, and the villages are Alanson, Pellston and part of Mackinaw City.

It has 33,775 people sharing 22,395 housing units as of July 2025, and 15,190 households. Owners occupy 77.0% of the homes, and the median household income is $78,112. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $315,700.

The Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians hold at least 13 scattered reservation areas in the county, among them parts of Petoskey and several townships. A buyer or seller with a parcel near one should ask the title company how that land is treated.

Selling with back taxes

Overdue taxes go through the county treasurer's office, which also issues the tax certification a deed needs before it can be recorded. The register will take redemption payments while the redemption period runs. After it ends, only the foreclosing unit can help.

A sale can wipe out the debt. The closer pays it from the proceeds and then orders the certification, so ask the treasurer for an exact payoff before you choose a closing day.

A short list of steps keeps the closing on track:

  1. Ask the treasurer for the exact payoff and whether the redemption period is still running.
  2. Give the figure to your closer so the certification can be ordered.
  3. Confirm the recording fee, with the extra $5 certification added for a warranty deed.
  4. Have the title company file the deed the same day, since the earliest filing ranks first.

A cash sale skips lender underwriting, but the treasurer's certification and the recording rules above still apply to the deed.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Emmet County register's office?

200 Division Street, Suite 150, Petoskey, MI 49770, phone 231-348-1761. Recording fees are paid in person by cash or check only.

What does a warranty deed cost to record in Emmet County?

$35. The county lists $30 as the base fee and puts warranty deeds, land contracts and other covenant-language deeds at $35, with the $5 tax certification folded into the payment.

Does Emmet County accept electronic recording?

Yes, through three providers: CSC, EPN and Simplifile. Contact one of them for guidance on sending a deed in electronically.

How old are Emmet County land records?

They start in 1852. Images are indexed from 1922 forward and earlier indexing continues, so some older searches mean a trip to the index books.

Do Michigan deeds still need witnesses?

No. Witnesses are no longer required, though most documents still need a notary acknowledgment.

Where Genesee County deeds are kept

The County Clerk and Register of Deeds keeps them, in the Genesee County Administration Building at 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, with holiday closings.

One elected office oversees vital records, elections and the register of deeds. The register's collection covers deeds, mortgages, liens and other papers touching Genesee land. Recording a paper makes it public. It does not make it legal. Staff index each filing into a searchable database and preserve it, so a flawed deed stays flawed after it is on file.

Recording fees in Genesee County

The statewide default under MCL 600.2567 is a flat $30 per recorded document, whatever its length. Charter counties can pass their own schedule, so get the current sheet from the office before you mail payment.

Recording and copy charges under the state schedule
ServiceCharge
Record one document$30
Extra instruments covered by one discharge or assignment$3 apiece
Photocopies$1 per page
Certification of a recorded paper$5
Index search by request$0.50 per year, $5 floor
Other filings$1

The $30 already includes the state remonumentation share, and $5 of each recording goes to the register's automation fund.

When you mail a deed, enclose a check for the recording fee, any extra instrument charges and any certification you want. Add a note with a phone number so staff can reach you if a paper is incomplete. A document that omits its value, or the affidavit that stands in for it, is the most common reason a closing has to wait.

Fees are due at drop-off. If the register takes electronic filings and you pay electronically, the statute gives one business day after receipt. Ask whether Genesee takes e-filing before you plan a closing around it.

Transfer tax when a deed is recorded

A sale deed brings two levies, and the seller owes both. Michigan's rate is $3.75 per $500 of price, rounded up by $500 block, and the county adds 55 cents on each block because its population is under two million.

The deed must carry the total value in its text, or a value affidavit goes with it. When land and personal property sell together with separate stated values, only the land is taxed. Remit to the county treasurer within 15 days of handing over the deed.

  • Tiny deals: instruments under $100.
  • Loan paper: mortgages and other collateral documents, with their assignments and discharges.
  • Gifts to descendants: deeds from a parent to a child or grandchild avoid the state levy.
  • Lender foreclosure: transfers made through foreclosure or in place of it, though a resale afterward is taxed.
  • Land contracts: exempt until legal title passes.

A seller who overpaid on an exempt transfer may request a refund from the Department of Treasury.
