Papers a house sale puts on record

A typical sale records a deed and, where a mortgage existed, a discharge. Each is filed separately with its own fee.

  • Deed: warranty, quitclaim or personal representative form.
  • Mortgage discharge or assignment: $30, plus $3 for every extra instrument it covers.
  • Tax foreclosure papers: forfeiture and redemption certificates, notices of judgment and auction deeds. Their fees may be settled within 30 days after the sale or transfer.
  • Transfer affidavit: kept with the local assessor, which in Flint is the city Assessments Division, so it never reaches the register.

Ask the office what it accepts for each paper, including whether it takes the paper electronically.

What a tax foreclosure judgment does to recorded title

For an owner who lost a house to tax foreclosure, or a buyer thinking about a former tax parcel, the recorded judgment is the paper that matters. It clears most of what is on the books. When the judgment takes effect on March 31, title vests in the foreclosing unit, which in Genesee is the county treasurer, and liens and interests on the parcel are extinguished. Some things survive: future installments of special assessments, environmental liens filed by government agencies, severed or leased oil and gas interests, visible or recorded easements and private deed restrictions.

The paper trail lands at the register's desk. A notice of judgment goes on record, and later so does the deed from an auction. Redemption stays open through March 31. After that date the former owner has no claim, and the buyer at the county auction relies on the recorded deed.

Old land descriptions and your title

If a deed in your chain uses an older description, or cites a township that was later renamed or split, tell the title company early so any correction deed can be recorded before the sale closes. Genesee County's land history goes back to the 1830s, which is why old deeds can describe parcels by township surveys that no longer match current boundaries.

Many sellers assume the register will catch a mistake at the counter. It won't, because staff index what is handed to them and the person who prepared the deed answers for its contents. A misspelled grantor name or a mortgage discharge nobody filed also has to be fixed before a closing can finish. Ask the title company to read the recorded chain well before the closing date, not on the last day.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Genesee County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Where the other property records sit

Four offices hold the records a seller is likely to need, and only the register holds the recorded documents.

  • Register of Deeds, Suite 1A: deeds, mortgages, discharges, liens and foreclosure notices.
  • Equalization, Suite 8B: parcel descriptions and land records for every municipality except Flint, with assessment data left to the local assessor.
  • Flint Assessments Division: Flint's own parcel records, transfer affidavits, splits and combinations.
  • County Treasurer, Suite 2A: payoffs on delinquent tax and foreclosure information.

Before closing, order a payoff from the treasurer if tax is overdue, and confirm with the assessor that the parcel description matches the deed.

Why the record matters to a seller

Title companies and buyers read it as the public chain of ownership. Genesee has 185,007 housing units and 167,334 households, with owners in 70.7% of homes. A seller with a house that needs work or carries back tax can sell as-is for cash, and the payoff comes out of the proceeds when the deed is recorded.

A short checklist before listing:

  1. Pull your recorded deed and confirm the name and description match your ID and survey.
  2. Check that every old mortgage has a recorded discharge.
  3. Ask the treasurer for a payoff if any tax is overdue.
  4. Bring the deed, the fee and any value affidavit to the closing agent.

Frequently asked questions

What does the register charge to file a deed in Genesee County?

The state's baseline in MCL 600.2567 is $30 per document of any length. Because charter counties can set their own amounts, confirm the current Genesee County figure with the office before you pay.

Where do I find the Genesee County Register of Deeds?

The office is in the County Administration Building, 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. It is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, excluding holidays.

Is a recorded deed automatically valid?

No. Recording makes a document public and does not make it legal. The deed still needs proper signatures, a correct description and a grantor who owns the land.

Who writes the transfer tax check when a Genesee County house sells?

The seller does, to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed changes hands. The two levies are $3.75 and 55 cents on each $500 block of price.

Do I owe transfer tax on a deed to my child?

A deed to a child, stepchild, adopted child, grandchild or step-grandchild escapes the state tax. The deed is still recorded, and the usual filing fee applies.

Gladwin County register charges
ServiceCharge
Recording a document$30 flat, any number of pages
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3, added to the flat fee
Certification$5
Copies$1 a page
Searches50 cents per year, $5 minimum

Questions about the schedule trace back to MCL 600.2567. The flat charge already covers the state's remonumentation and automation shares.

What to bring when you file

A deed package that arrives complete is recorded without a second trip. Bring the signed original deed, a check for the $30 flat fee, and any extra $3 charges for additional instruments a discharge or assignment covers. If you want a certified copy afterward, add the $5 certification and $1 for each page copied.

Put the value of the sale in the text of the deed, or attach an affidavit that states it. Counter staff can quote the fee schedule. Drafting the deed itself falls to a title company or attorney.

Mailing it in? Phone ahead for the current total, because the amount turns on how many instruments the paper covers. Counter filings are paid on the spot, while e-filings get a one business day grace period.

Online land records and e-recording

The register's page links an online land records search and a free fraud alert sign-up, and the office takes electronic recording through three vendors. Paper filings still come in by hand or mail. Call the office to learn which vendors it uses before you submit anything online.

The alert is worth setting up if you own land you rarely visit. Whoever is away from the parcel tends to be the last person to learn that a paper was recorded against it, and the sign-up costs nothing.

Transfer tax at recording

Beyond the recording fee, the main charge is transfer tax. A seller pays $4.30 for each $500 of price, made up of $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county (the rate for counties with fewer than two million people). The county treasurer must receive it within 15 days after delivery.

The deed carries its value in the text, or an affidavit does. Several transfers sit outside the state levy, among them gifts to a child or grandchild, foreclosure deeds and mortgages. Payment timing follows the filing method, as described above.

Gladwin County at a glance

Gladwin County is rural and thinly settled, in the middle of the Lower Peninsula, and had an estimated 26,077 residents in 2025. Local government is two cities, Gladwin and Beaverton, and 15 townships. Each has its own treasurer for current bills, so first confirm which township or city your parcel is in.

  • Housing: 17,329 housing units, 11,280 households and an owner-occupancy rate of 86.1%.
  • Rent and value: median gross rent is $690, and the midpoint home value is $162,300.
  • Income: $55,349 for the median household.
  • Permits: 93 building permits in 2025.

Old legal descriptions

Gladwin's land was surveyed under the Northwest Ordinance in the 1830s, and settlement came much later. County government was organized in 1875. Some of the early survey work was faulty, so a seller holding an old legal description should ask the title company to check it against the parcel before closing.

The equalization department's GIS viewer helps locate a parcel on a map. If your description is old, print the viewer's map and the recorded deed together and bring both to your title company, so any mismatch is found while there is still time to record a correction.

How the tax calendar touches a sale

Township and city treasurers bill and collect first. Bills for summer are mailed July 1 and carry no interest through September 14 (Gladwin City runs a different summer schedule). The winter round is mailed December 1 and is due February 14.

Any balance left on March 1 moves to the county, which adds a 4% charge plus one percent interest a month. The county's timeline then shows a $15 mailing fee in October, forfeiture on the next March 1, a personal visit fee, a publication fee in the fall and a last payment date of March 31. Foreclosed parcels go to auction at tax-sale.info. Postmarks don't count. Payment is dated the day the county receives and processes it.

The treasurer also certifies deeds, plat maps and tax histories, so order a payoff and history before a sale. For principal residence, taxable value, hardship and veteran questions, ask the township or city assessor.

Who checks assessments

Equalization is a county department that reviews local assessments on behalf of the Board of Commissioners. Using an annual study, it aims to hold each property class in each local unit at 49% to 50% of true cash value. The local assessor stays responsible for fairness between individual parcels.

  • April: equalization report of values.
  • June: millage reduction fractions for each taxing authority.
  • October: apportionment report of allowable millage rates.
  • December 31: the sales and appraisal study.

The department also maintains the countywide database of values, descriptions, title changes, owner addresses and exemption status, plus a GIS viewer for locating land records and principal residence exemption forms. A deed recorded at the register shows up there as a title change, so a buyer should send in a change of address form after closing.

Selling when tax is still owed

A sale can proceed. The closing agent settles the overdue amount out of the seller's proceeds, based on a payoff that runs to the day of closing.

Timing matters because costs step up. Once a parcel forfeits, monthly interest goes from 1% to 1.5% retroactive to the original delinquency date, and a personal visit and publication fee follow. Redemption rights end at the close of business on March 31, so a seller near that date should request the payoff first. Buyers paying cash as-is can often close quickly when repairs or an inheritance stall a listing.

If the sale is a cash deal with a buyer who wants to move fast, the same payoff and certification still come first, because the closing agent needs both either way. Sellers who inherited a house and are still sorting out the title should ask the title company to review the recorded chain before listing. Steps that keep a sale moving:

  1. Ask the county treasurer for a payoff and a tax history.
  2. Pass both to the closing agent.
  3. Check that the deed carries its value or an affidavit.
  4. Pay the transfer tax to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivery.
You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What is the flat recording charge at the Gladwin County Register of Deeds?

It is $30 per document, whether the document runs one page or many. A discharge or assignment that covers several instruments adds $3 for each extra one.

When can I visit the Gladwin County Register of Deeds?

The office is open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon at 401 West Cedar Avenue. The telephone number is 989-426-7551.

Does the Gladwin office take e-filings?

Yes. The county works with three e-recording vendors. Call the office to learn which vendors it uses before you submit anything online.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Gladwin County sale?

The seller owes it. The combined state and county rate is $4.30 per $500 of price, paid to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

When does overdue Gladwin County tax go to the county?

On March 1 of the following year. A 4% fee and monthly interest of one percent start then, and the parcel can forfeit a year later.

What the Grand Traverse County Register of Deeds keeps

Land paperwork for the whole county lands here: warranty and quitclaim deeds, mortgages, land contracts, liens and releases. The public can search every file. Scanned images are indexed back to 1966, and a clerk can pull older papers, some dating to 1853, when given a liber and page.

The clerks hand out no blank forms and cannot coach a seller through the wording. The county's own advice is to hire a Michigan real property lawyer, call a title agent, or complete a deed yourself, with the warning that forms downloaded from the web sometimes fail the recording rules.

Traverse City is the only city and the county seat. A parcel on the Old Mission Peninsula, by a lake or in town is recorded at the same counter. A deed for land across the line in a neighboring county goes to that county's own register.

Fees at the recording counter

Filing a deed, mortgage or lis pendens costs $30.00 whether it runs two pages or twenty. Mailed checks go to Register of Deeds or GTROD, with a stamped return envelope or $3.00 to cover postage.

Grand Traverse County recording price list
ServiceCharge
One deed, mortgage or similar instrument$30.00
Each added instrument assigned or discharged$3
Treasurer certification, warranty deeds$5 for up to 25 parcels, then $0.20 each
Counter photocopies$1.00 per page, plus $5.00 to certify

The $30 figure traces to MCL 600.2567. The posted schedule is several years old, so phone the office before sending a large package.

How transfer tax is worked out

Clerks round the price up to the next $500 step and charge each step twice. The county levy is $1.10 for each $1,000, the 55 cents per $500 fixed by MCL 207.504 for a county this size. The state levy is $7.50 for each $1,000, which is the $3.75 per $500 in MCL 207.525. Together they take $8.60 from every $1,000 of rounded price.

A price that sits just over a $500 step jumps to the next step, so it costs a little more than one just under. Ask your closer to round the figure the way the register does.

The deed either states the full price or comes with a value affidavit, and an exemption is written into the instrument. The exemption lists sit in MCL 207.505 for the county tax and MCL 207.526 for the state tax. They cover small transfers under $100, foreclosure deeds and gifts from parents to children or grandchildren, among others.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Grand Traverse County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Filing a deed by mail

With a mailed package, complete paperwork matters more than speed, because the register can't fix a missing piece for you. Work through this list before you send it:

  1. Confirm the deed was drafted by a lawyer or title agent, since the register gives no drafting help.
  2. Check that the deed states the full price or has a value affidavit attached, and that any exemption is written into the instrument.
  3. For a warranty deed or land contract, attach the Treasurer's certification.
  4. Write one check payable to Register of Deeds or GTROD for the recording fee, the transfer tax and the certification.
  5. Add a stamped return envelope, or $3.00 for postage.

If anything is missing the package is likely to come back, and a delayed recording can hold up your closing. When in doubt, phone the office and ask what the total should be, and keep a copy of everything you send.

Why the treasurer certifies a warranty deed

Under MCL 211.135 a deed with a warranty covenant, or a land contract, cannot be recorded until the treasurer certifies two points: no tax liens are outstanding, and five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim with no covenant escapes this rule.

The Treasurer's office is at 400 Boardman Avenue, Suite 104, Traverse City, telephone 231-922-4735. Order the certification before the closing, because the register will hold the deed until it arrives.

The same elected official keeps the county's money, chairs the County Land Bank Authority, and runs the delinquent tax revolving fund that advances unpaid township and city taxes while the county pursues the owner. Each March the office starts collecting delinquent real property taxes. After a court order it can sell parcels that are more than 24 months behind, so a buyer or seller who sees an old balance on a parcel should get a written payoff first.

A seller who plans ahead can bring the following to the title company:

  • The Treasurer's certification, ordered ahead of the closing date.
  • A written payoff for any unpaid year, since the Treasurer collects delinquent bills from March 1 on.
  • The deed, drafted by a lawyer or title agent, because the register offers no drafting help.
  • A check for the $30.00 recording fee, the transfer tax and the $5 certification.

How fast unpaid tax can cost an owner the property

Current bills go to the township, city or village treasurer from July 1 through February. When March arrives, whatever is still owed shifts to the County Treasurer.

Two years of delinquency end the owner's rights. In year one the county adds a 4% fee plus 1% interest each month. After forfeiture the rate rises to 1.5% monthly, counted back to the first missed date, and a $175 title search and notice costs join the total. The county files a certificate of forfeiture with the register, so any buyer's title search will find it. On March 31 a year after forfeiture the county forecloses, and it calls that step final.

  • Partial payments slow the interest, provided the last one arrives before foreclosure.
  • Owners get five notices: two ordinary letters, two certified letters and one hand delivery.
  • If an auction brings more than the debt, a former owner files a Notice of Claim by July 1 and asks the court for the surplus the following February.

Owners with escrow accounts should know that lenders occasionally miss a bill, especially right after a refinance, yet the owner stays liable.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Grand Traverse County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Housing numbers and selling

Grand Traverse County has 40,287 households. A typical owned home is valued at $339,400, with owners living in 77.2% of homes. Median household income is $81,647 and median rent is $1,288.

Values at that level make transfer tax a noticeable line on a settlement statement. A seller with tenants, repairs or back taxes should order the treasurer's certification and a payoff letter first, so the title company can hand the register a clean deed.

A cash sale as-is can close faster when repairs or back taxes stall a listing, but the certification, the payoff and the recording fee all still apply.

Frequently asked questions

What is the filing fee for a deed in Grand Traverse County?

$30.00 per document, whatever the page count. A sale adds transfer tax, and a warranty deed adds a $5 treasurer certification.

How much transfer tax does a Grand Traverse County sale pay?

$8.60 for every $1,000 of price rounded up to the next $500: $7.50 to the state and $1.10 to the county.

Can a deed be mailed to the Grand Traverse County register?

Yes. Enclose a check payable to Register of Deeds or GTROD plus a stamped, self addressed envelope, or add $3.00 for postage and handling.

When do overdue taxes move to the Grand Traverse County Treasurer?

March 1 after the bill year. The county then adds a 4% fee and 1% interest each month, and forfeiture follows a year later.

Will the Grand Traverse County register help me write a deed?

No. The office provides no blank deeds and no drafting advice, so turn to an attorney or a title company.

This is a constitutional office, and its counter handles more than 200 kinds of paper. For a seller, the usual ones are warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, land contracts and mortgage releases. The shelves also hold powers of attorney and oil and gas leases, and filings stretch back to the 1800s. Anyone may inspect a recorded document during business hours. The same window takes passport applications until 3:30 p.m., so call first if you plan to do both errands.

Staff do not draft paperwork or give legal answers, so the deed itself is a job for an attorney or a title agent. Free public terminals sit on the courthouse's lower level and in the Treasurer's office if you want to look up a parcel yourself.

Recording fees

One $30 charge covers a document of any length. Cash, check or card all work. Transfer tax and a tax certificate are added where they apply, and the $30 base is set in MCL 600.2567.

Gratiot County recording and copy charges
ServiceFee
Record one deed, mortgage or instrument$30
Every added instrument assigned or discharged$3
Warranty deed or land contract tax certificate$5
Copy of a real estate record$1 per page
Certifying a copy$5 per document plus $1 per page
Name search of the real estate record$0.50 per year, minimum $5

Parcel research is priced through the Treasurer's side. Terminal printouts run $1 per page, phone lookups $3, and a written property tax and assessment report $5 per parcel. A new online account gets one free parcel lookup, and later searches on records with the same owner name stay free.

How transfer tax is figured

Think in $500 blocks, rounding the price up. Each block pays 55 cents to the county under MCL 207.504 and $3.75 to the state under MCL 207.525, for $4.30 a block. Raise the price by a single dollar past a block line and the count moves up by one. The tax is separate from the $30 filing charge.

The deed should show the whole price, or a value affidavit must be attached. The title company or closing attorney normally works out the exact figure and collects it at closing, so ask for it in writing a few days ahead.

  • County exemptions: MCL 207.505. State exemptions: MCL 207.526.
  • No state tax on a deed issued in a foreclosure or in lieu of one.
  • No state tax on a conveyance from a parent to a child, stepchild or grandchild.
  • No tax of either kind on a corrective quitclaim that confirms title already held.

When unpaid tax becomes the county's problem

Bills go out July 1 and December 1. A current tax is paid locally, at the township, city or village office, until the first of March next year. From that day the Gratiot County Treasurer collects it. Payoff amounts come by phone.

Unpaid balances move through a fixed schedule. They turn delinquent that first March 1, become forfeited one year later, and are foreclosed on the March 31 after that. For 2025 bills that means forfeiture on March 1, 2027 and foreclosure on March 31, 2028. Foreclosed parcels go to an online auction run through tax-sale.info.

  • Cards work for delinquent balances through Graphite, which bills 2.75% with a $1 floor and turns away American Express.
  • Neither the county nor a local treasurer answers for an escrow company that skipped a payment on a mortgaged home. If you have a mortgage, confirm the lender actually paid.
  • Since December 24, 2025 the Postal Service stamps the day mail is processed instead of the day it was dropped off, which can make a last-day envelope late. Pay a few days early or deliver by hand.

Selling with taxes owed

Taxes owed on the parcel do not block a listing, but they do surface at closing. The title company will ask the Treasurer for a payoff and take it out of your proceeds. If an old year is open, call the Treasurer's office early, because the amount grows as the schedule above advances and a foreclosed parcel can no longer be sold the ordinary way.

A cash buyer who skips the lender's underwriting and appraisal can often close faster, but the same tax certificate and recording steps still apply to the deed.

Tax certificate for a warranty deed

A $5 tax certificate from the Treasurer's office goes with warranty deeds, deeds containing a warranty covenant, land contracts and assignments of land contracts with a warranty clause. In MCL 211.135 the treasurer vouches that the last five years are paid and that no tax liens or tax titles hang over the land.

A quitclaim without covenants skips the step. For anything else, request the certificate early in the closing window and ask what an unpaid year would cost, because the register waits for it.

What happens after you record

Clerks screen each document against Michigan law first. A deed that clears is given the next number, stamped with the time, scanned whole and cross indexed, and its legal description plus buyer and seller are keyed into the search system. A title company later leans on that index to follow ownership.

Township and city offices, Equalization and the Treasurer each learn of a sale from this register and use it to prepare valuations for the next tax roll. After recording, any member of the public may read or copy the deed. The office suggests double-checking a document against recording requirements before submitting it, since a deed that fails the screen comes back and your closing date slips.

Before you go to the counter

Bring the signed and notarized deed, the $30 fee, any transfer tax due, and the Treasurer's tax certificate if the deed carries a warranty. If a lender is paid off at closing, the mortgage release is recorded as a separate instrument at its own fee. Most sellers never visit in person, since the title company or closing attorney files the paperwork for them. Ask them for the recording number afterward so you have proof the sale reached the public record.

Housing in Gratiot County

Gratiot County is mostly farmland and small towns in central Michigan. Ithaca is the seat and Alma is the largest city. Population has hovered near 42,000 since 2000, and the 2025 estimate is 41,190. The median home value is $147,500, with 78.9% of homes owner occupied and median rent at $834.

Frequently asked questions

How much does Gratiot County charge to record a deed?

$30 per document, no matter the page count. Transfer tax is extra on a sale, and a warranty deed needs a $5 tax certificate.

What are the Gratiot County Register of Deeds hours?

Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at the courthouse, 214 E Center Street, Ithaca. Passport applications stop at 3:30 p.m.

Is there a card option for delinquent tax in Gratiot County?

Yes. The Treasurer takes cards for delinquent taxes through Graphite, which adds 2.75% with a $1 minimum. American Express is not accepted, and online payments are processed in the morning and afternoon.

Will the Gratiot County register write my deed?

No. The office prepares nothing and answers no legal questions, so hire a lawyer or title agent. Before you submit, review the deed against the recording requirements so the clerks do not have to send it back.

When do Gratiot County tax bills go out?

July 1 and December 1. If one never shows up, call the township, city or village treasurer, because the tax is still owed. Current-year tax stays payable at that local office until March 1.

Filing a deed in Hillsdale County

Walk in to Room 212 of the County Office Building, 33 McCollum St., Hillsdale 49242, or phone (517) 437-2231. The window is staffed Monday to Friday from 8:30 in the morning until 5:00 in the afternoon. E-filings can be sent at any hour, but clerks work them only during posted hours and not on holidays.

Four e-recording vendors are approved: Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile and CSC/Ingeo. They are paid by ACH, may add charges of their own, and return the recorded document electronically. An e-filing that violates the Michigan Recording Act can be rejected.

A personal check will not pay for a paper filing, though certified funds are fine, meaning cashier's checks and money orders. Staff do not draft documents, supply templates, or offer anything that could be read as legal advice, so lean on your attorney or title company for the deed itself.

What recording costs

Recording a document costs a flat $30.00 under MCL 600.2567, as amended by PA 224 of 2016, with side charges listed below.

Statutory deed fees posted by Hillsdale County, effective October 1, 2016
Charge forPrice
Filing a deed or mortgage$30.00 total
Each extra instrument released$3.00
Treasurer's tax certificate (five descriptions)$5.00
Name search$5.00 floor, then 50 cents per year
Page of a real estate record$1.00
Certifying a copy$5.00

Lien searches at the state or federal level cost $3.00 per name, and plats copy at $2.00 per page. A transfer tax calculator is posted on the register's page for planning, with the final amount settled when the deed is presented.

Transfer tax on a sale

Count the $500 blocks in the sale price, rounding up, and multiply the count by $4.30. That rate is 55 cents for the county, from MCL 207.504, plus $3.75 for the state, from MCL 207.525. Your closing agent will run the number and collect it with the recording fee.

  • The deed shows the price, or an affidavit does.
  • A claimed exemption is stated on the instrument.
  • Statutory exemptions: MCL 207.505 (county) and MCL 207.526 (state).
  • A land contract is exempt while title stays with the seller, and the deed that completes it must reference the contract.

2018 law changes that still apply

A notice dated June 22, 2018 went from the register to title companies, attorneys and lenders about Public Acts 191 to 200, signed two days before. Most of the changes started on September 19, 2018, and they still shape what the office will accept.

  • A deed from a surviving owner must be backed by a certified death certificate recorded earlier, cited by liber and page, or filed alongside as a separate recording. Attaching a copy no longer meets MCL 565.48.
  • Documents signed outside Michigan follow Michigan's recording rules too, except for page layout (MCL 565.203).
  • Anything partly in a foreign language comes with an English translation (MCL 565.201).

Court orders need the clerk's certification and seal, an acknowledgment cannot omit its date, and fees are collected when a document is handed over.

Deed checklist

The register keeps a checklist of what a deed must contain, and a deed lacking one item can be bounced. Run your draft against it before closing day.

  • Ink signatures, each with a printed name that agrees with the notary's wording (MCL 565.201).
  • A mailing address for the grantee, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • A Michigan judge, court clerk or notary acknowledging any deed signed in the state.
  • Readable black type of 10 points or more on white 20 pound sheets, leaving 2.5 inches blank at the top of page one and half an inch elsewhere, under a line naming what the paper records.
  • Property value stated on the deed or in an attached affidavit.
  • Social Security numbers cut back to four digits.
  • Trust certificates that meet MCL 565.432 and 565.433.

Deeds signed before April 6, 2017 also had to say whether any male grantors were married or single, a rule that no longer reaches newer deeds.

Searching deed records

The register's page offers search by full text, using optical character recognition, and by name, date, and liber and page. Tract books are linked through Kofile. An owner who wants a deed corrected should know that the office cannot change or alter a document already recorded or in the middle of recording.

Title companies do much of the research for a sale. Three operate in the city of Hillsdale: Public Title, Midstate Title and Bell Title Tri County. Ask whichever one handles your closing to confirm the transfer tax figure, since the register collects it with the recording fee.

What the Treasurer needs before and after closing

MCL 211.135 calls for a certificate from the Treasurer on any warranty deed, land contract, or land contract assignment carrying a warranty clause. Five descriptions cost $5.00, and the office answers at (517) 437-4700.

Every year the Treasurer sends a delinquent tax notice that describes the last stage of Michigan's foreclosure process. One cutoff date decides whose name is printed in a two week newspaper ad before the Show Cause Hearing in Circuit Court. A little later the office refuses partial payments and personal or business checks, taking only cash, cashier's checks, money orders and credit cards (3% convenience fee).

Anyone with an old balance should ask for a payoff before listing the house, because the deed cannot move until the certificate issues. A seller who pays the balance from closing proceeds should have the title company request the payoff figure a few days ahead.

A seller's checklist for the closing week

Gather the signed deed, the Treasurer's certificate where a warranty applies, and proof of the price. Confirm with the title company whether the filing will go by e-recording or paper, since paper needs certified funds. After recording, keep the recorded copy. Hillsdale County also runs a free Property Alert service from the register that warns landowners of possible property fraud, which is worth joining if you keep other parcels. If anything looks wrong on the recorded deed, such as a misspelled name, tell your title company right away, because the register cannot alter a document once it is recorded and the fix usually means a corrective instrument at a new filing fee.

Housing in Hillsdale County

Hillsdale is the county seat and largest city, and the county is 607 square miles. The 2025 population estimate is 45,738, nearly flat since 2020. The median home value is $176,100, and owners live in 82.0% of homes, so a typical recording here is a home sale. Median rent is $832.

$30.00 buys the filing of a whole document. Transfer tax comes on top for a sale, and a warranty deed also needs a $5.00 certificate from the County Treasurer.

Can I e-record a deed in Hillsdale County?

Yes, through Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile or CSC/Ingeo. Payment goes by ACH, and the vendors may add fees of their own.

Is a personal check good for a Hillsdale County filing?

No. The office takes certified funds, such as a cashier's check or a money order, in its place.

When is the Hillsdale County register open?

Weekdays, from 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., in Room 212 at 33 McCollum St. Electronic filings may be sent at any hour but are handled only during those hours.

How is transfer tax figured on a Hillsdale County sale?

Round the price up to the next $500 and multiply the number of blocks by $4.30. The rate splits into $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county.

Where deeds are filed and until what hour

Houghton County deeds go to the courthouse in the city of Houghton, second floor, 401 E. Houghton Avenue (ZIP 49931). Call 906-482-1311. Staff are in from 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, yet the recording day closes at 3:30, so a deed delivered after 3:30 misses that day's recording.

The Register of Deeds page on the county site describes the office's job: keeping an index plus a copy of every recorded instrument tied to land here. The shelves hold deeds, mortgages, plats, surveys, land corners and a miscellaneous category. Anyone with a nagging boundary question can request the survey or the land corner record for the parcel before the listing goes live.

What the courthouse charges to file a deed

One flat $30.00 covers a document of any length. The figure already includes the state remonumentation charge and the register automation charge. Make the check out to the office by name. The fee comes from MCL 600.2567.

  • Add $3.00 for every instrument beyond the first named in an assignment or discharge.
  • Add $5.00 when a warranty deed, covenant deed, land contract or land contract assignment is certified.
  • Copies of real estate records are priced by the page at $1.00, and plat copies at $2.00.
  • A lien certificate search, state or federal, runs $3.00 for each name.

Transfer tax is billed separately and is not part of any of these numbers.

Transfer tax on a Houghton County closing

Michigan stacks a state tax and a county tax on the sales price. The county half, set at 55 cents in counties under two million people by MCL 207.504, governs here because Houghton County has under 40,000 residents. The deed must show the full consideration, or a sworn statement of value must ride along with it. Your title company will work out the total and collect it at closing.

Charges on a Houghton County deed
ChargeRateStatute

  • Paper that carries consideration below $100.

  • Court-ordered transfers where the judge sets no price.
  • A gift deed to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • A land contract, until title actually moves to the buyer.

The county statute's exemption list, MCL 207.505, contains no child or grandchild entry. Ask the office how the county portion works for a family deed.

Formatting mistakes that get a deed bounced

Under MCL 565.201 the register must refuse paper that breaks the layout rules. Check the draft against this list before it leaves your hands:

  • Black or dark blue ink for signatures, with a printed name under each one.
  • A grantee mailing address, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • A blank strip of 2.5 inches across the top of page one and half an inch elsewhere.
  • 10 point type or larger, on white stock of 20 pounds or heavier, sized 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • One opening line naming the single recordable event.
  • Social Security numbers cut to the last four digits, and any foreign language text translated.

Once a conforming instrument is in, the statute bars the register from refusing it over its content.

Can a deed be filed or searched without driving to the courthouse?

Yes on both counts. Four vendors send electronic filings here: CSC, ePN, Simplifile and Indecomm. They may submit at any hour, and the office works the queue between 8:30 and 3:30. The county advertises same day recording and fewer lost papers, while warning that some document types cannot go electronic.

For searching, the county points to Tapestry, an occasional-user tool covering September 1993 to the present. A search costs $8.75, viewing images is free and each printed page is $1.00. Professionals who search constantly can subscribe to Laredo. The in-office tract index is billed at $400.00 a month, $20.00 an hour or $5.00 per quarter hour. Owners can also enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert, which pings them when their exact name shows up on a newly recorded paper.

Old titles and parcels in the Copper Country

The mining boom drew people from dozens of countries, and a name search on a very old Houghton County deed is worth running under several spellings. Raise that with the title company early.

The land itself has changed too. In June 2018 a flash flood left sinkholes and washouts in Chassell, Houghton, Ripley, Lake Linden and Hubbell. A seller in one of those places should gather repair invoices and permits and keep them with the sale file, since a buyer will ask what was fixed.

County desks that handle taxes before a sale

The Treasurer is on the courthouse second floor too, at 906-482-0560, and keeps the same weekday schedule of 8:00 to 4:30. That desk collects delinquent real estate tax, certifies deeds and plats, prints tax histories and arranges partial payment plans. It also hosts the tax sale and foreclosure timeline pages.

Equalization supports 16 assessing jurisdictions and sends their taxable values to the State Tax Commission annually. Write to equalization@houghtoncounty.net or to Attn: Equalization, 401 E Houghton Ave, Houghton MI 49931. Calling the Treasurer ahead of closing shows the title company whether anything is owed.

Steps for a seller at the courthouse

First, get the signed deed from your attorney or title agent and check it against the layout list above. Second, ask the Treasurer whether the parcel has any unpaid tax and whether a warranty deed needs the $5.00 certification. Third, bring the check for recording and the transfer tax, or let the title company e-file. Arrive before 3:30 if you are delivering paper, because a later deed waits for the next recording day. Keep the stamped copy once it is returned.

The Houghton County market

The county covers 1,502 square miles of the Keweenaw Peninsula and has about 37,842 residents by the 2025 estimate. Houghton is the county seat, and Michigan Technological University is in the county. Owners live in 71.8 percent of the 19,308 housing units. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $159,900, and the typical rent is $840.

A single $30.00 charge applies no matter how long the document is. A $5.00 certification is added for warranty deeds and land contracts, and $3.00 for each further instrument in an assignment or discharge.

Is 3:30 really the last call for recording in Houghton?

Yes. Doors stay open until 4:30 p.m., though the day's recording ends at 3:30 p.m. E-files may arrive overnight and get worked during the 8:30 to 3:30 window.

Who pays transfer tax when a Houghton County home is sold?

Ask the title company or the register how your contract assigns it. The rates are $3.75 state plus $0.55 county for each $500, due when the deed is submitted.

Yes. Tapestry has records from September 1993 forward at $8.75 a search with free image viewing, and Laredo suits frequent searchers. For earlier material, call 906-482-1311.

Where Huron County deeds are recorded

Room 203 of the county building, 250 East Huron Avenue in Bad Axe (48413), is the recording desk. Phone 989-269-9941; fax 989-269-8786. The counter runs 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays, holidays excepted, and nobody locks the door at noon.

The county's page for the office explains that the land record indexes are searchable online back to 1947, with older land records going back to 1848 kept in the office. Documents can be delivered by hand or mailed. Correct fees have to arrive with the paper, and payment can be a check, a money order, cash or a card.

Why older records get thin around 1865

A courthouse fire explains it. The Legislature created Huron County on April 1, 1840, and it was fully organized January 25, 1859. Sand Beach, today's Harbor Beach, hosted the county seat until the courthouse burned in 1865 and took most of the records with it. Government moved to Port Austin, and in 1873 the Board of Supervisors picked Bad Axe.

Farm and shoreline parcels held by one family for generations may therefore show gaps in the earliest paper. Ask the title company early how it plans to deal with the oldest links in the chain, and look through the paper books in Room 203 where the online index stops.

Checking the record before you list

Begin with the online index and write down the book and page, or the document number, of your own vesting deed. The county page also links to Laredo search details and to Property Fraud Alert enrollment. Laredo is the program title searchers use on the official record, and the alert tells an owner when a filed paper carries the exact name entered.

  • Pull the deed that put the property in your name, plus every mortgage, so you know what must be released at closing.
  • Scan the index for easements, land contracts and assignments touching the parcel.
  • Enroll your name as it appears on title, and add a second entry for any variant.
  • Call 989-269-9941 about anything older than 1947.

If a recorded paper surprises you, staff in Room 203 can help you find it in the index.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Huron County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What a Huron County filing costs

Michigan sets a $30.00 charge for each recorded document, however many pages it has, in MCL 600.2567. The smaller items below may also appear on a seller's bill.

Huron County recording charges
ServiceCharge
Record one document$30.00
Each added instrument reached by one assignment or discharge$3.00
Certify a document on record$5.00
Photocopy$1.00 per page
Grantor or grantee search50 cents per year, $5.00 minimum

The charge is due as the paper is left for recording; for an electronic filing the statute gives one business day. Huron County names two e-recording firms: Simplifile, 1-800-460-5657, and CSC, 1-866-652-0111. For an unusual instrument, call the register to learn the exact amount.

Transfer tax after a sale

Two levies run on the price: $3.75 for each $500 or part of $500 as the state's share in MCL 207.525, and 55 cents per $500 as the county's share in MCL 207.504, which applies to a county under 2,000,000 residents. Divide the price by $500, round up, and multiply by the combined rate. The instrument must state the whole value, or an affidavit of value is attached.

The two acts diverge on family deeds. The state list in MCL 207.526 excuses a conveyance to a child or grandchild, yet the county list in MCL 207.505 has no such line. Ask the register before a parent signs a house over to a son or daughter.

What trips up a deed headed for Bad Axe

The recording statute, MCL 565.201, lists what a register of deeds may insist on. Walk through it with the drafter:

  • The typed name under every signature should match the name the notary wrote in the acknowledgment.
  • The notary's printed or stamped name belongs on the same page, near the notary signature.
  • A deed signed after January 1, 1964 carries its drafter's name and business address.
  • Cover or remove the first five digits of any Social Security number.
  • Attach a written English translation to any paper in another language.

When a paper is accepted and recorded, the statute treats it as conforming, and a compliant instrument cannot be refused for what it says.

Selling in the Thumb's northern tip

Huron County has Saginaw Bay on the west and Lake Huron on the north and east, with over 90 miles of shoreline. Farming leads the economy, and weekend visitors concentrate around Port Austin and Caseville. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $154,300, and owners occupy 81.8 percent of homes. The county's home page links an Assessing and Tax Search tool and a FetchGIS map, both handy for checking acreage and the parcel number before a deed is drafted.

Other offices in the Huron County building

The Treasurer's Office is in Room 204 of that building at 989-269-9238, open 8:30 to 4:30 with no lunch closure. Equalization is in Room 306 at 989-269-6497, sharing the room with Tax Mapping and GIS at 989-269-9421. Ask the Treasurer about the parcel's tax standing before the closing date so any balance is cleared out of the proceeds. The Huron County Land Bank operates from that same Treasurer's office. If the owner has died and the house passes through an estate, Probate Court is in Room 206 at 989-269-9944, and the County Clerk is in Room 201 at 989-269-9942.

Recording day, step by step

Your title company or attorney will usually handle this, but it helps to know the sequence. The signed and notarized deed is checked against the list above, then sent by e-recording or delivered to Room 203. The fee and transfer tax are paid with it. Once the office records the deed, it becomes part of the public index, and the Treasurer and assessing units update their files from it. Ask for the recording information afterward and keep it with your closing papers. If a mistake turns up later, such as a misspelled name, a corrective instrument is recorded as a new document at its own $30.00 charge, so it pays to read the deed carefully before it is signed. A seller who has a mortgage should also confirm that the lender's release was recorded, since a lingering lien can surface when the buyer's title company searches the index.

Frequently asked questions

When can I reach the Huron County Register of Deeds?

Weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except holidays, with no break at noon. The office is Room 203 at 250 East Huron Avenue, Bad Axe.

Can a Huron County deed be e-recorded?

Yes. Simplifile and CSC are the listed e-recording providers, so contact one of them and the office receives the document electronically.

How far back can I search Huron County deeds?

Online indexes begin in 1947, and land records from 1848 forward are held in the office. The 1865 courthouse fire at Sand Beach destroyed most early records.

Does a gift deed to my daughter owe transfer tax in Huron County?

The state tax exempts conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, while the county act's list shows no matching item. Call 989-269-9941 before counting on it, and state the exemption on the deed.

How do I pay the Huron County register of deeds?

Use a check, money order, cash or credit card, and include the correct fees with each recording. Checks may be made out straight to the Register of Deeds.

Mason holds the county seat, even though most of Lansing, the state capital, sits inside Ingham County. The recording desk is the Register of Deeds, 2nd Floor, 341 S. Jefferson Street, Mason, MI 48854. Mail goes to PO Box 195 at the same town, and the phone is 517-676-7216.

The front counter is staffed weekdays from 8 until 5. Older books live in the vault, which is open 8:30 to 4 by appointment only. A seller coming from East Lansing or Okemos should phone before making the drive.

Recording costs at the desk

The county fee schedule sets $30.00 for any deed, mortgage, lis pendens, certified court paper or similar real estate instrument, however many pages it runs. Smaller charges stack up when several papers file on the same day.

Does the Treasurer have to sign off before a warranty deed is recorded?

Yes. A tax certificate from the County Treasurer is a precondition for recording a warranty deed, covenant deed, land contract, or an assignment of land contract that carries a warranty clause. The same gate covers an affidavit fixing the legal description in one of those papers, and condominium master deeds, amendments that alter the legal description included.

The certificate is $5.00 for five parcel numbers and $0.20 for each one after that, citing MCL 211.135. A seller with a split or multi-parcel property should count the tax IDs first. Treasurer telephone: 517-676-7220. Ask for the certificate before the closing date, so it is already in hand when the title company sends the deed to Mason for recording.

Transfer tax: who pays and how much

The county's fee page puts the burden on the seller or grantor, payable when the instrument arrives for recording. The rates are $3.75 per $500 (state) and $0.55 per $500 (county). Divide the price by $500, round any fraction up to the next block, and multiply by the combined rate. The deed shows total consideration on its face, or a Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit comes with it, and any claimed exemption has to be written on the instrument.

The county tax falls under MCL 207.501 through 207.513 and the state tax under MCL 207.521 through 207.537. Three odd cases come up:

  • Land spanning two counties needs the price divided by parcel, and each county taxes its piece.
  • County tax applies to the price named in a foreclosure instrument.
  • A deed of easement or right of way is taxable as well.

Exemptions sit in MCL 207.505 and MCL 207.526.

What the Mason office checks on a deed

The office's recording requirements list covers only the common problems, but it is a useful pre-flight check:

  • Original ink signatures, typed or printed names beneath, black or dark blue.
  • An acknowledgment with the notary's signature, county and state of commission, expiration date and the place of signing.
  • A certified death certificate recorded as a separate document and cross-referenced when a survivor is named.
  • Court orders certified under the clerk's raised seal.
  • No correction fluid or tape.
  • A top margin of 2.5 inches on page one, and Social Security numbers cut to four digits or fewer.

The underlying rules are in Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, and neighboring sections.

How far back the online records reach

The index goes to 1956, and images start in 1960. Choose among three tools: Direct Search, a free index lookup that leaves out the latest seven days; Tapestry, at $8.95 a search with $1.00 per printed page; and Laredo, a subscription aimed at regular title searchers. For the years 1956 to 1981, check the vault by appointment, since county staff are still auditing indexed data from that stretch. Laredo subscription questions go to 517-676-7294.   • County Clerk, 517-676-7201: listed beside the Register of Deeds among the county's elected officials.
  • 30th Judicial Circuit Court, 517-483-6500: judgments and orders that may need recording against the property.

The courthouse is at 341 S. Jefferson, Mason, MI 48854, and the county also has an Equalization office for valuation questions.

Selling with taxes owed

If the parcel has an unpaid balance, ask the Treasurer at 517-676-7220 for the amount before you list. The title company will pay it from your proceeds at closing, and the tax certificate for a warranty deed cannot be issued until the parcel's tax standing is settled. Sellers who want a quick sale without repairs or lender delays sometimes go the cash route, but the recording steps stay the same: certificate, transfer tax, and the $30.00 filing. Bring or send the original signed deed, and ask the title company which of you will deliver it so nothing is filed twice. If you are coming in person, phone 517-676-7216 first to confirm the counter is staffed and that the deed meets the format list above. A rejected deed means a second trip to Mason and a delayed closing, which is easy to avoid with a quick call to the office.

The Ingham County market

Ingham County is home to Lansing, East Lansing, Mason and Michigan State University. The 2025 estimate is 289,709 people, with 59.5 percent of homes owner-occupied. A typical home is valued at $198,800 and typical rent is $1,084.

Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The vault closes earlier, with appointment hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Call 517-676-7216 to book.

Who writes the check for transfer tax in Ingham County?

The seller or grantor, as the county fee page describes it. Payment comes due as the deed is presented, at $3.75 per $500 for the state and $0.55 per $500 for the county.

Must I visit the Treasurer before my Ingham County deed is recorded?

Only for warranty deeds, covenant deeds and land contracts, which need a tax certificate first. It costs $5.00 for up to five parcel numbers and $0.20 for each extra one.

Is there a free way to search Ingham County deeds?

Yes, Direct Search is free and covers the index from 1956 forward, minus the most recent seven days. Seeing images through Tapestry costs $8.95 a search, and printing adds $1.00 a page.

Who records your deed

The Register of Deeds handles it. This office holds the land records for all of Ionia County, and a sale becomes public only once the deed is stamped, indexed and filed there. Staff will not help you draft or repair paperwork, so the papers should arrive complete, drafted by a lawyer or the closing company.

The seat is the city of Ionia. Filing can happen at the counter, through the mail, or through an approved electronic provider. Counter filings are handed back on the spot. Mailed packets come back only if you include a self-addressed return envelope, and anything sent without one is held 90 days. For questions, call (616) 527-5320 or write deeds@ioniacounty.org.

Filing costs

Thirty dollars pays for one document, however many pages it runs. The counter accepts cash, checks and cards, and a card adds a processing fee that varies with the amount. One check can cover the filing charge and both transfer taxes.

Ionia County Register of Deeds charges
ChargeAmount

Treasurer tax certification (warranty deeds, land contracts)$5.00

Transfer tax on an Ionia sale

A deed that transfers real estate for money owes two taxes. For the state it is $3.75 on each $500 of the price, and for the county $0.55 on each $500, with any leftover amount under $500 counted as a whole block. Your closing agent will confirm the final number before you sign.

Any claimed exemption goes in writing on the deed itself. The two Michigan statutes differ, and the gap matters for family transfers:

  • MCL 207.526 (state tax) exempts a deed from a parent or grandparent to a child, stepchild or grandchild, along with foreclosure deeds and deeds in place of foreclosure.
  • MCL 207.505 (county tax) exempts instruments valued under $100, security instruments, leases, and court orders that name no price, and it omits the child and grandchild category.
  • Both statutes exempt a land contract until the full contract price has been paid and title passes.

So a gift deed to a daughter can owe county tax while owing nothing to the state. Ask the office how your transfer is classified before you sign.

Treasurer certification

A Tax Certification from the Ionia County Treasurer has to accompany any warranty deed, any deed that contains a covenant of warranty, and any land contract or assignment of one. The $5 fee may be written into the check that pays the filing charge. A quitclaim deed has no warranty covenant, so it usually avoids this step, and you can ask the Register of Deeds whether yours qualifies.

If back taxes are owed on the parcel, raise it with your closing agent early, because the certification is part of the package that gets filed. Ask the County Treasurer what the office requires before it will issue one.

Why the office might send your deed back

Recording clerks hold each paper up to the state recording law, MCL 565.201 and its neighbors. A deed that falls short goes back to you, and a closing can stall for days while it is redone. Expect clerks to look at these points from the county's checklist:

  • Each signature must be an original, written in black or dark blue ink, and the signer's printed name goes underneath.
  • The notary block repeats those printed names, and the notary's name appears on the same page as the notary signature.
  • The buyer's mailing address is shown, along with the name and address of whoever drafted the deed.
  • Page one keeps a 2 1/2 inch blank band across the top, and half an inch is left clear on the other edges.
  • The first printed line says which single recordable event the paper covers.
  • The type is black and at least 10 point, set on white paper of 20 pound weight or heavier, letter or legal size.
  • When the grantor is a surviving owner, a certified death certificate is recorded first or together with the deed.
  • The full property value appears on the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit is attached.

Have the person who prepared the deed read through this list once more the day before closing.

Looking up Ionia County land records

Public workstations in the office are free for grantor and grantee searches, and copies cost $1 a page. Searching those machines by legal description or parcel number runs $1 per minute. If you ask staff to find your last deed, the fee is $5 plus copies, and the lookup works by name rather than by property.

Remote searching comes in two forms. Tapestry charges $8.95 per search and suits a single visit. Laredo bills monthly and fits agents, investors and anyone searching often; call the office to open an account. If either service gives you trouble, contact the vendor's support team (Fidlar) first and the Ionia filing counter after that. A title company search digs deeper than either tool when you need the full ownership chain behind your house.

Back taxes before closing

Old tax on the parcel surfaces the moment the title company asks the Treasurer for a certification. Call the County Treasurer for a payoff number before the sign goes up. It is paid out of your sale proceeds at closing, and the deed is not filed until the certification is in the package. A cash buyer can often close quickly, but the same certification, transfer tax and filing steps apply to the deed.

Local market snapshot

Ionia County had 66,557 residents in July 2025, a little below the 66,804 counted in April 2020. About 77.3 percent of households own, with a typical owned home worth $198,500. Rent runs $884 a month at the median. The county feeds the Grand Rapids job market, and resale houses supply most of what buyers see, so your listing joins that pool.

Property tax after you sell

A sale ends the cap on the house's taxable value. Under Proposal A the reset lands in the year following the sale, so the buyer's first full bill can rise toward the assessed value. Michigan Treasury posts the Property Transfer Affidavit, Form 2766, and it is the buyer who files that form with the local assessor. Ask the assessor for your city or township about the filing deadline.

Some transfers, listed in section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act, leave the cap in place. Assessment is a local job in Michigan, handled by the city or township where the house stands, so the assessor there is the person to call about taxable value. Current bills come from that same local unit, and the County Treasurer takes over delinquent ones.

Frequently asked questions

Does Ionia County bill by page count?

No. Each document costs $30 to file. Documents that assign or discharge several instruments add $3 for each extra one.

May I email a deed to the Ionia County Register of Deeds?

No. Email filings are refused. Electronic recording runs through accredited servicers: Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, EPN and CSC. Only a scanned original signed document is accepted.

Who covers transfer tax in Ionia County?

Payment comes with the deed at filing, and who bears it depends on your purchase agreement. Read it, and watch the settlement statement for the amount.

Will paying off my mortgage give me a new deed?

No. Your lender files a discharge of mortgage, which carries the same $30 filing charge, and your original deed remains the proof of ownership.

Is a quitclaim to a relative taxed in Ionia County?

It may be taxed by the county. The state list exempts gifts to a child or grandchild, and the county list leaves them out. The deed has to state the exemption, so ask the office first.

What the Register of Deeds does for a home seller

The Iosco County Register of Deeds files and keeps every deed, mortgage, survey, land contract, condominium and subdivision document for real estate in the county. The county's own records begin in 1858. All of them have been digitized, and the online index reaches back to the early 1970s. Anything older is searched in person at the office, or by a title company you hire.

Tawas City is the seat. Selling a house here means the closing deed gets filed with this office. The office has no forms, is not staffed by attorneys, and will not advise on legal questions or prepare papers, so line up a lawyer or title company for that part.

Filing fees

A deed costs $30 to file. Some documents, such as a discharge of mortgage, an assignment of mortgage or an oil and gas paper, cross-reference other instruments, and each cross-reference after the first adds $3. Two payees are involved, so write two checks when a treasurer certification is needed.

Certified copy$5 plus $1 per pageIosco County Register of Deeds
Tax certification$5 per documentIosco County Treasurer

Which documents need a tax certification?

Warranty deeds, land contracts, assignments of land contracts, and any other paper containing a Warrant and Defend or Covenant clause need a tax certification. The $5 payment goes to the Iosco County Treasurer, not to the Register of Deeds. Ask your closing agent to add it to the settlement statement.

Quitclaim deeds carry no covenant of warranty. Whether yours needs a certification is a question for the Register of Deeds before you submit it.

Transfer tax on an Iosco County sale

Michigan taxes deeds that convey property for money twice, once for the state and once for the county. The Resources page of the Iosco Register of Deeds carries three PDFs: a Transfer Tax Chart, a county exemption list and a state exemption list. Ask the office, or open that chart, for the exact dollar amount at your sale price.

Both statutes (MCL 207.505 for the county tax, MCL 207.526 for the state tax) shield some transfers entirely. Examples that come up in house deals:

  • An instrument with consideration under $100.
  • A deed used to confirm a title already held, such as a quitclaim that fixes a flaw.
  • A conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties between spouses.
  • A deed that creates a joint tenancy when one of the people already owns the property.
  • A transfer in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure of a government-backed or government-made loan under the county act, and any mortgage foreclosure under the state act.

If one fits your sale, the deed has to cite it on its face.

Michigan filing rules an Iosco County deed must meet

The state recording statutes, chiefly MCL 565.201 and 565.8, govern the format of every deed, and the Iosco office insists on an original with original signatures. Court orders and death certificates must carry a certified raised seal. Beyond that, county offices across Michigan flag these points:

  • Signatures are typed or printed beneath, and the notary acknowledgment matches those names.
  • The paper lists who drafted it, with name and address.
  • A deed to survivors comes with a certified death certificate on record.
  • A trust agreement that accompanies an instrument is recorded as its own document.
  • Anything in a language other than English has a written English translation attached.

A rejected deed pushes a closing back, so have the preparer check the document against the Iosco office's own requirements page before it goes in.

From closing to a filed deed

Most of the sequence happens before anyone walks into the Tawas City office, and a short checklist keeps the file complete:

  • Have the deed drafted by an attorney or title company, since the office will not prepare it.
  • Sign it in front of a Michigan notary, using original signatures only.
  • Add the tax certification request if the deed has warranty language, with a separate $5 check to the County Treasurer.
  • Calculate the transfer tax from the county chart, or note the exemption on the deed.
  • Submit the deed with a $30 check to the Register of Deeds, adding $3 for each extra cross-reference where one applies.
  • Confirm the filing later through the DoxPop search to see that the document shows up in the index.

The search index reaches back only to the early 1970s, but a deed from this closing will be in it, so a quick lookup afterward confirms the record is complete.

Searching Iosco County property records

Search recorded documents through the county's DoxPop link, or visit the office. Staff will not run genealogy searches on your behalf, though visitors may use the records themselves. A Property Watch service from DoxPop sends a notice when a new document is recorded against a property you name.

If you want a copy of your deed, you can get one online or at the counter for $1 a page. Paying off a mortgage does not produce a new deed, since your lender records a discharge and your original deed remains the proof of title.

Selling with taxes owed

Delinquent tax on the parcel is something to settle before the deed is filed. Ask the Iosco County Treasurer for the amount owed and give it to your closing agent, who can pay it from the sale proceeds. The tax certification for a warranty deed is the Treasurer's confirmation that the taxes are in order, so an open balance can hold up the paperwork. Sellers who want to avoid lender delays sometimes choose a cash sale, which still ends with the same deed, certification and filing.

The Iosco County market

Iosco is a Lake Huron county where most residents live along the US-23 shoreline in East Tawas, Tawas City and Oscoda. The population estimate for July 2025 is 25,266. There are 20,221 housing units but only 11,713 households, and 41.3 percent of the units were vacant in the 2020 census, a sign of the cottages and seasonal houses common here. Owners hold 82.1 percent of the occupied homes. A typical owned home is valued at $142,200, and median rent is $719 a month.

Property tax after you sell

A change of ownership lifts the cap on taxable value the following calendar year, as Michigan Treasury explains in its guidance on Proposal A. The affected buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the local assessor. Which exemptions avoid uncapping is spelled out in section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act.

Iosco County has an Equalization department and a Treasurer's Office. Ask them how a specific parcel is assessed and billed.

Frequently asked questions

What does the Iosco office charge to file a deed?

$30, with $3 more for each additional cross-referenced instrument on documents such as mortgage discharges. Copies are $1 a page and certified copies are $5 plus $1 a page.

Do I need a new deed after paying off my Iosco County mortgage?

No. Your lender sends you a discharge of mortgage to record. The deed you received at purchase continues to prove ownership.

Who writes the check for the $5 tax certification in Iosco County?

You do, payable to the Iosco County Treasurer only. Recording fees and copy charges go on a separate check payable to the Iosco County Register of Deeds.

Will Iosco staff add a name to my deed?

No. The office tells people to consult an attorney for that kind of change, because each situation differs. Staff do not prepare documents or give legal advice.

Can I record a photocopied court order in Iosco County?

Where an Isabella County deed gets filed

Filing happens in Room 220 of the county building at 200 N. Main Street, Mount Pleasant, MI 48858. The office phone is (989) 317-4089. Land records here reach back to the mid-1800s, and a recorded document is open for anyone to review or copy. Staff neither draft documents nor answer legal questions, so a lawyer or closing company should finish the paperwork first.

Mount Pleasant is the county seat. When your house sells, the closing deed lands at this counter, and the office urges a careful read against the recording rules before anything is handed in.

The filing charge

State law sets a flat $30.00 for each document. If a document lists several liber and page references, each one beyond the first costs $3.00. Mail-in filers who want the original back should send a prepaid return envelope.

Isabella County recording and certification charges
ServiceCharge
Recording, per document$30.00 flat
Each additional liber and page listed$3.00 (first one free)
Tax certificate, up to 5 descriptions$5.00
Tax certificate, each description past 5$0.20
Name search by the office$0.50 per year searched, $5.00 minimum

Tax certificate checks are payable to the Isabella County Treasurer. Copies from a search carry the statutory copy fee, which the office will quote.

Which sales need a tax certificate first?

Section 211.135 of Michigan law requires a treasurer certificate before the office will file any of these:

  • Warranty deeds, plus any other deed with a covenant of warranty written into it.
  • Land contracts, and their assignments when a warranty clause is attached.
  • Condominium master deeds.

The treasurer issues it, so the check goes to the Isabella County Treasurer. Parcels with many descriptions pay 20 cents for each one after the fifth. Have your closing agent request the certificate before signing day so it cannot delay the filing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Isabella County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording rules for deeds

The county posts a summary of the Michigan recording rules people ask about most, and refers readers to the legislature's website for the full text. Highlights from that list:

  • Original signatures only, each name typed, stamped or printed below, and no mismatch among the body text, the signature and the acknowledgment.
  • Every party's address is shown on any instrument that conveys, assigns or encumbers title.
  • A deed signed in the state is acknowledged by a notary and names its drafter with an address.
  • If the grantor section names a survivor, a certified death certificate is filed as a separate document.
  • A trust agreement attached to an instrument is filed on its own under Public Act 194 of 2018.
  • Court orders arrive certified and sealed by the clerk of the court.
  • Page one leaves 2 1/2 inches blank at the top, other margins run 1/2 inch, and the type is black, 10 point or larger, on white paper.
  • Any part written in another language needs an English translation attached.

Public Acts 191 through 200 of 2018 changed some of these rules, and the legislature's site has the details.

Transfer tax on an Isabella County sale

Two Michigan laws tax real estate transfers: Act 330 of 1993 at the state level and Act 134 of 1966 for counties. The dollar amount at your sale price comes from the Register of Deeds, and the settlement statement will show it.

A few statutory exemptions come up with house transfers, and the deed must carry the claim:

  • Spouses moving property into or out of entireties ownership.
  • Boundary-line adjustments made without payment.
  • Corrective quitclaims that only confirm a title the grantee already holds.
  • New joint tenancies where one of the co-owners already had the property.

Gifts to a child or grandchild are exempt only in the state act, so a family gift needs a question to the office first.

What to gather before the deed goes in

A complete package avoids a second trip to Mount Pleasant. Pull these items together with your closing agent:

  • The signed, notarized original deed, with the drafter's name and address on it.
  • A check for $30.00 to cover the recording, plus $3.00 for each extra liber and page.
  • The treasurer's tax certificate and its separate check, when the deed has warranty language.
  • The transfer tax payment or a stated exemption.
  • A return envelope, stamped and addressed, if the package goes by mail.

Once the office records the deed, it becomes a public record, and any buyer, lender or neighbor can pull a copy. That is why a clean filing matters.

Selling near a university

The paperwork is the same, yet the buyer pool differs. Central Michigan University sits in the county, and 61.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied, with renters in 39.9 percent of occupied units at the 2020 census. For a landlord selling a rental near campus, that means a deed from an investor-owned property that may have tenants in place. Read any lease before you fix a closing date.

Part of Mount Pleasant also lies within the Isabella Indian Reservation, which spans 217.67 square miles and is the main land base of the Saginaw Chippewa Tribal Nation. Your title company can tell you whether your parcel sits inside the reservation and whether that changes the paperwork.

Selling with taxes owed

If the Treasurer shows unpaid tax on your parcel, the certificate for a warranty deed cannot be issued cleanly until it is dealt with. Call the Treasurer for the amount, hand it to your closing agent, and it comes out of your proceeds at closing. A sale to a cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal but not this step. If you plan to mail the package, send it early with a prepaid return envelope, since the office cannot return the recorded deed without one. After recording, ask your closing agent for a copy of the recorded deed and keep it with your sale papers, because the county's index is the public proof that ownership moved to the buyer.

Housing in Isabella County

Isabella County had 64,691 residents in mid-2025. A typical owned home is valued at $170,400, and median rent is $913 a month.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How the next tax bill changes after a sale

Selling resets taxable value: under Proposal A the cap lifts in the calendar year following the transfer. Form 2766, the Property Transfer Affidavit, is the paper the new owner sends to the local assessor. Some transfers are carved out of uncapping in subsection (7) of MCL 211.27a.

In Michigan, assessing is largely handled by cities and townships. The local assessor can tell you your taxable value and when the affidavit is due.

Frequently asked questions

How much does a deed cost to file in Isabella County?

Thirty dollars flat per document, with $3.00 added for every extra liber and page reference past the first. When a tax certificate is required, it runs $5.00 for up to five descriptions.

Who issues the tax certificate for an Isabella County warranty deed?

The county treasurer's office. Your check for the certificate is payable to the Treasurer, and it must be obtained before the Register of Deeds records a warranty deed, land contract or condominium master deed.

How do I get my filed deed returned by mail?

Include a self-addressed, stamped return envelope with the package. Without it the office has no way to mail the recorded paper back.

Will Isabella County staff review my deed for legal problems?

No. The office neither drafts papers nor answers legal questions. An attorney handles that, and you should check the recording requirements before you submit.

What does a name search cost at the Isabella County office?

Fifty cents for every year searched, set by MCL 600.2567, with a $5.00 floor. Copies pulled from a search are billed at the statutory copy rate.

Where to bring a signed deed

The Jackson County Register of Deeds is at 120 W Michigan Ave, 12th Floor, Jackson, MI 49201. The counter opens 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, and stays open over lunch. Call 517-788-4350 with questions. County holidays are days off.

Most sellers never make the trip. Your closing agent normally files the deed and pays the fees. Transfer tax is still yours, and it shows as a deduction from your proceeds, so it pays to understand how the counter treats it.

One office handles the whole county, whether the parcel is in the city of Jackson or in a village such as Brooklyn, Concord, Grass Lake, Hanover, Parma, Springport or Cement City. The county has 159,552 residents and 69,801 housing units, and 75.0 percent of occupied homes are owner occupied.

Recording fees

The recording charge is a flat $30 for one document of any length. It has been in place since October 1, 2016, and $4 of it goes toward survey monument upkeep. The authority is MCL 600.2567.

Smaller charges that may apply:

  • $3 per extra instrument when one paper assigns or discharges several.
  • Page copies at $1, and $5 for a certified document.
  • Name searches at 50 cents per year searched, $5 at the least.
  • Tax lien name searches, state or federal, at $3 each.

Payment is accepted by cash, check or card. Make checks payable to the Register of Deeds, and transfer tax can go on that same check.

How transfer tax works

A sale triggers two taxes. The county rate is 55 cents and the state rate $3.75, each applied per $500 of price, with any leftover part of $500 billed as a whole step. The seller is the taxpayer under MCL 207.523, and the county's share is set by MCL 207.504.
