Put the full price on the deed. To leave the price off the document, file a valuation affidavit and say so on the deed. The affidavit has no filing fee. An exemption claim also goes on the deed itself.

Deeds that owe no transfer tax

Some transfers are exempt, though the county and state lists differ. Both taxes skip a deed given as security, a transfer under $100, and a deed between spouses that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties. The state tax also skips a deed from a parent or grandparent to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, plus deeds made through a foreclosure or in lieu of one. See MCL 207.526.

The county list in MCL 207.505 is shorter. So a gift deed to a daughter or son may owe no state tax but still owe county tax. Call the register of deeds and describe the exact deed before anyone signs.

Tax paid on a deed that turns out to be exempt can be reclaimed by asking the state treasury department for a refund.

Treasurer's certificate for warranty deeds

Any deed with warranty language needs one, and so do land contracts and assignments of them that include a warranty clause. The county treasurer first certifies the tax history that MCL 211.135 covers, five years back from the date of the deed. A quitclaim deed with no warranties is excepted.

The certificate costs $5 in Jackson County. It needs its own check payable to the Jackson County Treasurer, submitted along with the deed.

When taxes are owed on the house, request the payoff amount early. Closing pays it out of your sale proceeds.

Why a deed gets sent back

Paper that breaks MCL 565.201 comes back unrecorded. The usual culprits are layout slips and missing names:

  • Sheets outside the legal size range, faint ink, or type below 10 point.
  • A top band on page one that is under 2.5 inches.
  • A first printed line that fails to say which single event is being recorded.
  • No printed name beneath a signature, a notary name on a different page from the notary's signature, or no grantee address.
  • Missing drafter name and business address.
  • Unredacted social security numbers.

Photocopies are refused, because only original signatures qualify. Court papers need the court seal, and a death certificate needs the clerk's seal. The office cannot write your deed or sell forms. An attorney or title agent can.

Step by step when you record the deed yourself

Closings rarely need this, but anyone filing alone can follow a short path. First, confirm the deed type and whether it carries warranty language, since that decides whether a treasurer's certificate is needed. Second, compare the layout to the list above before printing. Third, sign before a notary, in original ink.

Then take the deed, the $30 fee, any transfer tax and the separate $5 treasurer check to 120 W Michigan Ave. Ask the counter if your exemption is on the correct list. Bring a phone or pen for notes, and ask the clerk to confirm the recording date before you leave. If something is wrong, staff return the paper and you fix it and file again, so allow a little time before a closing date.

Hold on to a copy of the recorded deed, along with your receipt. A later buyer or title agent will want it first.

Housing in Jackson County

Owners are the bulk of the market. Median monthly owner costs run $1,377 with a mortgage and $557 without, and median rent is $985. The middle home value is $193,700, and 21.5 percent of residents are 65 or older.

Because more than one resident in five is past 65, sales following a death or a move into care are common. A tidy deed history speeds those along.

Land near the Grand River in the city of Jackson, or the north branch of the Kalamazoo River in Hanover Township, may carry easements in its recorded history. Request a records search if yours might.

Searching recorded documents

The online grantor and grantee name search spans deeds, mortgages and miscellaneous papers. High volume copy buyers may request an escrow account. You can also bring your parcel's legal description to the counter, and staff will help you start a records search. Questions about easements or lake rights are often answered by the title insurance policy you received when you bought.

Owners can enroll in a free alert that reports any filing made under their name. It is a no cost way to spot a forged deed.

What to gather for a buyer

When a buyer asks a title question, assemble your recorded deed, your loan payoff letter and any lien notices. That bundle covers most requests. A cash buyer has no lender demanding extra title paperwork, so these pieces are often enough.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Does the recording fee go up with extra pages?

No. A long deed costs the same $30 as a short one. The only add on is $3 for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges.

Who owes transfer tax on a Jackson County sale?

The seller does. The county takes 55 cents and the state $3.75 on each $500 of price, unless the deed states a valid exemption.

Will the office record a copy of my deed?

No. Only the original signed paper is taken. Court orders carry the court seal, and death certificates carry the clerk's seal.

Is a tax certificate needed for a quitclaim deed?

Usually no, since the statute exempts quitclaim deeds that carry no warranty covenants. Warranty deeds and land contracts are the ones that need it.

When can I visit the Register of Deeds?

Come Monday to Friday between 8 and 4, noon hour included. Legal holidays are days off, so call 517-788-4350 first.

Where Kalamazoo County land records are filed

The Register of Deeds sits in the County Administration Building at 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue, Kalamazoo, MI 49007. The phone is 269-383-8970. It is a constitutional office dating from 1835, and recording a document makes it public without making it legally valid.

Staff index and preserve the records, nothing more: title searches and legal advice are off limits. In most sales the title company either walks the deed in or e-records it. If you file on your own, read the formatting checklist below, because the counter turns away papers that miss a rule.

All four cities (Galesburg, Kalamazoo, Parchment and Portage) and all five villages (Augusta, Climax, Richland, Schoolcraft and Vicksburg) record at this single office.

Recording fees

Recording costs $30 a document under MCL 600.2567. Extras that can apply:

  • $3 more for each added instrument on a paper that assigns or discharges several.
  • Copies at $1 a page, plus $5 a document if certified.
  • $5 per search when staff look something up.

Payment options at the counter are cash, check, money order or card. Recording checks are payable to the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds and certificate checks to the treasurer involved. There is no online payment portal for counter filings, so card payers phone the office or come in. The full list is on the county fee schedule.

Transfer tax

The seller owes transfer tax, and it is paid at the counter when the deed goes on record. The state act names the seller as the taxpayer in MCL 207.523, and the county rate comes from MCL 207.504. Both are applied to a price rounded up to the next $500.

Deeds that need a tax certificate

When the grantor "warrants" or "defends" the title in the deed, the treasurer must clear the taxes first. On the county's list are warranty and covenant deeds, land contracts, land contract assignments with warranty wording, and master deeds, amendments adding property to a condominium among them. The rule comes from MCL 211.135.

Inside the City of Kalamazoo there is one more step. You obtain a city certificate from the City Treasurer at Kalamazoo City Hall, 241 W South Street, phone 269-337-8036, for $10. The County Treasurer issues its own only after that.

Unpaid taxes block clearance until the balance is settled at closing. Get the payoff amount early, since delinquent balances gather interest every month.

What a document must look like

Layout is governed by MCL 565.201, and the county FAQ turns it into a checklist:

  • White copy paper, letter or legal size.
  • Black ink, 10 point type or larger.
  • A clear 2.5 inch strip across the top of page one, the document type printed on the first line below it, and half inch margins elsewhere.
  • A notary for the deed types the county lists, including warranty, quitclaim, executor, trustee and sheriff's deeds. Witnesses are no longer required.
  • Court documents bearing the court's certification and seal.

Rejected papers are returned with a letter giving the reason, and you fix and refile. Changing the names on a deed means a new deed. The office cannot prepare it for you, so call an attorney or title agency.

Recording a deed electronically

E-recording runs through four certified vendors: Simplifile, Indecomm, ePN and CSC. Submissions are worked on county business days. Money moves by ACH under the vendor's agreement, and a vendor can tack on its own processing fee. Plats and master deeds with full size maps cannot be sent this way.

Michigan's statewide e-recording standards took effect on January 1, 2014, and the county follows them. The title company submits the deed, so sellers seldom meet a vendor.

A Consumer E-Recording portal serves one time filers with affidavits, discharges, mortgages, certificates of trust, liens and releases. Ownership transfers such as deeds, UCC documents and foreclosure papers are not accepted there. For a deed, go to the counter or a title company.

Searching land records

Start with the Document Searches page on kalcounty.gov. The Deeds Search tool is free for index searching, then costs $1 a page plus a processing fee to view, print or save an image. Tapestry EON, available since October 21, 2024, costs $8.75 per search. Laredo is a monthly subscription aimed at frequent users such as title professionals.

Staff can pull your latest deed for $5 a property and $1 a page, with certification for another $5. Public workstations in the Administration Building let you search grantor and grantee names free, with printing at $1 a page. Search by name, since recorded papers need no address.

Land record images reach back to 1831, though the complete index only starts in 1984. For a long chain of title, a title company search is the safer route.

When an owner dies

Surviving owners do not need a new deed. Recording an official death certificate with this office shows that the deceased owner's interest has ended, and the certificate becomes part of the title chain. Photocopies of death certificates are refused.

County staff cannot tell heirs what authority they need to sell, so put that question to the title company. A free fraud alert is also available: register a personal or business name and you hear whenever a matching document is recorded. That is handy for an empty inherited house.

Selling an inherited house

Collect the death certificate, recorded deed, and any payoff or tax statements first. A cash sale skips the repairs and showings of a traditional listing, which suits an estate that wants to finish quickly.

What to expect at closing

A title company or closing attorney drafts the deed, subtracts transfer tax from what you net and delivers everything to the Register of Deeds. For a City of Kalamazoo address, both treasurer certificates are requested ahead of filing, so build that extra step into your closing timeline.

Filing on your own means carrying an original notarized deed, a $30 check, the transfer tax and one more check per treasurer certificate. Not sure what type of deed you hold? Phone 269-383-8970 first, because the type decides whether a certificate is needed.

Kalamazoo County housing at a glance

Kalamazoo County has 263,795 residents and 116,117 housing units. Owners live in 64.5 percent of occupied homes, so many sellers here are landlords. The middle home value is $241,800, median gross rent is $1,093 a month, and median household income is $72,532 in 2024 dollars.

Owners outside the city limits record here as well. Ask the township or village treasurer about local tax.

What does it cost to record a deed in Kalamazoo County?

Thirty dollars a document. Transfer tax and treasurer certificates are billed separately, and a paper discharging several instruments adds $3 per extra one.

Is transfer tax my bill as a seller?

Yes, paid at the Register of Deeds counter when the deed is recorded. The county charges $1.10 and the state $7.50 for every $1,000, after the price is rounded up to the next $500.

Yes. A parcel within city limits pays $10 for the city certificate first, then $5 for the county one.

Are witnesses required on a Kalamazoo County deed?

No. A notary is the requirement now, for warranty, quitclaim and most other deed types.

Can I pay recording fees by card?

Put the property value on the deed, or file a valuation affidavit. The affidavit costs nothing but must be noted on the deed. An exemption claimed under MCL 207.505 for the county or MCL 207.526 for the state has to be written on the deed too.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Kalkaska County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Deeds that owe no transfer tax

Exemptions come from the two transfer tax acts, and the county posts both lists on its recording fees page. Both exempt security instruments, leases and deeds from a government grantor, along with confirmation deeds, such as a quitclaim that repairs a flaw in a title the grantee already holds.

Family transfers split. Only the state act exempts a deed from a parent to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild. The same statute also exempts foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu, though a later resale by the foreclosing party is taxed.

Whichever exemption applies, write it on the deed. If tax was paid on a deed that qualified, the state act lets the seller request a refund from the state treasury.

Electronic filing

Most document types can be e-recorded. Judgments, court orders, plats, surveys and other certified papers cannot. The partner vendors are ePN, CSC, Indecomm and Simplifile. Simplifile alone handles warranty deeds, land contracts and other treasurer certified papers.

Title professionals sign up for Laredo, the county's records search program, by sending the register of deeds a subscription agreement. Individual owners can use the fraud alert and the front counter.

A one time seller is usually best served when the title company or closing attorney e-records. To carry a paper deed instead, read the layout list below first, because a returned deed can delay closing.

Page layout the counter accepts

MCL 565.201 binds this office like any other, and an instrument missing an item cannot be accepted. Homemade deeds tend to fail on these points:

  • 2.5 inches of open space atop page one, and half inch margins around the rest.
  • Dark print, 10 point type, on white paper no lighter than 20 pound.
  • A single phrase on the first printed line naming what is being recorded.
  • Names printed beneath every signature, and the notary's name beside the notary signature.
  • The grantee's address, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • An attached English translation when part of the text is in another language.

The statute adds that anything already recorded is conclusively presumed to comply, so a deed that clears the counter stays on record even if a small slip went unnoticed.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Kalkaska County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Filing a paper deed yourself, step by step

Start by deciding which deed you hold. A warranty covenant deed or land contract needs the treasurer's certificate first, so visit the county treasurer before the register of deeds. Next, check your document against the layout list above, including the blank strip on page one and the printed names under every signature.

Then take the original to 605 N. Birch Street with the $30 recording fee and the transfer tax. State the value on the deed or attach the valuation affidavit, and write any exemption on the deed. Card payers use the county payment page and the posted paycode.

Afterward, sign up for the free fraud alert with your name so you hear about any document recorded against your property. It costs nothing and works for individuals and businesses. If a deed ever appears that you did not sign, call 231-258-3315 right away and ask what steps the office can take.

The Kalkaska County housing market

This is a small market where nearly everyone owns. The county has 18,693 residents in 11,820 housing units, a gain of 4.2 percent over the April 2020 base. Owners live in 88.2 percent of occupied homes. The middle home value is $188,900, and median rent is $853 a month.

About 24.6 percent of residents are past 65, and density is only 32 people per square mile. Buyers sometimes arrive from neighboring counties such as Antrim, Otsego, Crawford, Roscommon, Missaukee, Wexford and Grand Traverse, so ask the closing agent early where each party will sign.

What to line up before closing

Pick up the certificate and any tax payoff figure from the county treasurer, and let the register of deeds look over your paperwork. Confirm the treasurer's hours and number before you head over, since schedules change.

Agree with your title company on who pays each of these, so nothing is paid twice:

  • The $30 deed filing charge.
  • The treasurer's certificate, $5 for a short parcel list.
  • Both transfer taxes, which land on the seller.

If the sale includes several parcels, count the descriptions early, because each one past five adds 20 cents to the certificate.

If you sell for cash, the same recording steps apply, but there is no lender's list of title requirements to satisfy. Ask the buyer's closing agent which of the items above they will handle.

Frequently asked questions

What does the Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?

Thirty dollars covers a whole document of any length. A paper assigning or discharging several mortgages adds $3 for each extra instrument number.

Does a Kalkaska County deed need a tax certificate?

It does when the deed has a warranty covenant, and for land contracts and their assignments. The treasurer charges $5.00 an instrument for up to five descriptions.

Who pays Kalkaska County transfer tax?

The seller does. Recording triggers 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state per $500 of price, unless an exemption stated on the deed applies.

Can I pay by card?

Yes. The register of deeds page links a county card payment service and gives a paycode to use. Treat the treasurer's tax certificate fee as a separate payment and ask that office how it takes payment.

What number do I call at the Register of Deeds?

Dial 231-258-3315. The counter is at 605 N. Birch Street in Kalkaska and keeps weekday administration hours.

Where Kent County deeds are recorded

The Register of Deeds is in the county Administration Building at 300 Monroe Avenue NW, in the middle of downtown Grand Rapids. Land contracts, liens and mortgages go through the same counter, under the Michigan Recording Act.

Staff will not supply blank deeds or advise on preparing one. Anyone changing the names on a deed can hire a real property attorney, use a title company or fill in a blank form. The office warns that forms pulled from the internet may fall short of recording rules.

Kent is a big county, with 675,232 people and 275,076 housing units. Owners occupy 70.3% of homes and the median home value is $289,900. Every parcel, from river valley city lots to rolling township acreage, is recorded at this one counter.

Recording fees

The base fee is $30 per document, in place since October 1, 2016. It covers deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and certified copies. These add-ons come up most often when a house changes hands:

  • Assignments or discharges covering several instruments add $3 per extra instrument, and the office asks you to limit these to 25 per document.
  • Deeds with a covenant of warranty, plus land contracts, need the treasurer's certification at $5 per deed (up to 25 parcels, 25 cents each beyond that). Write that check to the Kent County Treasurer, not the Register.
  • Copies are $1 per page. Searches start at $5, and certifying a document adds $5.
  • Pay with cash, a check or a money order. Make the check out to the Kent County Register of Deeds.

Electronic filers pay the statutory recording fee to the county, and an e-recording vendor can add its own processing fee on top.

Transfer tax rates

The county rate is $1.10 and the state rate $7.50 per $1,000 of price, so every $1,000 carries $8.60. They come from Michigan's two transfer tax acts, MCL 207.504 and MCL 207.525.

Kent County transfer tax rates
TaxRate per $1,000 of pricePaid by
County$1.10Seller
State$7.50Seller
Combined$8.60Seller

The statute taxes each $500 or fraction of $500, so an odd price rounds the count up. Michigan has no transfer tax on mortgages.

Getting the deed's tax certification

The certification stamp comes from the Treasurer's Office, a separate counter from the Register of Deeds. It is one of the few transactions the treasurer still takes in person, at the first-floor counter of the Administration Building, weekdays 8 am to 5 pm.

Plan the order of events. A seller who learns at the last minute that taxes are open must first pay the treasurer, then collect the certification, and only after that bring the deed to the recording counter. The county's online delinquent tax search lets you check a parcel before you start, and the payment options page covers e-check, card, phone and mail payments for any balance.

Who owes the tax and how to claim an exemption

The seller, or grantor, owes it. Write the full price into the deed, or attach a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit. The affidavit carries no fee as long as the deed mentions it.

Exemptions must be written on the deed itself. The state's list in MCL 207.526 includes a parent deeding to a child or grandchild, foreclosure deeds, land contracts that have not yet passed title, and court orders that set no price. If land lies in two counties, state the price for each part.

Possible refund of the state tax

Some sellers can recover state transfer tax. The case is a seller who held a principal residence exemption and sold near the property's earlier assessed value. MCL 207.526(u) exempts a conveyance of property that carried the principal residence exemption when the state equalized value is no higher than the value set at the first tax day after the home was built or acquired, and the sale was an arm's-length price.

A refund claim needs the state refund application, copies of the recorded deeds showing the transfer tax stamp and proof of the sales price, and proof of the SEV from the local municipality. Copies of deeds come from the online deed search or from the office itself.

Recording a deed electronically

Approved e-recording vendors can file within a fixed window. Electronic documents are processed on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm, skipping county holidays, and the fee is collected by ACH through the vendors.

The county can reject any electronic filing that fails the Michigan Recording Act, and a party whose documents violate the state standards is cut off until further notice. It works with CSC eRecording, ePN, Simplifile and File and Go, and each vendor sets its own pricing. Recorded documents return to the submitter in electronic form. An individual seller will usually leave this step to the closing office.

Step by step for a seller

First, ask the closing office whether your deed carries a covenant of warranty. If it does, the treasurer's certification comes before anything else. Second, pay any open tax balance. Third, make sure the deed states the full price or has the valuation affidavit attached, and that any exemption is written on it.

Fourth, send the deed in. Most sellers let the title company e-record, but the counter at 300 Monroe Avenue NW takes paper too. Bring a check for $30 payable to the Kent County Register of Deeds, a second check for the treasurer's $5 certification, and the transfer tax. If a cash buyer is on the other side, the same steps apply, and the closing office usually handles them in one visit. Keep the receipt for your records.

Before the deed goes in

Settle the property tax first, because the office cannot take a warranty deed without a treasurer's certificate. Under MCL 211.135 the certificate depends on a clean five-year tax record. Any open balance is settled by closing, and the Kent County Treasurer will quote it.

Check that the names on the deed match the owners of record. If a parcel's owner is unclear, ask Equalization or the local assessor for the tax roll name, which may differ from the true owner, then search recorded documents under it. After recording, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor the transfer notice under MCL 211.27a.

Ordering copies is simple. Visit in person, write a letter, or use the online document search. Copies cost $1 per page, certification is $5 per document, and a records search carries a $5 minimum.

Frequently asked questions

What is the recording fee for a deed in Kent County?

Recording is $30 a document, under a schedule dated October 1, 2016. Budget a further $5 for the treasurer's tax certification on a warranty deed, plus any vendor charge if a filer submits electronically.

How high is the Kent County transfer tax?

It is $8.60 per $1,000 of price in total, split $1.10 county and $7.50 state. The seller owes it unless the deed states an exemption.

Does the Register of Deeds help write a deed?

No. The office does not supply blank deeds or offer advice on preparing them. It sends people to an attorney, a title company or a blank form.

Will Kent County take a warranty deed while taxes are delinquent?

Not a warranty deed. State law requires a treasurer's certificate that taxes for the previous five years are paid. Quitclaim deeds with no warranty covenants are excepted.

How do I order a certified copy?

Visit the office in person, write a letter, or use the online document search. Copies cost $1 per page, certification is $5 per document, and a records search carries a $5 minimum.

Where the Register of Deeds is

The office is in Suite 200 at 800 Tenth Street in Baldwin, the county seat. The clerk and the register of deeds share it, so every deed for Lake County land goes across the same counter.

  • Monday to Thursday: 8:30 am until 5:00 pm
  • Friday: 8:30 am until 4:00 pm
  • Phone (231) 745-2725, fax (231) 745-8632

Equalization has its own suite at the same address, Suite 230, phone (231) 745-2723. It maintains property descriptions and helps with assessment questions.

Lake County for a seller

Lake County is rural, seasonal and low priced. About 567 square miles of land hold an estimated 13,182 residents. The typical owner-occupied home is worth $133,900, and owners occupy 82.0% of homes. Of 13,315 housing units counted in 2020, 61.9% were vacant, and 28.6% of residents are 65 or older.

That vacancy share means many parcels sit empty for long stretches, so an owner selling one may live far from Baldwin. Call the office with the parcel number to learn what it needs before you mail anything.

Paying recording fees

Bring or mail a check, money order or cash to the clerk's office. Recording fees cannot be paid online. The county's web payment page covers copies, vital records and cremation permits, and the register of deeds page carves out recordable land record fees as the exception.

State law sets the amounts. Under MCL 600.2567 the charge is $30 per recorded document however many pages it runs, $1 per copied page, $5 to certify a recording, and a $5 floor on a records search. A discharge or assignment covering extra instruments adds $3 per instrument. A charter county may adopt another schedule, so phone the office to verify the total first.

Transfer tax on a sale

Two layers apply, as elsewhere in Michigan. The county layer is 55 cents per $500 because Lake County has fewer than 2,000,000 residents (MCL 207.504). The state layer is $3.75 per $500 (MCL 207.525).

Lake County transfer tax rates

County55 centsSeller
State$3.75Seller

Because the seller bears the tax, the instrument has to show the full value, or a valuation affidavit has to go with it. Any exemption has to be written on the deed.

Why a deed gets rejected

The clerk's office sends back non-compliant instruments with a checklist, and the checklist cites the Michigan statute for each problem. Most are fixable before you submit.

  • Original ink signatures, with each name printed or typed below, matching the notary block.
  • A street number or post office address for every grantee.
  • The drafter's name and address.
  • One statement of the recordable event on line one of page one, in black ink, 10-point type or larger, over a 2.5 inch blank top margin (half an inch on the other margins).
  • Paper no smaller than letter size and no longer than legal.
  • At most four sequential digits of any Social Security number.
  • An attached English translation for any foreign-language text.

Other triggers include a survivor deed with no recorded death certificate, an uncertified court order, a trust document that is not recorded as its own instrument, and a missing date in the acknowledgment.

Assessment forms and parcel data

The Equalization Department posts them, and it is the first stop for questions that are not about recording. It runs annual sales and appraisal studies on every class of real property and uses them to equalize values across the county's 15 local units of government. State law (MCL 211.34) frames that work around an assessment level of 50% of true cash value.

Its page links to the state forms an owner is most likely to need: the principal residence exemption and homestead form, a request to rescind a PRE, the disabled veteran exemption, and the property transfer affidavit. It also links the Michigan Treasury property tax estimator, which lets you compare millage rates across local units. A seller can use that tool to show a buyer what the tax on the parcel is likely to look like.

Annual apportionment and equalization reports are posted on the same page, with years back to 2015 for apportionment, so a buyer or heir can see how values were adjusted from year to year.

Filing a deed from out of town

Many Lake County owners live elsewhere, so mail filing is common. Call (231) 745-2725 with your parcel number before you send anything, and ask whether the office sees any problem with the deed type you hold. Then confirm the total: $30 for recording, any $3 extras for added instruments, the transfer tax, and a separate certificate fee if the deed carries warranty covenants.

Send original signed paper only, with a check or money order, because fees cannot be paid online. If the office finds a problem, it returns the deed with the checklist, so build in time for a second mailing before your closing date. Keep a copy of everything you send.

Land records fraud alert

The register of deeds runs a fraud alert program that notifies subscribers when land record activity matches their name. Mail your name, email, phone number, mailing address and parcel ID (if known) to Lake County Register of Deeds, Attn: Fraud Alert, 800 10th Street, Suite 200, Baldwin, Michigan 49304.

An owner who lives elsewhere and holds a cabin or vacant land can use the alert as an early warning that someone has recorded a document against the parcel. The same page links to online land record searches, which you can use to review a parcel's recorded deeds before a sale.

Before you record

Deal with taxes first. A deed that carries warranty covenants will not record without the county treasurer's certificate under MCL 211.135, which speaks to liens and the last five years of tax. Request it from the Lake County treasurer well ahead of closing.

Equalization covers the 15 local units and about 27,000 real property parcels, with permanent parcel numbers in use since 1987, so keep the number handy when you phone. After closing, the buyer has 45 days to report the transfer to the local assessing office (MCL 211.27a), and next year's taxable value is reset.

Whether the buyer finances or pays cash, the steps are the same. With a cash buyer there is usually no lender checklist on top of them, which can shorten the time between signing and recording.

The base fee is $30 for each recorded document, and a discharge or assignment that covers extra instruments costs $3 more per instrument. Take payment to the clerk's office as a check, money order or cash, since the online payment page excludes recording fees.

When can I visit the office?

Monday through Thursday it runs 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and on Friday it closes at 4:00 pm. Go to Suite 200, 800 Tenth Street, Baldwin, or call (231) 745-2725.

Who owes transfer tax on a Lake County sale?

The seller. Together the two rates are $4.30 per $500 of value, and a deed gets no exemption unless it says so on its face.

Why would the office return my deed?

Usually for a formatting or signature problem: no original signatures, no drafter name and address, a missing grantee address, the wrong margins or paper size, or no statement of total value. The office sends back a checklist of the reasons with the instrument.

Reaching the Register of Deeds

The office is open to the public on weekdays, opening at eight and closing at half past four. The office page carries a Location Directions link for the street address. Every deed, mortgage and discharge touching Lapeer County land is filed there, and staff promise prompt handling of papers that satisfy the Michigan Recording Act.

Payment can be cash, a check or money order made out to Lapeer County Register of Deeds, or a card used at the counter itself. Title companies and attorneys who file in volume are pointed to Simplifile for electronic submission, and that vendor's help line is 800.460.5657.

A homeowner bringing in a deed should have it signed in dark ink, with each signer's name printed or stamped under the signature, the buyer's street address shown, and the drafter's name and business address on the page.

Recording charges

The flat charge is $30 for each document, however long it runs. A sale adds transfer tax and, for most warranty forms, a tax certificate. The office posts every figure on one fee sheet.

Lapeer County Register of Deeds fees
Fee or taxCharge
Entering and recording one document$30.00
Each additional instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
Treasurer's tax certificate$5.00
County transfer tax$1.10 per thousand dollars
State transfer tax$7.50 per thousand dollars
Copy of a real estate record$1.00 a page
Certifying a document$5.00 each
Fixture filing on the standard form$30.00

Deeds the treasurer must certify first

The fee sheet singles out warranty deeds, land contracts, land contract assignments and any deed containing a covenant of warranty. The County Treasurer has to certify each one ahead of recording.

The certificate costs $5, so allow time for that stop before the recording counter. If your paper is some other kind of instrument, ask the treasurer's office whether it also requires one. If the parcel carries unpaid back taxes, talk with the treasurer about what must be cleared before a certificate is issued.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lapeer County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax for sellers

Combined, the two rates come to $8.60 for every thousand dollars of value, and the seller pays at recording. The instrument must show the full value of the land and buildings, or carry an attached affidavit that gives it. MCL 207.504 writes the county rate as 55 cents per $500 or fraction, which is the same as the $1.10 per thousand on the local sheet.

The Transfer Tax page on the county site links two exemption lists. The county statute, MCL 207.505, excuses several kinds of paper:

  • anything where the money involved is under $100;
  • a mortgage or other security paper, and its later assignment or release;
  • leases, plus land contracts while legal title stays with the seller;
  • a spouse to spouse conveyance that sets up or ends ownership by the entireties;
  • a quitclaim that merely fixes a defect in a title already held;
  • a court order moving title with no dollar amount attached.

After the deed is recorded

Nothing changes on the tax bill automatically. The County Treasurer cannot take a name off a bill, so the new owner or the seller has to carry the deed or other proof of transfer to the assessor in the township, city or village where the property lies.

Until the assessor updates the record, the old name may keep receiving the July 1 and December 1 bills from the local treasurer. A bill that goes unpaid after March 1 moves to the county as delinquent, with the 4% administration fee and interest attached, so buyers and sellers should settle who is watching the mailbox before the closing date. Mortgage lenders sometimes miss a payment, and the owner remains responsible for confirming the bill was paid.

Recording a deed step by step

Start with the deed type. A warranty deed, a land contract or any paper with a covenant of warranty goes to the County Treasurer first for the $5 certification. If taxes are open, settle them before that stop.

Next, check the paper against the formatting list below, and make sure the full value appears on the deed or an affidavit is attached. Write any exemption on the face of the deed. Then bring it to the Register of Deeds with the $30 recording charge and the transfer tax. Most sellers skip all of this and let the title company file, which is the simplest route if a lender or an escrow is involved.

After recording, remind the new owner to take proof of transfer to the local assessor so the next bill carries the right name.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lapeer County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Why a deed gets turned away

A register may not receive a paper that skips the formatting rules in MCL 565.201. The usual causes are small and fixable before you arrive.

  • A printed name that differs from the name in the notary's acknowledgment.
  • Pages with too little white space: the first page needs about two and a half inches clear at the top.
  • Type under 10-point, or ink that is not black on white stock.
  • Full Social Security numbers left visible, when only the last four digits may show.
  • No English translation attached to a foreign-language document.
  • A first line that fails to name the one recordable event the paper evidences.

Once a paper is accepted, the law presumes it complies, and a register cannot reject a conforming instrument because of its content.

Other fees under state law

MCL 600.2567 allows extras that the Lapeer sheet does not itemize. A name search can be billed at fifty cents for each year covered, with a $5 floor, and any other filing or lookup is $1 per paper.

  • $5 of each $30 recording fee is set aside for the county's automation fund.
  • The statute counts a page as one side of a sheet 8.5 inches wide and 11 to 14 inches long.
  • Foreclosure deeds and forfeiture certificates that a treasurer files can be settled after the sale on a delayed schedule instead of at the counter.

Phone the office before a research trip and ask how a search request would be priced.

Protecting yourself from deed fraud

Enroll in the free email alert the office offers. Every filing made in a name you list sends a message, so a forged deed or loan against your house gets noticed early.

The signup is announced at the top of the office page, and a one page form sits on the county website. Sellers should also confirm that the name on their title matches the name they plan to sign, because a mismatch with the acknowledgment is one of the statute's own grounds for refusal.

Lapeer County is more rural than Oakland County next door, and many parcels are farms or lake lots. A seller with an older family property should look up the recorded chain of title early, so any gap or name mismatch is found before a buyer finds it.

What is the filing fee for a deed in Lapeer County?

Thirty dollars per document, however many pages. A warranty deed adds a $5 certificate from the County Treasurer, and the seller owes transfer tax at $1.10 plus $7.50 for every thousand dollars of value.

What are the office hours?

Monday to Friday, opening at eight and closing at half past four. The Location Directions link on the office page gives the street address.

Is a credit card accepted?

Yes, at the counter only. The office also takes cash, checks and money orders, and checks are written to Lapeer County Register of Deeds.

Who covers transfer tax in a Lapeer County sale?

The seller. The deed shows the total value or has a valuation affidavit attached, and the exemptions under MCL 207.505 apply to the county portion.

Can I be warned if someone records a deed in my name?

Yes. The office runs a free email service that alerts you to any filing under a name you enter.

Selling in Leelanau County?

Leelanau County Register of Deeds office

The office is at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, in Suttons Bay. Call 231-256-9682 or email rod@leelanau.gov. Documents received after 4:30 p.m. are held until the next business day, so a deed dropped off late in the afternoon is not recorded until the following morning.

This is the place where every deed, mortgage discharge and similar paper for Leelanau land is filed. Records here go back to 1863. The office records instruments that transfer or encumber real property. It cannot judge whether a document is legally sufficient or what its author intended. Michigan is a race-notice state, so papers are recorded in the order they are first presented, and first in time is first in line.

Leelanau County at a glance

The whole county is the Leelanau Peninsula, a triangle of land that reaches into Lake Michigan from the western Lower Peninsula. Only 347 of its 2,532 square miles are land, because 86% of the area is water, and that shoreline and inland lake frontage shapes much of the housing market. The population was 22,301 at the 2020 census, up from 21,708 in 2010. The villages are Empire, Northport and Suttons Bay, and ten civil townships cover the rest. Every deed for any of this ground is filed in the Suttons Bay office, whether the parcel is a lake cottage, a farm or a village lot.

What makes a deed recordable?

The office accepts only documents with original signatures, and it does not allow digital recording. The wet ink rule is deliberate, because it has stopped fraud attempts. Check these points before you bring a deed in:

  • A court document must be certified by the court. A true copy cannot be recorded, and the same applies to a death certificate.
  • Under MCL 565.201 each signer's name is printed, typed or stamped beneath the signature, and the signature is in black or dark blue ink.
  • The notary's name appears on the same page near the signature.
  • Each grantee's street address, or post office address, appears on a deed.
  • The drafter's name and business address appear on instruments signed after January 1, 1964.

The staff cannot supply forms or give legal help, and they do not run title searches. For drafting, ask an attorney or a title company.

A quick pre-check saves a second trip. Read the deed once more for the notary's name, the grantee's address and the drafter's name, and confirm the ink is black or dark blue. If anything is missing, the signers may need to fix it before the office can accept the paper, and a late fix can push back a closing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Leelanau County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording fees

State law sets recording at $30 for any document, whatever its length. The office takes cash, checks, debit cards and credit cards. One check can cover recording for several documents, along with transfer tax, a tax certificate and any copy fees.

ChargeAmount
Recording any document$30.00
Extra instrument on an assignment or discharge$3.00
Copy, in office or online$1.00 per page
Certified recorded document$5.00
Card convenience fee on $1 to $50$2.00
Card convenience fee above $50.012.95%

For a typical sale, plan on one check that covers the $30 recording fee, the transfer tax and any certified copy you want for your files. Bring the original signed deed, because a scan or photocopy will be turned away. If you pay by card, remember the convenience fee is added on top of the total.

Transfer tax when you sell

Counties of this size levy 55 cents per $500 of value, and the state adds $3.75 per $500. Any leftover fraction counts as a whole $500 unit. The seller pays when the deed is filed, and stamps must be bought in the county that holds the land.

A few rules from the county's own guidance are worth knowing before closing. The deed has to show the total consideration. A Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit may be filed in its place at no charge, provided the deed says so. If land straddles two counties, the price is divided between the parcels and each county is paid its share. An easement is taxable, and a foreclosure instrument carries county tax based on the stated sale price.

Exemptions listed in MCL 207.505 include transfers for under $100, instruments given as security, leases, land contracts that have not yet passed title, spousal conveyances creating a tenancy by the entireties and corrective quitclaims.

How do I search Leelanau County land records?

Use the county's Self Service site, the two public workstations in the Suttons Bay office, or the vault. Enter names last name first with no punctuation. A search needs a grantor or grantee name plus an approximate year.

  • The free search shows index information only, and each image costs $1.00 per page.
  • Subscription passes run $5 for 15 minutes, $15 for a day, $200 a month and $1,100 for six months.
  • A parcel number search requires the county prefix 45 and the dashes, as in 45-000-000-000-00, and only documents that list the number turn up.
  • Online, only deed records are available before January 1, 1972. Older records of other kinds are searched in the office.
  • The historical grantor and grantee indexes went online in October 2025.

Try spelling variants, such as Richard, Rick and Dick, because names are indexed exactly as written on each document.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Leelanau County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

After a payoff, a death or a sheriff's sale

The office only records. It issues no replacement deed after any of these events, and your original deed stays the deed to the property.

  • After a mortgage payoff, the lender sends a discharge or satisfaction of mortgage. No new deed follows, because the deed was delivered when you bought.
  • When a co-owner dies, bring a certified death certificate and the recording fee. It shows that the deceased person no longer holds an interest.
  • A sheriff's deed is recorded when it is submitted after the auction closes. To redeem, contact the attorney named on the sheriff's deed.
  • If you have lost your deed, a recorded copy is available at the office, and copy fees apply.

If you are selling and one of these items is unfinished, get it recorded first. A buyer's title company will look for the discharge or the death certificate in the county index before it lets the sale close.

Watching for property fraud

Subscribe to Fraud Notify, which costs nothing. It sends an email whenever a filing appears under a name you register, and the office has stopped several fraudulent attempts to list owners' property once owners were told.

If you see a neighbor's lot offered for sale, ask the owner. Also be wary of mail that looks official and charges for copies of your own deed. A 2016 Michigan law set rules for such mailings, and a copy from the office is $1.00 a page.

Frequently asked questions

What is the phone number for the Leelanau County Register of Deeds?

231-256-9682. The office is in Suttons Bay at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, and also takes questions by email at rod@leelanau.gov.

Does Leelanau County record deeds electronically?

No. The office requires original wet ink signatures and does not allow digital recording, to make deed fraud harder.

How much is transfer tax on a Leelanau County sale?

The county rate is 55 cents per $500 of value and the state rate is $3.75 per $500. The seller pays when the deed is recorded.

Will the office record a copy of a death certificate?

Only a certified one. A true copy cannot be recorded, and the office issues no new deed afterward because it only records.

Where can I get a copy of my Leelanau County deed?

Go to the Suttons Bay office, call 231-256-9682 or use the Self Service website. Each page costs $1.00.

What the Lenawee County Register of Deeds does

The Register of Deeds in Adrian, the county seat, receives, records and digitally stores every legal document that affects real estate in Lenawee County. That covers deeds, land contracts, mortgages, liens, surveys and land corners. Staff check each item against Michigan's recording rules, record it, and send the original back by U.S. mail to whoever presented it unless instructed otherwise.

Whether a house stands near Adrian, in Tecumseh or on a farm road in a rural township, the deed goes to this one county office. Michigan leaves assessing, zoning and building rules to individual cities and townships, and keeps deed recording with the county. The legal description in the deed gives the exact boundaries. The county had 43,577 housing units at the 2020 census, and 77.3 percent of occupied homes were lived in by their owners.

The office supplies no forms, and its employees are barred from advising on or helping complete a document. Content and intent are the preparer's responsibility, so closings usually run through a title agent or a lawyer.

If you are preparing to sell, call the office with your parcel's legal description and ask what is of record. Staff can tell you whether the vesting deed, a mortgage or a lien shows up, though they cannot interpret what it means for your sale. That answer helps your title agent plan the closing, and it costs nothing to ask.

Recording fees and copy costs

Recording runs $30.00 per document, whether it is one page or twenty. A page copy at the counter is $1.00. The counter takes checks, cash and cards, and cards carry an access fee.

Charges at the Lenawee County Register of Deeds
ServiceCharge
Recording a document$30.00 flat
Counter copy$1.00 per page
Escrow account to view and print online$100.00 to open
Deed copy direct from the officeAs little as $2.00

Owners sometimes receive letters from commercial services offering certified copies of their deeds by mail for as much as $83.00 each. The identical record is available from the county's own counter for as little as $2.00. Call the office before paying a mailer.

Why deeds get rejected

The county posts 17 statutory requirements and treats them as a minimum, since some instruments carry extra rules. These are the ones that most often matter on a home sale:

  • Signatures must be original, with names typed or printed beneath, and those names must agree with the notary block (MCL 565.201).
  • Page one needs a 2.5 inch blank band across its upper edge, and all remaining edges need half an inch.
  • Use black ink in at least 10-point type on white 20-pound paper that is at least letter size and no longer than legal.
  • The first printed line has to state the recordable event, and one instrument may evidence only one event.
  • Include the grantee's street or post office address, plus drafter identification with a name and address.
  • A Michigan-signed deed needs acknowledgment by a judge, a court clerk or a notary public.
  • Social Security numbers may appear only as the final four digits.

A deed that says "survivor" must be backed by a certified death certificate that is recorded with it or already of record and cited by liber and page. A court order must carry the court clerk's certification and seal.

A rejected document is mailed back, and the closing waits until a corrected one is presented. Because the title agent normally handles this, ask early whether the deed has been checked against the list above, and read the notary block yourself before signing day.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lenawee County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax on a house sale

On nearly every sale for money, tax is owed. Michigan's state transfer tax attaches to deeds given for consideration. Under MCL 207.523, the seller is the liable party, and the money is paid to the county treasurer for the parcel's location. A separate county transfer tax comes from Act 134 of 1966. Phone the Register of Deeds for the combined figure on your price. Closing agents ordinarily subtract it from the seller's proceeds.

The statutes also list transfers that escape the tax. A few that touch homeowners:

  • Deeds with consideration under $100.
  • Gifts of a home by an individual to a child or grandchild (state exemption, MCL 207.526).
  • Court orders that move title without naming a price.
  • Corrective quitclaim deeds that only fix a defect in title.
  • Land contracts, until legal title actually passes.
  • Mortgage foreclosures and the deeds that replace them.

Any exemption you claim must be cited correctly in the deed itself, so run the citation past your closing agent.

Searching land records in Adrian and around the county

The county offers an online search with two doors. A text search reads typed or legible text and works on a phone. A second tool serves experienced users and searches by name, recorded date, and liber and page. It runs best on a computer in Chrome or Edge with pop-ups allowed. Results are for information, and document images must be purchased.

Sellers can use the name search to see what stands against the property before listing: the vesting deed, open mortgages, an old lien that was paid but never discharged, or a death certificate that was never recorded. A buyer's title agent runs the same search, so a problem found early costs less time.

Anyone worried about deed fraud can enroll in the free property fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com or by phone at 1-800-728-3858. It sends a notice whenever a document carrying the owner's name is recorded.

Where recording fits in a sale

It comes last. At closing the title agent collects the signed, notarized deed, pays the recording fee and any transfer tax, and sends the package to the county. Until the deed is recorded and indexed, the sale is not visible in the public record.

Property tax enters the same week. The year after a transfer, the new owner's taxable value is uncapped, and the buyer files a property transfer affidavit with the local assessor. Challenging an assessment starts at the March Board of Review in your city or township and can continue to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. Owners who need more time on summer taxes are sent by the county treasurer's page to the state's deferment rules.

A house with deferred repairs, back taxes or an estate behind it can sell for cash with no lender repair list. The recording steps are identical in every case, and the $30.00 fee is the same for a one-page quitclaim as for a long deed with exhibits. After the office indexes the instrument, ask your closing agent for the recorded deed and its recording details.

Frequently asked questions

How much is recording in Lenawee County?

$30.00 per document, whatever the page count. Transfer tax is a separate charge that depends on the sale price.

Can Lenawee County staff draft my deed?

No. Staff do not provide forms and cannot advise on or complete a document for you. Hire a title agent or attorney to draft it.

Who pays Lenawee County transfer tax?

The seller, under MCL 207.523, with payment due to the county treasurer for the property's location. Settlement statements normally show it as a seller charge.

What is the cheapest way to get a deed copy?

Ask the county office itself. A counter copy is $1.00 per page, and a deed can run as little as $2.00, versus as much as $83.00 from commercial mailers.

Why would a Lenawee County deed be rejected?

Typical causes are photocopied signatures, narrow margins, a missing drafter address, names that differ from the notary block, or type that is too small. Compare the document against the county's 17-point list.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Livingston County Register of Deeds office

The office sits in the Historical Courthouse at 200 E Grand River Ave, Howell, the county seat. Call (517) 546-0270. The counter opens weekdays at 8:00 a.m. and shuts at 4:30 p.m., with county holidays off.

Most documents never reach the counter. Title companies and attorneys send them electronically through four certified vendors: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. A few instruments cannot go that way, including deeds that come with valuation affidavits, plats, and master deeds with large drawings. Those must be brought in or mailed on paper.

The county had a 2020 population of 193,866, and roughly 86 percent of occupied homes belong to their residents, which keeps deeds flowing through this office steadily. Sellers in the rural townships record at the same counter as sellers in Howell. Legal descriptions on a Livingston deed read as a section number plus a starting corner.

Recording fees

Every recording carries a flat $30.00 charge, and $4 of it is sent to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation fund. If one instrument assigns or discharges several earlier records, each reference past the first adds $3.

Livingston County Register of Deeds fee schedule
ServiceFee
Recording a document$30.00 flat
Each extra liber and page cross-reference$3.00
Tax certification, first 25 parcel numbers$5.00, then $0.20 per added number
Fixture filing$30 per document
Copy of a recorded page$1.00 ($2.00 for plat or condo drawings)
Certifying a copy$5.00, all pages must be bought
Tract index use, unless it is your own property$10 per hour

Recording fees and transfer tax are never put on a charge account. Pay with cash, check or card; a card adds a service fee.

How the office calculates transfer tax

If a deed states a price, the office takes transfer tax the moment it records. The total is .086 of the amount, meaning $8.60 per $1,000: $1.10 per $1,000 to the county and $7.50 per $1,000 to the state. The grantor normally bears it. Before the math, the price rounds up to the next $500 step. Land that straddles two counties needs the price divided by county on the deed itself.

Exemptions exist. A deed may be exempt from the state share alone or from both shares, never from the county share by itself, and the exemption cited must fit the facts on the page. Mistakes the office sees:

  • Claiming the family-gift exemptions when a trust is the grantor; an individual has to be the grantor.
  • Assuming a church is automatically exempt.
  • Assuming a sheriff's deed escapes county tax. It is always exempt from the state portion, but exempt from the county portion only when the mortgage is federally backed.
  • Citing the under-$100 exemption while the deed shows a $5,000 price.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Livingston County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Tax certification

A tax certification is a Treasurer's sticker showing that taxes are paid up and that the legal description matches the township tax roll. It is part of what makes a warranty deed a warranty deed. The county requires it before recording warranty deeds, any deed with "warrant" in the conveyance line, land contracts, assignments of land contract (except those given as collateral), master deeds, and master deed amendments that add property to a condominium.

For a mailed document, enclose the $5.00 and the office gets the certification for you. An e-recorded document that needs one goes through the document router so both departments receive it. A seller with unpaid taxes learns of it at this stage at the latest, so pay off any balance before the deed goes in.

Copies, searches and corrections

Searching the index by name is free online. Viewing a page costs $1 plus a convenience fee that covers card processing, and a link arrives immediately. Certified copies, death certificates, tax liens, condo master deeds and documents over 75 pages are mailed after purchase. Records are imaged and indexed back to November 7, 1980 (liber 1000), with earlier books imaged or kept in hard copy.

  • You cannot change a signed, notarized or recorded deed. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed signed by the current owners.
  • When a joint tenant or spouse dies, recording the death certificate shows the survivor as sole owner without a new deed.
  • An enhanced life estate (ladybird) deed becomes proof of ownership once both death certificates are recorded.
  • Paying off a mortgage produces a discharge, not a new deed.
  • A rejected document comes back with a letter listing the reasons, and it can be corrected and resubmitted.

Paper filings by mail or at the counter must come with a return envelope or $3 for postage. Giving an email address instead brings the recorded copy back at no charge, usually the same day.

Can the office tell me when my house was built?

No. Deeds describe land and a legal description and rarely say whether a building stood on it, so ask the city or township assessor. The Howell Carnegie Library reference desk, at (517) 546-0720, can search its archives, and the county Plat Books for 1875, 1895 and 1915 show homesteads and, in 1875, the houses in the towns.

Staff suggest one rough method for older homes: a deed whose price is far below a mortgage recorded the same day often marks an owner who was about to build. Name indexes go back to the first recorded documents in 1836 and 1837. For a sale, a seller who wants proof of a renovation or a permit should ask the local building department instead.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Livingston County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What a seller should verify before closing

Have the closing agent pull the recorded chain: vesting deed, recorded death certificate if any, mortgage discharges and liens. The Register of Deeds cannot verify ownership, since unrecorded land contracts or deeds can affect it, and its staff do not run title searches or give a guarantee. Title companies do that work and can also check probate court records the recorder lacks.

The buyer owes the local assessor a property transfer affidavit within 45 days or faces $5 a day in fines, up to $200, and the home's taxable value is uncapped the next year. A seller who knows the taxes will jump for the buyer can say so up front, because it affects what the buyer can afford.

Back taxes, estate paperwork and repair needs are the usual reasons owners ask for a cash sale. Recording works the same whoever the buyer is.

On closing day, bring government ID and your copy of the settlement figures. Once the deed is recorded, the new owner's name appears in the county index, and the buyer's transfer affidavit follows.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Livingston County recording fee?

The flat fee is $30.00 per document, including $4 for the state survey and remonumentation fund. Extra cross-references cost $3 each, and transfer tax is separate.

Who bears transfer tax here?

Usually the seller, who is the grantor. It is collected at recording: $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, using a price rounded up to a $500 step.

Can I record a photocopy of a deed?

No. Only documents with original signatures can be recorded, and even electronic services must scan originals. Court orders, death certificates and surveys must be certified versions.

How do I put a family member on my deed?

The current owners must sign a new deed conveying the property to everyone who should hold title. A signed or recorded deed cannot be altered, and a lawyer or title agent can draft the new one.

Does the office run title searches?

No. The office does not do title searches or furnish abstracts and cannot guarantee results. Title companies perform and insure searches, while the office teaches the public how to use its index.

The County Treasurer is one floor up (second floor, Room 30, phone (906) 643-7318), and the Equalization Department sits in the Courthouse Annex, Room 120, at (906) 643-7310. A seller who needs a deed filed, a tax certificate and a parcel record can finish all three errands in one courthouse complex.

Mackinac County is spread across the Straits of Mackinac, with 1,079 of its 2,101 square miles in the lake and 10,834 residents at the 2020 census. St. Ignace is the seat and Mackinac Island is the other city. Owners who live far from the courthouse should use the mail or e-recording options below.

Can a deed be sent by mail or e-recording?

Yes to both. Nobody has to appear in person, and documents with the right fee can go by mail, UPS or FedEx. Electronic filers can route through CSC E-Recording Solutions, Simplifile or EPN E Recording Partners Network, each with its own price list.

Staff offer a service most counties skip: they will look over a draft before you submit it. The office cannot write a private legal document or advise you, but it will check a draft against the recording rules. That can save a round trip across the Straits. A few handy points:

  • Include a self-addressed return envelope so the original comes back sooner.
  • In a deed the grantor is the seller and the grantee is the buyer.
  • Copy the legal description from the prior deed or a new survey, and avoid the shortened version printed on a tax statement unless someone has verified it.
  • Blanket assignments and blanket releases are accepted.
  • Forms are sold at office supply stores or available online, and a local title company may supply one.

Before you send anything, call (906) 643-7306 to confirm the total. Put the deed, the fee check and the return envelope in one package, and keep a note of the date you mailed it so you can follow up if the recorded copy is slow to come back.

Recording fees

One flat charge covers a document of any length. Under MCL 600.2567 that is $30.00, in force since October 1, 2016, and $4 of it goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund. A deed with a warranty clause also needs a treasurer's certificate for $5.00, and the register suggests a single $35.00 check. If you mail the deed, its staff pick up the certificate for you.

Mackinac County Register of Deeds charges
What you are buyingPrice
Filing a deed, mortgage or other instrument$30.00
Each extra instrument released in one document$3.00
Tax certificate for a warranty clause$5.00
Certifying a copy$5.00
Plain copy$1.00 a page
Name search$0.50 a year searched, $5.00 floor
State or federal tax lien search$3.00 a name

A certified copy must reproduce the whole document. Michigan's registers of deeds pushed in 2016 to stop private companies from selling deeds to residents at inflated prices, so compare any mailer against the office's own rate above.

Transfer tax for a Mackinac County seller

Seller-side transfer tax runs $4.30 for every $500 of price, rounded up for any leftover amount. That is the county's 55 cents (MCL 207.504) plus the state's $3.75. The statute puts the burden on the grantor.

The deed must state the full price on its face, or a valuation affidavit goes with it at no filing charge, and the deed must say the affidavit is attached. Tax stamps are bought where the land sits, and land in two counties needs a stated split.

Exemptions appear on the register's county and state exemption pages and in MCL 207.526. Gifts to children and grandchildren, foreclosure transfers and court-ordered transfers are among them. An exemption has to be written on the face of the deed, so settle it with your closing agent before signing.

Ask your closing agent to show the transfer tax line on the settlement statement ahead of time. It is a seller cost, so it comes out of your proceeds at the table, and it is paid when the deed is filed.

If the house is behind on a mortgage or taxes

Mackinac County's register and treasurer jointly run a foreclosure prevention page, and it explains a ranking that surprises many owners: a tax foreclosure takes precedence over a mortgage foreclosure. Once a mortgage foreclosure starts, the owner keeps control of the property for 6 months, or 12 months if the parcel is larger than 3 acres, and can refinance or sell during that time.

The page also offers a set of practical steps:

  • Call the lender early and read every letter it sends.
  • Look for a HUD-approved housing counselor, since counseling is free or low cost.
  • Contact the Michigan State Housing Development Authority about its Save the Dream program.
  • Do not pay a company that promises to stop a foreclosure, and never sign a paper that appoints someone to act for you.

On the tax side, the County Treasurer collects delinquent property taxes for the local units and handles the summer auction of foreclosed properties under Public Act 123. The Equalization Department hosts a property and delinquent tax search and a list of each local unit's assessor and treasurer. A sale that pays off the balance before the redemption window ends is one way out.

What a recorded deed changes for property tax

The register notifies the assessor of recorded transfers each month, and the new owner must also file with the local assessor within 45 days under MCL 211.27a. A transfer of ownership resets the following year's taxable value to the state equalized value. Moves to a spouse, and residential moves to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild with no commercial use, do not count.

A rental of fewer than 15 days in a year counts as non-commercial, which matters for a cottage that sees a few weekend guests. Longer rentals fall outside that carve-out. Ask the assessor for the parcel's current taxable value before you list.

The register also processes passport applications Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., which helps a relocating seller who needs travel documents at the same visit.

Keep the recorded deed with your closing papers. If a buyer later files the transfer notice late, the assessor may contact the new owner first, but your own records show when title passed.

Frequently asked questions

Is it $30 or $35 to file a deed in Mackinac County?

It is $35.00 when the deed contains a warranty clause, made up of the $30.00 filing fee and the $5.00 treasurer's certificate, and $30.00 when it does not. Each extra instrument released in one document adds $3.00.

Who writes the deed for a Mackinac County sale?

A title company or attorney should draft it. Register staff cannot draft private legal documents, though they will review a draft for compliance with the recording rules before you submit it.

What is the combined transfer tax rate for a Mackinac County home?

The combined rate is $4.30 per $500 of price or fraction, made up of 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state. The grantor pays it.

Who runs the foreclosure auction in Mackinac County?

The County Treasurer, at 100 S. Marley, Room 30, handles the summer auction of foreclosed properties. Call (906) 643-7318, or use the property and delinquent tax search on the Equalization Department page.

How long can an owner stay after a Mackinac County mortgage foreclosure begins?

Six months, or twelve months if the parcel has more than 3 acres. During that window the owner can refinance or sell.

Macomb County Register of Deeds office

The register works inside the county Clerk's office at 120 N. Main St. in Mount Clemens, MI 48043, staffed on weekdays until 4:15 p.m. after an 8 a.m. start. The phone is 586-469-7953 and the email is registerofdeeds@macombgov.org. An online booking tool lets you reserve a visit, and the same page links a land records search, a status page for documents already submitted, and a mail-in request for certified copies.

With 881,217 residents at the 2020 census and 27 cities, townships and villages, the office handles a high volume of parcels, and return times stretch. Expect recorded documents back roughly 6 to 8 weeks after the recording date, so put a correct RETURN TO name and address on page one.

Before a sale, check the status page to confirm that your earlier recordings, such as a mortgage discharge, actually posted. An unrecorded discharge is a common reason a title company asks for extra paperwork.

Deed, search and copy costs

Flat pricing applies: $30 for a deed, mortgage, lis pendens or certified court paper, whatever its page count. A document that releases several instruments adds $3 each after the first. Of each fee, $4 goes to the state survey fund, with exceptions for fixture filings, liens, state deeds, plats and tax reversion papers.

Searches and copies are priced separately, and the schedule includes oddities such as large-format plats and Uniform Commercial Code filings. Plat copies run $3.50 at 11 by 17 inches and $4.50 at 18 by 24, with $2.50 postage if mailed. Fixture filings and UCC terminations are $30 each, the same as a deed. A UCC search is $12 per debtor name, made up of $6 for the name search and $3 each for state and federal tax lien certificates, and a copy of a UCC filing is $2 a page. Personal property financing statements filed after July 1, 2001 go to the state UCC office and are not part of the register's searches, so the register's results cover fixture filings and similar land-based items.

Macomb County Register of Deeds charges
ServiceCharge
Record a deed or mortgage$30
Release or assign extra instruments$3 each after the first
Real estate search, mail or in person$5 minimum
Copy of a real estate record$1 a page
Certified copy$5 a record
UCC search$12 per debtor
Plat copy, 11 by 17$3.50

Which deeds need a treasurer's certificate?

Anything carrying a warranty clause. Warranty deeds, deeds with a covenant clause, land contracts and assignments of land contract need certification from the County Treasurer before recording. Since July 1, 2015 the certificate costs $5 for up to five legal descriptions and $0.20 for each extra description. The authority is MCL 211.135.

The Treasurer, at 586-469-5190, confirms that tax is paid up for the five years before the deed date. The Land File office at 586-469-5313 supplies legal descriptions, and the same number plus the local assessor are free sources for a taxpayer's name and address. Questions on transfer tax go to 586-469-5309.

Quitclaim deeds without a warranty covenant skip the certificate. Macomb also posts its own quitclaim form on the register's page, along with a construction lien claim form and a sheriff's deed payoff request. These forms come with no promise about their legal effect.

First-page margins and other recording rules

A first page needs a 2.5 inch top margin and a half inch on all other sides. If it falls short, attach a cover page that states the document's title. This matters for older deeds that crowd the top edge.

The county stresses a few other points:

  • Names typed or stamped under original signatures must match the notary's acknowledgment.
  • A deed must show each grantee's address and the drafter's name and address.
  • Instruments signed before April 16, 2017 had to state the marital status of male grantors.
  • Court orders are recorded only if certified and sealed by the court clerk.
  • A death certificate cannot be attached to another document since September 18, 2018.

Statutory sources are in MCL 565.201, and the county offers a link to common document problems.

Changing who is on a deed

To add a person, record a quit claim deed, typed or in black ink, signed and notarized. The cost is $30. An attorney can advise if the goal is to avoid probate. To drop a deceased owner, record a certified copy of the death certificate for $30. The survivorship wording on the deed decides whether probate is still needed.

A paid-off mortgage does not produce a new deed. The lender sends a discharge, release or satisfaction of mortgage for recording, and the deed you received at purchase stays your title. Lost your copy? A recorded copy is just as good as the original, and you can ask in person, by mail or through the online search.

After any ownership change, the new owner must report it to the local assessor within 45 days. MCL 211.27a treats most deed transfers as a trigger to reset taxable value, with carve-outs for spouses and for residential transfers among close family.

Payoff letters after a sheriff's sale

Someone entitled to redeem after a sheriff's sale can ask the register for a payoff letter for $25, paid with the request form. It is ready after 2 business days, and the form can be mailed or dropped off. The state statute behind it is MCL 600.3240, which lets registers in counties of 750,000 to 1,500,000 people determine the amount using only recorded affidavits, and it frees the county of liability for an incorrect figure.

Redemption itself follows a short checklist:

  • Pay by certified or cashier's check, delivered by 4 p.m. on the last working day of the redemption period.
  • Expect a $5 care and custody fee, already included in a figure from the register.
  • Receive the office's letter confirming that funds arrived.
  • Leave the redemption certificate to the sheriff's deed holder, who drafts and records it.

The register also offers a Fraud Notify alerts system. Owners who sign up are warned when a document is recorded under their names, a safeguard worth having when a house is vacant or being sold.
