Transfer tax on a sale

The county rate is 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state adds $3.75 per $500. The seller owes it when the deed is recorded unless an exemption applies. Call 586-469-5309 for details, and have your closing agent confirm the amount before the settlement statement is final.

Plan the payment for the day the deed is filed, since the seller's share comes out of closing proceeds. If you think an exemption applies, tell the closing agent early so the right wording goes on the deed.

Frequently asked questions

What is the recording charge at the Mount Clemens register of deeds?

It is $30 per document regardless of length. A warranty deed adds the $5 treasurer certificate for up to five legal descriptions, and extra descriptions are $0.20 each.

How soon do recorded Macomb County deeds come back?

Roughly 6 to 8 weeks from the recording date. A correct RETURN TO name and address on the document helps it reach the right person.

Where can I see whether a Macomb County document has been recorded?

Use the status of recorded documents page on the register's site, or call 586-469-7953. The land records search lets you request copies, and search and copy fees apply.

What does Macomb County charge in transfer tax?

The county rate is 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state adds $3.75 per $500. Call 586-469-5309 for details.

Can I mail a deed to the Macomb County register?

Yes. A completed quit claim deed can be mailed in or brought in for recording, and certified copy requests are accepted through the U.S. Mail.

Manistee County Register of Deeds office

The register works from the county courthouse at 415 Third Street, Manistee, MI 49660, and the phone is 231-723-2146. Weekday hours split around lunch: morning window 8:30 to noon, afternoon window 1 to 4. The Treasurer (231-723-3173) and Equalization Department (231-723-5957) share the street address and stay open until 5, so a seller can collect a deed certification and a parcel record in a single trip.

Manistee County had 25,032 residents at the 2020 census, and about 738 of its 1,281 square miles are Lake Michigan water, so shoreline and lake property drive much of the market. Manistee is the only city and the seat.

Staff keep the records but will not run title for anyone. The office makes simple searches that reach back 20 years and sends anyone needing a full title search to a title company. A document handed in goes through a seven step recordation process, which usually takes one to two business days.

Recording by mail or e-recording

You do not have to come to the courthouse. Mailing completed documents to Register of Deeds, 415 3rd Street, Manistee, MI 49660 is acceptable and legal in almost every situation. Call 231-723-2146 first if you want the cost confirmed. The office accepts every form of payment, and it returns copies to other parties once copy fees are paid and an addressed, stamped envelope is supplied.

Manistee's business rules for electronic filers are:

  • Documents are handled between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. on weekdays, holidays excepted.
  • Payment goes through ACH, under each vendor's agreement.
  • A vendor that submits documents breaking the Michigan eRecording Standards can lose submission access.
  • The register may reject an electronic document that fails the recording act.
  • Changes to these rules are posted 90 days before they take effect.

The vendors may charge their own processing fees, but the register itself collects only the fees written into law.

Recording and copy fees

The flat recording charge is $30, with a $3 extra for each additional instrument released in one document. Copy pricing has its own shape here: $7 buys a two page real estate record copy and each added page is $1. The office requires payment before it releases anything.

Manistee County recording, copy and search charges
ServiceCharge
Recording, any length$30
Record copy, first two pages$7
Added pages or extra copies$1 a page

Online access is a pay for view site covering 1978 forward, and a separate search tool covers 1856 through 1991. The vault is open to the public for those who prefer to dig through the books.

When you order copies, bring a list of the instruments you need. Budget for the certification fee if a title company or lender wants a certified version, and ask the office to confirm the total before you pay, since payment comes first.

Why a warranty deed goes to the Treasurer first

Manistee's routing is unusual. You hand a warranty deed, a land contract, an assignment with a warranty clause or a condominium master deed to the County Treasurer for certification, and the Treasurer forwards it to the register with the fees. The register sends nothing back to the Treasurer, and an uncertified instrument is returned to whoever sent it. The legal basis is MCL 211.135, and the certificate costs $5.

The Treasurer's office also keeps tax histories on real property, handles Principal Residence Exemption audits, and bills or refunds for board of review changes. That makes it the right stop for a payoff question. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenant needs no certificate.

Each year, summer bills go out July 1. City summer taxes are due August 20, township and village summer taxes September 14, and winter taxes February 14. Unpaid township and city taxes move to the County Treasurer on March 1 with a 4% fee and 1% monthly interest, and foreclosure follows about three years after the tax year.

For a sale, give the title company the parcel details early and ask them to send the warranty deed to the Treasurer rather than straight to the register. That one routing step avoids a returned document and a delay at closing.

How a tax foreclosure plays out

After forfeiture on March 1 of the second year, the county's timeline stacks on several charges:

  • $175 for the title search, $60 for recording and $7.10 for notice.
  • Interest at 1.5% a month, applied back to the prior year.
  • $45 for a site inspection in June.
  • $50 for publication in December.

Notice runs in the Manistee News Advocate twice in January, and the Treasurer holds a show cause hearing. The circuit court enters judgment in February. Taxes can be paid through March 31 of the third year, and foreclosure becomes final the next day.

Tax-foreclosed property in the county goes to an online auction run by a contractor, Title Check, LLC. The auction happens once a year, typically in August or September. It opens with a minimum bid round, then a re-offer round with sealed bids, then a no reserve round with sealed bids about a month apart.

A former owner can file a Notice of Intention to Claim Interest in Foreclosure Sales Proceeds (Form 5743), due July 1 in the foreclosure year, and later a court motion to claim remaining proceeds. A seller with unpaid taxes should settle them before forfeiture, while a normal sale is still possible.

Property tax and transfer tax after a sale

The Equalization Department keeps the tax rolls up to date for transfers, principal residence and agricultural exemptions, and uncapping. It sets no individual assessment, since its role is to survey classes of property across the city and townships. Under MCL 211.27a, a transfer of ownership lifts taxable value to the state equalized value for the following year, so a buyer's first bill can exceed what the seller paid. The buyer reports the transfer to the local assessor within 45 days.

Transfer tax is separate and falls on the seller. The rate is $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, with a $100 floor. Check the legislature's exemption lists for transfers that owe nothing, such as family transfers of the kinds those lists cover.

Confirm the exemption wording with your title company before the deed is signed, since an exemption has to be claimed on the document.

Frequently asked questions

What is the total cost to file a warranty deed in Manistee County?

Plan on $35, which is the $30 recording charge plus the $5 treasurer certification. A document that releases several instruments adds $3 for each one after the first.

When is the Manistee County register office closed during the day?

The lunch hour, noon to 1 p.m., is the gap. Doors are open for the morning and afternoon windows, weekdays only.

Can Manistee County staff run a title for my house?

Staff can do simple searches back 20 years, but they will not run a full title. For that you need a title company, and the office cannot give legal advice.

How is the Manistee County tax auction run?

It is online and held once a year, usually in August or September, through Title Check, LLC. It has a minimum bid round followed by re-offer and no reserve rounds.

What transfer tax applies to a Manistee County sale?

The county charges $0.55 per $500 and the state charges $3.75 per $500. The seller owes it unless the deed is exempt.

Where to take a deed

Deeds go to the Register of Deeds at 234 W. Baraga Avenue, Marquette, MI 49855. The counter phone is (906) 225-8415, and weekday hours are 8 to 5. Documents sent through an e-recording vendor can be submitted around the clock, though staff work them between 8 and 4.

Michigan follows a race-notice rule, so the buyer who records first outranks a later claimant. Documents are processed in the order they arrive, which is why closings tend to record on funding day.

Three desks at the courthouse touch most house sales here:

  • The Register of Deeds, for the deed itself, mortgage releases and copies
  • The County Treasurer, at (906) 225-8425, for tax history and delinquent real property bills
  • Equalization and Tax Roll, at (906) 225-8405, for ownership records and parcel maps

Selling a home in Marquette County

Marquette County is large and thinly settled, with Lake Superior along its north edge. The cities are Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee, and Northern Michigan University sits in the county seat. The county had 66,017 residents in April 2020 and an estimated 68,064 by July 2025, making it the most populous county in the Upper Peninsula.

Owners value a typical house at $216,500, and 69.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Typical gross rent is $949 a month. Parcels near the range towns can have long chains of ownership, so ask your title company how far back it will search.

Townships and cities

Twenty-two local units assess property inside the county. Assessing, bills and zoning questions start with the unit where the parcel sits, not with the Baraga Avenue offices.

  • Cities: Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee
  • Townships, A to M: Champion, Chocolay, Ely, Ewing, Forsyth, Humboldt, Ishpeming, Marquette and Michigamme
  • Townships, N to W: Negaunee, Powell, Republic, Richmond, Sands, Skandia, Tilden, Turin, Wells and West Branch

Winters are cold here, so allow for weather when you schedule a showing or an inspection.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Marquette County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What a deed filing costs

Page count does not matter: one deed is $30.00 whether it runs two pages or twenty. The state remonumentation charge and the register's automation charge are built into that amount, so the window adds nothing else for the recording.

Charges at the Marquette County recording counter
ServiceAmount
File a deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
Each extra instrument released within one paper$3.00
Treasurer's certificate attached to a warranty deed$5.00
Certified copy stamp$5.00

Transfer tax is separate and applies to any taxable deed. You can pay at the counter by cash, check or card, with a processing charge on cards.

Transfer tax on a sale

The grantor, whoever signs the property over, pays the tax. The deed must state the total consideration. If the price is kept off the deed, a valuation affidavit fills the gap, and the office files it free as long as the deed notes that one exists.

Under MCL 207.525 the state portion is $3.75 for each $500 step of the price, with any remainder counted as another step. Call the office for the county's per-step amount before you finalize a net sheet.

MCL 207.526 exempts some deeds if the grantor says so in the text. Sellers lean on these most:

  • Consideration below $100
  • A deed from an individual to a child or grandchild
  • Transfers following foreclosure, or a deed given to avoid it
  • A land contract that has not yet delivered legal title
  • A corrective quitclaim that only repairs a title flaw

Why a deed gets sent back

Usually the cause is a defect under MCL 565.201. Staff cannot prepare a deed or give legal advice, and only original signatures are recorded, which rules out faxes and photocopies. A "true copy" of a court order is also refused, since the court itself must certify it.

Defects that get a deed returned:

  • Signer names printed under the signatures that disagree with the notary block
  • No mailing address for the buyer, or no name and address for whoever prepared the deed
  • Ink that is not black or dark blue, or type under 10 point
  • Less than 2 1/2 inches of clear space at the top of page one
  • An opening line that names more than one recordable event
  • Full Social Security numbers left on the page

Anything not in English needs an English translation attached.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Marquette County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Treasurer's tax certificate

For warranty deeds and land contracts, the treasurer must vouch that the parcel's taxes were paid in each of the five years before the deed (MCL 211.135). Plain quitclaims escape the rule. The treasurer works from the Courthouse Annex, weekdays 8 to 5, at (906) 225-8425.

On March 1 each year the townships and cities pass their unpaid real property bills up to the county treasurer, who then collects them. Debit and credit cards are taken on those delinquent accounts. An owner who is behind can pay before asking for the certificate, or have the title company settle the balance from sale proceeds.

The office also issues tax histories, handy when a buyer wants to see past billing on a parcel.

Searching and filing records online

Online, the index and images start with deeds dated January 1, 1980 and with mortgages and miscellaneous papers dated January 1, 1983. Earlier books can be read only at the office.

E-recording runs through CSC, ePN, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile. Some document types cannot go this way, so title companies check with their vendor first, and any rejection is returned electronically.

Beware outside companies charging $50 or more for a certified deed copy that the county sells for as little as $1 a page. Owners may also enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert service.

What happens to your tax bill after closing

Recording the deed sets off a taxable value reset. MCL 211.27a gives the buyer 45 days to report the transfer to the local assessor, and the following year's taxable value becomes the state equalized value. The register reports recorded transfers to assessors at least once a month.

The Equalization office recommends equalized values to the Board of Commissioners, prepares about 50,000 tax statements a year and keeps ownership maps. The printed assessment roll sells for $0.15 a page with a $35 minimum.

Before closing, call (906) 225-8405 for a tax code number or parcel map, and ask the local unit what the next bill is likely to be.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps for recording your sale deed

A clean recording usually goes in this order. First, the title company or closing agent proofs the deed against the defect list above. Second, if it is a warranty deed, the treasurer certifies five years of paid taxes. Third, the signed original goes to the register by hand, by mail or through an e-recording vendor, with the $30.00 fee and any transfer tax. Fourth, the buyer reports the transfer to the local assessor within 45 days.

If you are selling for cash to a buyer who handles the paperwork, much of this still applies, but the buyer's closing agent carries the filing steps. Ask for a copy of the recorded deed once it is indexed.

Frequently asked questions

How much is a flat deed filing in Marquette County?

It is $30.00 whatever the page count, which already covers the state survey and automation portions. Each additional instrument released in the same paper is $3.00.

Who has to pay the transfer tax in Marquette County?

The grantor, which in a sale is the seller. The state takes $3.75 for each $500 step of the price and the county adds its own amount. A deed to a child or grandchild may be exempt if it says so.

Can I mail a photocopy of my signed deed to the Marquette County recorder?

No. Only originals with live signatures are recorded, and court orders need the court's certification. Phone (906) 225-8415 first to check the paperwork.

Does my Marquette County warranty deed need a certificate from the treasurer?

Yes, and so do land contracts. The treasurer confirms the preceding five years of taxes are paid, and the fee sheet lists $5.00 for the certification. A quitclaim without warranty is excused.

How old are the Marquette County records I can search online?

Deeds go back to January 1, 1980, and mortgages and miscellaneous papers to January 1, 1983. For older books, visit the office on Baraga Avenue.

What the Mason County Register of Deeds keeps

Everything that moves title to land in the county, or burdens it, ends up on file here. The register is an elected officer on a four-year term, and MCL 565.551 obliges the office to give the public reasonable facilities to examine and copy the records.

The register also leads the county plat board, a three-seat panel that reviews proposed subdivisions before they reach the state.

The counter keeps three separate schedules, all skipping legal holidays:

  • General business, 9 to 5
  • Accepting documents for the record, 9 to 4:30
  • Passport applications, 9 to 3

Ask the office for its street address and direct phone line before you send a package.

Selling a home in Mason County

Ludington is the county seat and the biggest city. Of the county's 1,242 square miles, only 495 are land, and much of the rest lies under Lake Michigan. M-116 follows the lakeshore to Ludington State Park, which draws seasonal visitors.

The county had an estimated 29,040 residents for 2025, almost unchanged since 2020. It is an older, owner-heavy market:

  • Homeowners report a typical value of $219,600
  • 78.3 percent of homes are lived in by owners
  • Rent for a typical unit comes to $896
  • 28.8 percent of residents are 65 or older

Recording and copy fees

Filing one deed, mortgage or lis pendens costs $30.00. When a single paper discharges or assigns several instruments, each extra one costs $3.00. Ordinary copies are $1.00 per page, plats are $2.00, and a certification stamp is $5.00.

If staff run a name search for you, the price is 50 cents for every year covered, never less than $5.00, and a state or federal tax lien certificate search costs $3.00 a name. Fee schedules change, so ring the office to verify a figure before you cut the check.

Images and indexes reach back to June 23, 1840 and are online. Heavy users can buy a prepaid subscription, and occasional users can pay by card per search. The index is a working tool that may contain mistakes and is not a certified search.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Mason County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax on a Mason County sale

The county's table stacks $3.75 of state tax and $0.55 of county tax on each $500 of price, which makes $4.30 per slice. The grantor owes it on any deed given for $100 or more.

Mason County combined transfer tax at three sale prices
Price up toStateCountyTotal
$50,000$375.00$55.00$430.00
$75,000$562.50$82.50$645.00
$100,000$750.00$110.00$860.00

For a price that lands between rows, use the county's table, which continues past the top row shown here.

Separate exemption pages cover the county share and the state share. If one applies, say so on the deed itself. Foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, and land contracts that have not yet passed title are on the exempt list.

What a deed must show to be accepted

The register publishes the full text of MCL 565.201 as its standard. The short version for a modern deed: legible names under the signatures, the notary's name printed nearby, grantee addresses, and a preparer's name and business address.

Format rules run alongside those. Leave a clear strip about 2 1/2 inches deep at the top of the first sheet, print in 10 point or larger, and stay between letter and legal size. A single recordable event belongs on the first line. A translation must accompany foreign-language text, and most of a Social Security number has to be blanked.

Once the register accepts and records a deed, the law treats it as conforming. A compliant deed cannot be refused because of what it says, so closing agents proof the document before it is presented.

Treasurer's tax certification

The county treasurer signs off on deeds ahead of recording, confirming nothing is delinquent for the five years before the instrument date, and hands out tax abstracts on request. Under MCL 211.135 that certificate goes with warranty deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments.

Counter hours are weekdays 8 to 5, and the property tax line is 231 843-8411. Each March 1 the township and city rolls come to the county in a step called settlement, and unpaid real property tax becomes the treasurer's to collect. Village taxes run on a different timetable.

Since 2004 Mason County has run its own tax foreclosures, so the treasurer's staff run title searches, mail notices and sell tax-delinquent parcels instead of the state. The county also audits principal residence exemptions, so any exemption claimed in error is pursued from the same office.

If you owe back taxes when you sell, the usual route is to have the closing agent pay the balance from your proceeds, which clears the way for the certificate.

Parcel splits and address changes

Equalization handles these. It keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5 and answers at 231-845-6288. The department issues addresses for every unit except Ludington and Scottville, splits and combines tax parcels, takes mailing address updates and supplies aerial and tax maps. It also links the county parcel GIS layer, the apportionment report and the yearly equalization report.

Splits come up when a buyer wants only part of a lot or a lakeside piece is being divided. The register records the new deed, and equalization then revises the parcel records.

Owners can also sign up free for the register's Property Fraud Alert.

What to bring when you record

Bring the signed original deed, the fee, and the treasurer's certificate if the deed carries warranties. Check that the preparer's name and business address, the grantee's address and the notary details are all on the page. If a transfer tax exemption applies, make sure the deed says so.

Arrive before 4:30 on a weekday, since recording stops half an hour before the front office closes. A deed handed in late can slide to the next business day.

After recording, the register's index and images update online, and equalization revises the parcel records. Ask the closing agent for a copy of the recorded deed for your files. If you sold for cash and the buyer's agent handled the filing, confirm with the register's office that the deed was indexed under the right parcel and names.

If the sale involves a land contract that has not yet passed title, ask the closing agent whether the transfer tax exemption applies and how it must be worded on the paper that gets recorded.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Mason County deed filing price?

It is $30.00 for each document, with $3.00 more for every additional instrument it releases. Copies are $1.00 a page and certification is $5.00.

What time does Mason County stop taking deeds for the record?

Recording ends at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, half an hour before the front office closes at 5. A deed handed in late can slide to the next business day.

Who pays transfer tax on a Mason County sale?

The seller pays, unless the deed states an exemption. The combined rate is $4.30 for each $500 of price, and the county's table shows the total at each price level.

Does a Mason County warranty deed need anything from the treasurer?

Yes. The county treasurer must certify that no taxes are delinquent for the previous five years before the register records it. A quitclaim without warranty language is excused under MCL 211.135.

How far back do Mason County online land records go?

Images and indexes are online from June 23, 1840 to the present. The index is a working index, so check any key detail against the recorded document.

Where to send or drop off a deed

Recording packages are accepted by mail or courier at 400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307. USPS, UPS and FedEx all work. The phone is (231) 592-0148. Call first to learn the counter's recording hours.

The register maintains the real estate record for every parcel in Mecosta County. Indexing is complete back to January 1, 1968, and every document back to 1859 has been scanned and tagged by liber and page. Index books, including oil and gas, are imaged on the Countyfusion site, and a second public search runs through Vanguard at mecosta.mi.publicsearch.us.

Wherever the parcel sits, the deed is filed in Big Rapids, while assessing and collection stay with the township, village or city. Work out which local unit covers the parcel before asking for a payoff or tax certificate.

Selling a home in Mecosta County

The county has 16 townships, the city of Big Rapids and four villages: Barryton, Mecosta, Morley and Stanwood. Big Rapids is the county seat and largest city, home to Ferris State University.

The county had an estimated 42,320 people in mid-2025, up 4.9 percent from 2020. Owners live in 76.9 percent of homes, and a typical house is valued near $178,900.

Recording and copy fees

Recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, affidavit or similar instrument costs $30.00. That amount includes the statutory fee under MCL 600.2567a plus a $5.00 contribution to the automation fund. A document releasing several instruments adds $3.00 for each extra one.

ServicePrice

The office also records fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral under the Uniform Commercial Code. All other personal property filings belong with the Secretary of State.

Transfer tax on a sale

Two levies add together here. Mecosta County charges 55 cents per $500 slice of value and the state charges $3.75 per slice (MCL 207.525), with any partial slice counted as whole. A deed valued at $100 or more is taxable, and MCL 207.523 puts the liability on the grantor.

The Register of Deeds office collects both amounts alongside the recording fee, and the act calls for payment inside 15 days of delivering the deed.

The deed has to carry the property's full value. Alternatively, attach a valuation affidavit and add a line on the deed saying it is on file, which costs nothing to file. Claim any MCL 207.526 exemption on the deed's face, for instance for a parent-to-child transfer or a deed in lieu of foreclosure.

Why a document gets rejected

An eleven-point checklist drawn from Michigan statutes governs what gets filed. These are the points that most often cause trouble:

  • Names printed under the signatures that differ from the notary acknowledgment
  • A missing grantee address, or no name and address for the drafter
  • A notary block with no commission expiration date
  • A deed naming a surviving owner without a certified death certificate on record
  • A court order lacking the clerk's certification and seal
  • Type under 10 point, or less than 2 1/2 inches of clear top margin
  • An opening line naming more than one recordable event
  • No statement of total property value and no affidavit

Stock should be white and 20-pound, from letter to legal size. Run through the list before mailing, since a rejected package costs days.

Do you need a tax certificate?

A warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract and an assignment of a land contract all do. The certificate comes from the county treasurer and shows taxes paid for the five years before the instrument date, under MCL 211.135. A quitclaim without warranty is excused.

Unpaid taxes move toward forfeiture and foreclosure, so a seller carrying old bills should ask for a payoff figure before closing. Payoffs and certificates are usually handled by the title company out of sale proceeds, which keeps a cash sale moving without extra trips to the courthouse.

UCC filings and lien searches

The register records only the real-estate side of Uniform Commercial Code work: fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral. A standard-form filing with two debtor names and up to 100 pages is $30.00. Extra charges apply for a non-standard form ($7.00), for filings over 100 pages ($12.00) and for each debtor name past two ($10.00).

  • UCC search, per name: $6.00
  • State or federal tax lien certificate, per name: $3.00
  • Copy of a UCC filing, per page: $2.00
  • Copy of a state or federal tax lien, per page: $1.00

UCC search results cover personal property filings only through June 30, 2001. Real estate filings made after July 1, 2001 appear in the real estate index. Searches are done as time allows and carry no guarantee.

Parcels, maps and old records

The Equalization page links a land records portal and a map viewer, and it carries tax maps for each of the 16 townships: Aetna, Austin, Big Rapids, Chippewa, Colfax, Deerfield, Fork, Grant, Green, Hinton, Martiny, Mecosta, Millbrook, Morton, Sheridan and Wheatland. Its document center also lists the millage rates and a property tax estimator.

Lining up the parcel number on a tax map with the legal description on the deed is a quick way to catch a wrong lot before closing. Documents back to 1859 are imaged, which helps when an old lot line or easement turns up in a title search. The Vanguard support line is (888) 608-1808.

Steps for recording a sale deed

A typical sale follows this order. The title company drafts or reviews the deed and checks it against the rejection list above. You sign before a notary, and the notary block needs a commission expiration date. If the deed carries warranties, the county treasurer issues the tax certificate. The package then goes to 400 Elm Street with the $30.00 fee, any certificate charge and the transfer tax.

Bring or include the full property value on the deed, or a valuation affidavit with a line on the deed saying it is on file. Once recorded, the deed appears in the index and the register reports the transfer so the assessors can update the parcel. Ask the closing agent for a copy of the recorded deed afterward and keep it with your sale papers.

What is Mecosta County's charge for filing a deed?

Thirty dollars per instrument, plus $3.00 for each additional instrument released in the same paper. Page copies are $1.00 each.

The state charges $3.75 and the county 55 cents for each $500 of value, with a partial slice counted as whole. The seller pays unless an exemption is stated on the deed.

What address takes Mecosta County recording packages?

400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307. Phone (231) 592-0148 beforehand to confirm paperwork and payment.

Is an uncertified court order good enough for Mecosta County recording?

No. The clerk of the court must certify and seal it. A plain copy is sent back.

How old are the Mecosta County records that can be searched?

The full index starts January 1, 1968, and papers from 1859 onward are scanned and tagged by liber and page. Countyfusion and Vanguard are the two public portals.

Finding the Midland County recording counter

The Register of Deeds sits at 220 W Ellsworth Street in Midland, MI 48640, and answers at (989) 832-6820. The counter takes new documents on weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m. The vault holding the older books opens thirty minutes after that.

Anything arriving after 4 p.m. waits for the next business day, and papers are worked in the order received, provided payment came with them. Counter staff record warranty and quit claim deeds, land contracts, releases, powers of attorney, liens and plats. They do not draft documents or advise on law, so an attorney or title company writes the deed.

What recording costs

Any document, short or long, is recorded for one $30.00 charge that already folds in the state remonumentation and automation charges. A few add-ons exist.

Midland County Register of Deeds fees
ServiceAmount
Recording one document$30.00
Document assigning or discharging more than one instrument$3.00 per instrument beyond the first, added to $30.00
Treasurer's tax certificate$5.00 covers up to 5 legal descriptions, then $1.00 each
Plain copy$1.00 per page
Certified copy$5.00 plus $1.00 per page

You can pay with cash, a check payable to the Register of Deeds, or a card at the counter, where the card processor adds a charge generally about $1.50. Qualified submitters may e-record, but a paper that needs a raised court seal or a death certificate must come in on paper.

Instruments held up without a treasurer's certificate

The treasurer must issue a certificate before any of these four can be recorded:

  • A warranty deed, or any deed that includes a covenant of warranty.
  • A land contract.
  • A land contract assignment containing a warranty clause.
  • A master deed for a site condominium project.

Get the certificate ordered before closing day. A plain quit claim deed needs none. To see whether a parcel's taxes are current, use the county's online lookup, which shows what the treasurer's counter would.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Midland County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax

The county's chart shows $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county on each $500, so $4.30 together. At a $100,000 price the chart columns read $750, $110 and $860. Tax applies from $100 of value upward, subject to the exemption sheets the office links.

Buyer and seller can keep the price off the deed by attaching a Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit. A different form, the Property Transfer Affidavit, goes to the assessor for the City of Midland or for the township that holds the parcel, and state law allows the buyer 45 days.

From signing to filing

Your title company usually runs these, but knowing the sequence shows a seller where the paper and the money travel.

  • Ask the treasurer for a tax certificate if the deed warrants title.
  • Sign before a notary. Register staff will not notarize, but the County Clerk in the same County Services Building offers it for a small fee.
  • Send the state and county transfer taxes to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed (MCL 207.523(3)).
  • File the deed with the $30.00 fee before the 4 p.m. cutoff.
  • The buyer then has 45 days to give the Property Transfer Affidavit to the City of Midland or township assessor.

Recorders also pass a list of recorded transactions to local assessors at least monthly under MCL 211.27a(10).

Age of the record books

The oldest records date to 1855, the year the county was established. Books and microfilm cover the whole run, scanned images with computer indexing start in 1968, and online images reach back to 1950. Online searching uses Fidlar-hosted tools named Tapestry EON and Laredo. Recorded papers are public, and anyone may ask for copies.

The index for 1958 to 1968 is available in an Adobe search format, and entries older than 1958 turn up in the Simple Search option. Back-indexing is still underway, so an older chain of title may call for a visit or a phone call. The recording page also links a property fraud alert and a reporting form, worth using when an inherited parcel still carries a relative's name.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Midland County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

River flooding, wells and septic

The county seat is Midland, and Coleman is the county's other incorporated city. The Tittabawassee River runs through Edenville Township and past the village of Sanford. In May 2020 the Edenville and Sanford dam failures forced evacuations across parts of the city, the village and several townships, so a seller near the river should expect buyers to ask about flood history.

Utilities differ from one parcel to the next. The city of Midland provides water and sewer to its residents and a few neighboring townships, while parcels beyond municipal water rely on private wells and septic systems. Out in the townships, collect well and septic records before listing.

Buyers, owners and turnover

The county held an estimated 83,754 people in July 2025, living among 37,723 housing units, and growth since 2020 has been slight. Owner-occupants hold 78.1 percent of homes, and the middle-priced owned house is valued at $195,400. Renters pay about $1,016 a month. With just 128 building permits issued in 2025, a resale listing faces little new-build competition.

Roughly nine in ten residents lived at the same address a year earlier, a sign of long tenure, so many sellers have held their homes for years and have old deeds and easements to dig out.

With turnover low, a house with clean, well-kept title records stands out. Having the deed, tax certificate and any well or septic records ready makes your listing easier to price and to close.

Papers to gather before listing

Round up your current deed, any older family deeds and the newest tax bill. If a mortgage is being paid off, expect a release to be recorded for a fee. Find out from the title company soon whether a treasurer's certificate is required, and confirm the closing date leaves time to reach the counter before 4 p.m. If a river-area home is involved, add any flood or insurance paperwork to the pile.

Expect to pay the $30.00 recording fee on the deed, plus the same fee for each release if a lender is being paid off. Keep receipts, because the county gives a plain copy for $1.00 a page if you need one later.

A cash sale avoids the lender's appraisal and underwriting wait. The deed still goes through the same notary, certificate and transfer tax steps.

If you do not yet have a deed drafted for the buyer, the register's staff cannot prepare one for you. Line up an attorney or the title company first. Once the deed is signed and notarized, pick a time of day well before the afternoon cutoff, because a late arrival simply rolls to the next business day and can push back your funding.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where do I take a Midland deed, and until when?

220 W Ellsworth Street, Midland, MI 48640, phone (989) 832-6820. Recording closes at 4 p.m. on weekdays, and papers received later are recorded the next business day.

What does it cost to file one deed?

One document costs $30.00, whatever its length. A treasurer's tax certificate for a warranty deed adds $5.00 for up to five legal descriptions.

Does Midland County take e-recorded deeds?

Recording hours

Monroe County's deeds office takes recordings Monday through Friday between 8:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. A real property document that arrives after 3:00 p.m. is handled on the next working day, so the practical cutoff for same-day posting is an hour earlier than the closing time. Ask the office for its current counter location and e-recording instructions before sending a courier.

Most sellers never visit. Their title agent carries the deed in and pays the charge from the closing funds.

Recording fees

Every instrument, whether a deed, a mortgage or a lis pendens, costs a flat $30 however long it runs. The amount already includes the Michigan remonumentation and automation fees. The county accepts cash, checks and credit cards, and a card adds 3 percent, with a floor of $2.

Monroe County Register of Deeds charges that sellers meet
ServiceFee
Deed or mortgage, any page count$30
Each added instrument assigned or discharged in one document$3 on top of the flat fee
Certifying a recorded document$5
Real estate copy, per page$1
Tax certificate for a warranty deed, up to 5 descriptions$5, then $0.20 per extra description
State tax lien search certificate$1

UCC copies run $2 per page, and a recorded plat copy on letter paper is $1. One exception removes the $3 add-on: a document that moves from the State of Michigan or a local government to a Land Bank Authority.

Transfer tax

The state tax is $7.50 per $1,000 and the county tax is $1.10 per $1,000 of total consideration, so $8.60 combined. The county's fee page has the full schedule.

State law makes the seller liable, with payment due at the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed changes hands. MCL 207.526 exempts several kinds of deeds, among them gifts to children and grandchildren, deeds that simply confirm title, and foreclosure transfers. Warranty deeds, master deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments with a covenant of warranty must also show a certificate from the county treasurer's office under MCLA 211.135.

Searching for a deed by name, not address

The office searches by name only and asks for a grantor or grantee plus an approximate year. Staff cannot trace ownership from a street address. A person who lacks the owner's name can get the names on the tax roll from the County Equalization Department or a city assessor, though the roll may list someone other than the true owner.

That rule matters when a relative's house is being sold. Before asking a title company to search, collect these items and have the search check for any lis pendens or lien:

  • The earlier deed or deeds in the family.
  • Probate papers, if an estate owned the house.
  • The exact spelling of every owner's name, with the approximate year of each transfer.

Tax lien searches are priced separately: $1 for a state tax lien certificate and $6 per name for a federal one.

Commercial filings and liens

Uniform Commercial Code filings can surface in a title search. A standard form filing and a termination of a filing each cost $30. UCC search information runs only through June 30, 2001, because realty-related filings after July 1, 2001 are recorded in the real estate index alone.

When checking for a lien on a house, search the real estate index, not the personal property files.

Selling a home in Monroe County

Monroe is the only Michigan county touching Lake Erie, and the city of Monroe is both county seat and largest city. The Port of Monroe and the Enrico Fermi nuclear station in Frenchtown Charter Township give the lakeshore an industrial character. Nine public school districts operate within the county, and its district-of-choice policy lets a family enroll in any district with room.

The 2025 estimate is 156,004 people in 67,494 housing units. Owners hold 81.7 percent of homes, and half of owner-occupied houses sit above $228,900. Renters pay a median $1,059.

Boundary quirks and shoreline parcels

A legal description matters more here than a street address. The Toledo War settlement of 1836 left the Lost Peninsula in Erie Township separated from the rest of Michigan by the state line, and most of that land is a marina. A 1973 agreement ran the line through tiny Turtle Island in Lake Erie, giving Erie Township the Michigan half.

Lakeshore and river parcels raise their own questions about bottomland and easements. If your house touches Lake Erie, the River Raisin or Sandy Creek, hand the title company your survey and any earlier easements at the start, so the exceptions on the title commitment are known well before the buyer's deadline.

Steps to a smooth closing

Start a few weeks ahead. Gather the earlier deed, the exact owner names and any survey. Ask the title agent whether the deed needs a treasurer's certificate, and order it before closing. The agent sends the deed in before 3:00 p.m. with the $30 fee and the transfer tax, and the seller owes that tax unless an exemption is stated on the deed.

A cash sale skips lender appraisal, but the recording steps are the same. Check that the deed shows up in the index afterward under the right names.

If the house came to you through an estate, bring the probate papers, because the title agent needs the chain of ownership to line up name by name. If the house was a gift from a parent or grandparent, or the deed only confirms title, mention it early. Those transfers may be exempt from transfer tax, but the exemption has to be stated on the deed itself, so it cannot be added after recording.

Card payments cost extra, so ask the agent whether the closing funds will cover the fee by check. Expect the recorded deed to come back to the buyer or lender, and ask for your own copy for your sale file.

One more practical point: the county will not look up a deed by street address, so when a buyer's agent asks you for the recording details later, keep the owner names and the approximate year of the transfer handy. Those two items are what the office needs to find the document again quickly.

If anything in the paperwork looks unusual, such as a name spelled two ways across old deeds, tell the title agent before closing so it can be fixed with a corrective document rather than discovered at the counter.

Frequently asked questions

What hours does the Monroe County deeds office keep?

Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Anything real property related that comes in after 3:00 p.m. is recorded or filed the following working day.

How much is the flat charge for a deed in Monroe County?

It is $30 per document regardless of length. Extra instruments assigned or discharged add $3 each, and certifying a copy adds $5. Plain copies of real estate records are $1 a page, and the warranty deed tax certificate is a separate charge.

Does the Monroe County office search by property address?

No. It needs a grantor or grantee name plus an approximate year. The Equalization Department or a city assessor can supply the name on the tax roll.

Which transfer tax rates apply in Monroe County?

$1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, based on total consideration. The seller pays unless an exemption is stated on the deed.

How can I pay at the Monroe County counter?

Cash, checks and credit cards are accepted. A card carries a 3 percent fee with a $2 minimum, so a check costs less on a large closing.

Stanton became the county seat in 1860, replacing Greenville. A parcel in any township of the county, from Carson City to Vestaburg, is recorded here.

Selling near Greenville or Stanton

Greenville is the largest city, with 8,816 residents in 2020. It lies 16 road miles southwest of Stanton and about 33 miles northeast of Grand Rapids, which explains why Montcalm is counted in the Grand Rapids metropolitan area. Lakes and the Flat River sit inside the city limits, and the Fred Meijer Heartland Trail ends in Greenville. A house near a lake or trail often draws a buyer who wants the recreation, so mention those features in your listing.

Carson City, in the southeast, lies along M-57, 20 miles by road from Stanton. Stanton itself is a government town of 1,348 residents in 2020. Farms around both cities mean many listings come with acreage, outbuildings or wells, so gather those records before you list.

The county counted 66,614 residents in 2020 and an estimated 69,406 by July 2025. Owners live in 83.1% of occupied housing. Half of owner-occupied homes were worth under $185,500 in 2020 to 2024 figures, and rent at the median ran $869.

Recording fees

The Revised Judicature Act prices recording at a flat $30.00 a document. Money is due with the paper, and an electronic filing gets one extra business day. Call Stanton to confirm the amount before you mail a check, and ask whether the office has a preferred way to receive electronic filings.

Transfer tax

The grantor owes both taxes. Michigan charges $3.75 and the county $0.55 on each $500 block of value, a partial block counting as a whole one, and the money must reach the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is handed over.

Family handovers get special treatment. The state act excludes a deed from a parent to a child or grandchild, and it excludes foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu. The county act has no family exclusion, so the county share can still apply. Whichever exemption fits, write it on the deed itself.

Deed checklist before you file

MCL 565.201 gives the register grounds to refuse a paper, and a refusal costs a trip across the county. Hand your closing agent this short list before anyone signs.

  • Dark ink signatures, with every signer's name printed beneath and spelled as the notary spelled it.
  • Each grantee's mailing address, plus the preparer's name and address.
  • Roomy margins: 2.5 inches at the top of page one, half an inch around the rest.
  • One recordable event named on the opening line.
  • Letter or legal size sheets in 10-point type or larger.

Anything in a foreign language travels with an English translation, and a Social Security number has to be masked down to four digits.

How a sale changes taxes for the next owner

Between sales, In Michigan a house's taxable value can climb only 5% or the rate of inflation per year, whichever is lower. A transfer ends that protection, and the next owner's value jumps to state equalized value. A close relative who keeps a residence non-commercial can inherit without the jump.

Assessing is a city and township job in Michigan, not a county one, so your local assessor handles the paperwork even though the deed goes to Stanton. The new owner reports the transfer within 45 days.

Sellers who claimed the homestead exemption rescind it on Form 2602 within 90 days of moving out. Late filing runs $5 per day to a $200 limit, and the exemption ends December 31. New occupants file Form 2368 by June 1 or November 1.

Estates and fixer-uppers

Yes, it can still sell. An heir signs through the personal representative, and a certified death certificate gets recorded when the deed names a survivor. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as it stands skips lender appraisals and repair demands.

Before choosing a closing date, ask the county treasurer where the parcel stands on taxes, because any delinquent balance is cleaned up first. If you cannot reach the person named on the deed, a title company can tell you what paper the register will need.

Signing through recording

Begin with a finished deed from an attorney or title company. Register staff review a paper for recording standards, and drafting is not their job. Sign in front of a notary, then walk through the checklist above with your agent. Send the original with the $30.00 fee, plus the transfer tax payable to the county treasurer, to the Stanton office or file it electronically. After recording, the buyer has 45 days to tell the local assessor.

If you live far from Stanton, an electronic filing through your title company saves the trip, though the office allows one extra business day for it. Ask for a copy of the recorded deed for your closing file. Keep it with your tax records, since you may need the date later.

Timing matters when you set a closing date. The recorded date is what fixes your buyer's place ahead of any later claimant, so closing agents usually send the deed the same day funds are released. If something is wrong with the paper, the register returns it, and the fix has to be made before the deed can be recorded.

Closing-day paperwork

Take photo identification for the notary and the names of every owner exactly as they appear on the earlier deed. Know where the buyer's mailing address will be printed, because the register will not accept a deed without each grantee's address. Have the closing agent confirm the legal description, the preparer's information and the notary block before you sign anything.

If your house is part of an estate, collect the personal representative's papers and a certified death certificate for the record. If you moved out, remember the homestead exemption deadline on Form 2602. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can often close sooner, but the deed, the transfer tax and the recording steps are the same as in any other sale.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where is a Greenville-area deed recorded?

Stanton's register of deeds, even for a Greenville address, because Montcalm County has a single recording office at 211 W. Main St. The phone is 989-831-7337.

What is Montcalm's transfer tax rate?

The state charges $3.75 and the county $0.55 for every $500 block of value, rounded up, and the seller pays within 15 days of delivering the deed. Some family transfers are exempt if the deed says so.

Will the register check my deed form?

Staff check that a paper meets recording standards and then record it. Drafting is outside their role, so bring a finished deed prepared by an attorney or title company.

How far is Stanton from Greenville?

About 16 miles by road. Carson City is roughly 20 miles from Stanton, so sellers in the south and west should allow time for an in-person filing.

What do I do about my homestead exemption?

It has to be rescinded on Form 2602 with the local assessor within 90 days of moving out. A late filing is charged $5 per day up to $200.

Each paper gets an exact receipt time, a liber and page, and a line in the entry book. Originals are scanned and sent to microfiche for off-site archive storage, and a tract index lets a searcher start from the legal description rather than a name.

The same staff chair the county plat board and take passport applications. Abstractors, title companies, mortgage lenders, oil and gas land agents and township assessors all rely on this counter.

Selling a home in Montmorency County

Montmorency sits in Northern Michigan, and most of its 547 square miles of land is state forest with lakes left by glaciers. Atlanta, the county seat, is an unincorporated community 46 miles west of Alpena and 32 miles east of Gaylord. Hillman, a village, lies 15 miles east-northeast.

Only 9,153 people lived here in 2020, and the estimate for July 2025 is 9,842. The 2020 census counted 8,930 housing units with 51.6% of them vacant, a share that goes with a market of cabins, lake lots and trail traffic. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $158,600.

If your parcel is rural, confirm which township it sits in, since the local unit handles assessing and your title company will need it. Townships are Albert, Avery, Briley, Hillman, Loud, Montmorency, Rust and Vienna, plus the Village of Hillman.

How recreation shapes sales

Trail access drives much of the local market. The county's ORV, ATV and snowmobile trails are among the best in the state, and it is one of the few counties that let ATVs ride public county roads, which links fuel stops, food and lodging in Hillman, Atlanta and Lewiston. Buyers who hunt, fish or ride often care more about where a parcel touches state forest or a lake than about square footage.

A house near the Thunder Bay River or a lake lot can read as a rental or a weekend place to a buyer. State the road type, the water frontage and any recorded easement in the listing, then confirm each against the register's index before the contract is signed.

Forms and helpers on the county page

The county page carries downloads for a quit claim deed, a warranty deed, an affidavit of affixture for a mobile home, a notice of intention to maintain mineral rights and a principal residence exemption form. It also posts fee sheets for statutory charges, copies and searches, commercial code filings, recording standards and transfer tax, with separate sheets for county exemptions, state exemptions and valuation.

For a cabin, hunting parcel or acreage, three items come up most.

  • A deed that repeats the legal description exactly, because the tract index runs on it.
  • A recorded survey when a boundary matters. The page lists several surveyors and independent searchers in the region.
  • Mobile home or mineral paperwork, when either appears in the chain of title.

Title companies in Atlanta, Alpena and Gaylord are also listed. One of them can draft the deed and order the search that a buyer will want, which the register's staff cannot do.

Tax bill after a sale

A sale resets taxable value. Under MCL 211.27a the next year's figure moves up to state equalized value, half of true cash value, and the buyer informs the local assessor within 45 days. A cabin held for decades can carry a taxable value far below that number, so the new owner may see a jump. A parent, child, sibling or grandchild who keeps a residence non-commercial is excepted, and so is a surviving spouse.

An inherited property counts as a transfer when it passes by will or intestacy to anyone outside those groups. Ask the township assessor which rule fits before you decide on a price, since the next owner's bill may differ a lot from yours. The Montmorency County treasurer can report the parcel's tax status before you set a closing date.

If the seller took the homestead exemption, it must be rescinded on Form 2602 within 90 days of the house ceasing to be the owner's home.

Getting a cabin or acreage ready to close

Order a title search early, since mineral interests and old easements can sit in the chain of title for a long time. If a mobile home is part of the sale, look for the affidavit of affixture. Have the deed prepared by a title company or attorney, then bring the original to the Atlanta counter with the $30.00 fee and the transfer tax paperwork. A cash buyer can often close faster, but the same search and recording steps apply.

Expect the buyer's title company to ask for the legal description, any recorded survey and the names on the earlier deed. If the property crosses a county line, tell the agent early, since the price must be split and tax paid to each county. The state takes $3.75 and the county $0.55 for every $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500. The seller owes it, and it is paid to the county treasurer within 15 days.

Can the office prepare my quit claim deed?

No. It records and indexes. The county page offers quit claim and warranty deed forms, but a title company or attorney should confirm which one fits your transfer.

How do I find out whether mineral rights were severed?

Ask a title company to search the chain of title. The register records mineral interests apart from surface interests, and the county page lists a notice form for keeping mineral rights.

Taxes the seller owes at recording

Two taxes land on the grantor: $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county on every $500 block of the price. A leftover partial block is charged as a full one, which nudges the bill up slightly. Both are paid at the register's counter along with the recording fee.

Distressed sales are handled differently. A sheriff's deed always escapes the state tax and only sometimes escapes the county tax. The state act also exempts deeds given in foreclosure or in place of it, and both acts exempt a corrective deed and a spousal conveyance that makes or ends a tenancy by the entirety. Whichever exemption fits, the deed itself must carry the wording.

Pre-closing checklist

The treasurer's stamp comes first. It shows the parcel's taxes are current, and the register will not record a warranty deed lacking it, so any balance is cleared by closing.

Then the mortgage. When it is paid off, the lender records a discharge, and no new deed is needed. Copies of the discharge or of your deed can be bought at the counter or through the online record search.

  • Pull the current deed so the legal description is copied word for word.
  • List every owner by exact name, since a missing owner means a missing signature.
  • Record a certified death certificate or proof of death if the deed names a survivor.
  • Get the clerk's certification and seal on any court order.

Removing or adding a name takes a new, notarized deed, not an amendment. Recording a certified death certificate takes a deceased owner off title without a fresh deed. A title company or attorney should prepare the paper, and you should expect to sign in front of a notary. Double-check each owner's name against the earlier deed before signing.

Exemption forms

Equalization, the county department, keeps the property forms. The new owner delivers the transfer affidavit to the city or township assessor, and an owner who lives in the home can claim the principal residence exemption from up to 18 mills of school operating tax. Other hardship relief is requested at the local assessor. Some cities and townships are assessed by the county, while the rest keep their own assessors.

If you claimed the principal residence exemption as a seller, ask the local assessor how to rescind it once you move out. Keep the confirmation with your sale papers. The buyer's new exemption and the transfer affidavit are separate filings, so each side should confirm theirs was received.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Muskegon County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling near the lakeshore

Most of Muskegon County by area is water: 961 of 1,460 square miles are lake, leaving 499 square miles of dry ground. Muskegon Lake is Michigan's only deep water port on Lake Michigan, and White Lake and Mona Lake add more shoreline. The urban southwest corner holds Muskegon, Muskegon Heights, Roosevelt Park and Norton Shores.

Muskegon County counted 175,824 people in 2020 and an estimated 177,901 in July 2025. Owners live in 78.1% of housing units, median home value stands at $198,300 and median rent is $1,028. Builders took out 451 permits in 2025.

Heavy lake-effect snow each winter leads buyers of older homes to ask about roofs and porches, so have repair records ready. Beaches and bike trails shape how buyers value a lakeside address. A cottage-style house near Pere Marquette Beach or Mona Lake often draws different offers than a mid-century house inland, so a seller should pin down the parcel's legal description and township before listing.

After the sale closes

The buyer files the property transfer affidavit with the assessor. From the day the deed hits the record, your homestead-type exemptions are over and the new owner has to claim fresh ones. If you still owe back taxes, ask the treasurer what the payoff is a few days ahead; the title company will send it from the money you receive.

All-cash purchasers who accept the home as is must still get the tax certificate, a notary signature and the recording done. Ask how long each takes before you pick a closing date.

The register accepts new papers only until 4:30 p.m. If the lender wires funds after that, the deed is filed the following morning, so tell your closing agent about the cutoff. When the deed is indexed, buy a copy at the counter for $1 a page or print one from the online search, and put it in your closing folder.

Frequently asked questions

How late can a deed be filed?

4:30 p.m. on weekdays. The office itself stays open to 5 p.m., at 1903 Marquette Avenue, Suite A102.

Will a photocopy be recorded?

No. Only papers with original signatures are accepted, and a court order must carry the court clerk's certification and seal.

Why two checks at the counter?

The treasurer's $5 certificate for a warranty deed is paid to the Muskegon County Treasurer, separately from the $30 recording fee and any transfer tax.

Who owes transfer tax on a sale here?

The seller, as grantor. The state charges $3.75 and the county $0.55 for each $500 block of price. Any exemption has to be stated on the deed.

How does a co-owner come off a deed?

By a new, notarized deed that is then recorded. Staff cannot draft it, so use a title company or attorney. A certified death certificate takes a deceased owner off title without a new deed.

Address and schedule

Look for the red-roofed Administration Building in downtown White Cloud, across the street from the post office. The register works from 1087 Newell Street (mail to box 885, ZIP 49349), answers at 231-689-7246 and keeps a fax line at 231-689-7271. Doors are open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. Call ahead if you are driving a long way, since staff can confirm what to bring.

Deed records are indexed back to 1910, and the books themselves reach 1840, so an old family parcel often has a paper trail worth pulling before a sale. The office takes deeds, mortgages, land contracts, trusts and other papers about real property. It supplies no abstracts, forms or notary service, and it cannot tell you when a house was built because it handles land records only.

Paper and electronic recording

Photocopies and faxes are turned away. Only an original with live signatures is recorded, and a self-addressed stamped envelope gets the recorded paper back to you. Fees are collected on the spot and cannot be billed to you later.

Newaygo County counter payment methods
Payment methodSurcharge
Cash or checkNone
Debit or credit card, $100 or less$3.50
Debit or credit card, over $1003.5%

E-recording follows the Michigan eRecording Standards that took effect January 1, 2014. The county handles e-filed documents from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays and takes ACH payment, though the filing vendor may bill extra. Providers are CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile.

  • Left out of e-recording: court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys.
  • On paper, a court document or death certificate must be certified, since a plain true copy is refused.
  • A sheriff's deed goes on record within 20 days of the sale, so call the sheriff's office for sale details before bringing it in.

Transfer tax

The rates are $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, applied after a price is rounded up to the next $500. The grantor pays.

A deed has to state total consideration, with any exemption written beside it, or both taxes are collected. Exchanges are taxed on the actual value of each parcel, and land lying in two counties gets a price split with tax paid to each. Stamps are bought only where the parcel is located, and filing a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit costs nothing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Newaygo County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Free searches of the records

Grantor and grantee name searches cost nothing, and you can use the books yourself even though staff will not run searches for you. A tract index search starts from a legal description, which the county equalization department or your township can supply. A parcel number works too.

Everything recorded is public, so a buyer's title agent will see your deed, any mortgage discharge and any recorded survey. The register has a survey of your lot only if someone recorded one, and it knows lot dimensions only for recorded subdivisions and site condominiums. A deed describes the land, not the buildings on it. A new street address comes from the equalization department, not this office.

A fraud alert signup page on the county site suits owners of land they seldom visit.

Selling a home in Newaygo County

West Michigan's Newaygo County covers 862 square miles, 813 of them land, with more than 230 natural lakes and 350 miles of rivers and streams. Over half the county lies within the Manistee National Forest. Fremont, Newaygo and White Cloud are the main towns, and White Cloud is the county seat.

The July 2025 population estimate is 51,622, up 3.3% from 2020. Owners occupy 86.5% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home was worth $186,700 in 2020 to 2024, and the median renter paid $904.

  • The register keeps plat books, which matter for lake lots in platted subdivisions.
  • Confirm the township before advertising a lake property, because the township assessor holds the tax record.

What buyers ask about

Summer cottage residents are common here, and anglers come for steelhead in spring and salmon in fall. Camping, hunting, cross-country skiing, cycling, birding and ORV riding fill the Manistee National Forest, so a listing that sits near public land should say so.

A seller with an old parcel near Fremont or Newaygo may find early plats and deeds in the register's books, which reach back to 1840. Check the dates on your own paperwork before you list, and note any recorded plat for a lake lot so buyers can see the lot lines.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Newaygo County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Taxes after the house sells

Expect the buyer's taxable value to rise. Michigan resets it at the next assessment to state equalized value, half of true cash value, and the buyer has 45 days to notify the assessor. Close relatives who keep a residence non-commercial are excepted.

The township assessor, not the register, holds the tax record for a lake or forest-edge property, so confirm which township the parcel is in before you list. A new street address comes from the equalization department. Once the deed is recorded, the register's index shows your sale, and the buyer's name appears on the next tax roll.

Ask the Newaygo County treasurer for a tax statement, and for the certification that has to be stamped before a warranty deed can be recorded.

Getting a deed ready for White Cloud

Order the tax certification first, then have the deed prepared with the exact legal description and every owner's name. Sign before a notary, since the register provides no notary service. Bring the original, the transfer tax and a self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the recorded paper mailed back. Pay by cash or check to avoid the card surcharge. Because fees are collected on the spot and cannot be billed, have the payment ready before you arrive or before the title agent sends the package.

If the sale is for cash and the buyer's agent handles the filing, ask when the deed will be filed and confirm it was indexed under the right names afterward.

If you inherited the parcel or it has been in the family for decades, pull the earlier deeds first. The books reach back to 1840 and the deed index to 1910, and the register will not run searches for you, so use the free name search yourself or have your title company do it. Finding a missing owner or an old easement before the buyer's title agent does saves time and avoids a delayed closing.

When land lies in two counties, plan on splitting the price and paying transfer tax to each. If an exemption applies, such as a corrective deed, write it on the deed so the tax is not collected by default.

Frequently asked questions

When does the Newaygo County register of deeds close for the day?

The counter is open until 5 p.m. on weekdays. E-recorded documents are processed between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., so a late file waits for the next business day.

How is Newaygo County transfer tax calculated?

The county charges $1.10 per $1,000 and the state $7.50 per $1,000, after the price is rounded up to the next $500. The seller pays it.

Is there a charge for paying by card at the counter?

Yes: $3.50 on payments up to $100, and 3.5% of the payment above that. Cash and check carry no surcharge, and recording fees cannot be billed.

Can a sheriff's deed or death certificate be e-recorded here?

No. The e-recording rules exclude court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys, so those arrive on paper, certified where required.

Will the register record a photocopy of my signed deed?

No. Only originals with live signatures are accepted, and a court document needs the court's certification.

Which office files deeds

The combined Clerk/Register of Deeds handles land records for Oakland County. Questions go to the office by phone at 248-858-0597 or by email to deeds@oaklandcountymi.gov. Walk-in service is weekdays only, from 8:30 a.m. through the late afternoon. The office serves roughly 1.2 million residents and records more than 140,000 real estate documents every year.

The county has 530,460 households and 569,537 housing units, and median monthly owner costs are $1,998 with a mortgage against $778 without. Mortgages and discharges pass through the recording counter next to deeds.

The public record spans deeds, mortgages, foreclosure records and personal property filings. The Oakland County Super Index supplies copies of recorded documents from 1964 forward, except subdivision plats. As of November 3, 2025 the office stopped recording UCC filings apart from land records, so land record fees cover them.

Not every records request belongs at the deeds counter. The Register of Deeds does not issue birth certificates or other vital records, and it does not take UCC filings for utility transfers. The wider Clerk's office keeps circuit court documents, military discharge forms and birth, death and marriage records, so route those questions to the Clerk instead of the land records staff.

Recording fees and charges

One deed carries a flat $30 charge, whatever its length. Of that, $4.00 is the state survey and remonumentation charge. The same $30 base amount appears in Michigan's fee statute, MCL 600.2567.

Charges at the Oakland County register
ServiceCharge
Deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
Extra liber and page cited in a discharge or assignment$3.00
Photocopy, per sheet$1.00 per page
Certified copy$5.00 per document

Transfer tax, county portion55 cents for each $500 of price
Transfer tax, state portion$3.75 for each $500 of price

A deed carrying a warranty covenant, along with every land contract, needs the county treasurer's tax certification before it is recorded. If you mail a document in, the register will obtain the certificate and attach revenue stamps for you, and the $5 certificate fee goes into your payment.

Transfer tax on an Oakland County sale

Any written transfer of real property worth $100 or more is taxed. Oakland's county rate works out to $1.10 for every $1,000 of price and the state rate to $7.50. A claimed exemption must be explained on the document. Michigan's two transfer tax acts place the tax on the seller or grantor, so plan for it on the seller's side of the closing statement.

  • Put the full property value on the deed, or attach an affidavit stating it.
  • Print any claimed exemption on the document.
  • Find out from the closing agent who buys the stamps and when they are paid.

If the transfer qualifies for an exemption, such as a gift within the family, the document still has to say so. Staff will not guess. Ask your closing agent or attorney to word the exemption line before you sign, because a deed recorded without it is taxed as an ordinary sale.

What a document must contain before recording

Recording depends on meeting the signature and format rules of MCL 565.201, Michigan's recording statute. Staff examine each paper and record only those that pass, and a validation unit checks the legal description before the cashier takes the document.

  • Signatures are original, with the signer's name typed or printed below.
  • The names in the notary block match the names under the signatures.
  • Any instrument that conveys or encumbers real estate shows the grantee's name and address.
  • A document signed in Michigan carries a notary acknowledgment listing the notary's county of commission and expiration date.
  • Black ink, type of at least 10 points, and white paper of 20-pound weight, sized from letter to legal length.
  • An unprinted band of 2.5 inches opens the first page, with half an inch left clear elsewhere.
  • The first printed line names the recordable event.
  • Total property value is given on the document or an affidavit.

When a document names a survivor, a certified death certificate or proof of death must go with it. A court order has to carry the court clerk's certification and seal. Older instruments follow the rules of their day: male grantors' marital status was required before April 6, 2017, and two witnesses before March 2002.

Electronic recording

Four registered providers connect to the register: Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and HopDox. UCC documents and mortgage foreclosure documents cannot be e-recorded.

The county also runs MiPropDocs for documents that do not transfer ownership. It accepts affidavits, association liens and discharges, claims of lien, certificates of trust, discharges, lis pendens, mortgages, notices of commencement, releases and satisfactions of mortgage. Deeds cannot use it, so a house transfer still goes through a provider account or on paper.

Paper filings remain open to anyone. Bring the original to the counter or mail it with payment. Copy the legal description from the prior deed word for word, since the validation step reviews it.

How the register and county treasurer work together

The tax certificate is where the two offices meet. The treasurer confirms the parcel is paid up before a warranty deed goes on record, and the register will not file the deed without the stamp. To price a delinquent balance in advance, buy an official statement through the county's Property Gateway.

Tax foreclosure reaches the register too. It collects redemption money for sheriff deeds and clerk deeds, checks the person redeeming has a stake in the parcel, and passes the funds to the treasurer, who holds them in trust until the paperwork is finished and a check can go to the grantee. If you inherited a house with unpaid taxes, read the Oakland County property tax guide before listing, since the county's foreclosure calendar runs on fixed dates.
