How soon a recorded deed comes back

A document carried to the counter returns in roughly two weeks. One sent by mail takes two to four. A document that came through a title company usually returns about two weeks after recording. Originals are indexed and then mailed back.

Copy requests move faster. Counter customers get five pages as a courtesy, and bigger orders are usually ready within a day or two, for pickup or mailing. The office can quote a foreclosure payoff and takes redemptions on sheriff deeds and clerk deeds from parties with a stake in the land.

A cash sale does not shorten any of these steps. The deed, the certificate and the transfer tax are the same whether the buyer pays with cash or a loan, so build the two-week return into your plans for getting the recorded original.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Oakland County recording fee?

$30 per document, whatever its length. The $4.00 state survey and remonumentation charge is part of that. A discharge that covers several instruments adds $3.00 per extra reference.

Is a tax certificate required for a warranty deed in Oakland County?

Yes. Warranty deeds, land contracts and deeds with a warranty clause need the county treasurer's certification, at $5.00, before the register records them.

How far back do the county's online records reach?

To January 1, 1964, apart from subdivision plat maps. Call the Register of Deeds at 248-858-0597 about anything older.

Are UCC statements still filed separately in Oakland County?

No. Since November 3, 2025 they are handled with land records, and the land record recording fees apply.

Which party owes transfer tax on a house sale?

The seller or grantor, under the Michigan acts, paid with the recording. The county rate is $1.10 per $1,000 of price and the state rate is $7.50 per $1,000.

Where deeds are recorded

Deeds for Oceana County property are filed with the Register of Deeds, whose office is inside the Hart courthouse. Reach it at (231) 873-4158 or write to P.O. Box 111, Hart, MI 49420. Voters elect the register to a four-year term, and the post makes that person the official keeper of the county's land records.

Behind the counter sits an index of everything recorded, plus the original plats for each subdivision. Local governments call on the office for liber and page numbers, instrument numbers and parcel descriptions taken from those plats. UCC financing statements may be filed there as well, and the register chairs the County Plat Board that signs off on new subdivisions.

You can request copies or file a document in person or by post, as long as the fee is enclosed. Include a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself. Adding a daytime phone number lets staff call about a defect instead of returning the paper. The department page also links an online official records search.

Oceana County at a glance for sellers

Oceana is a rural West Michigan county on the Lake Michigan shore. Hart is the county seat and the largest incorporated community. The county has 27,177 people, 16,115 housing units and 10,419 households, and owners hold 84.5% of them. The typical owned home is worth $190,100, median rent is $759 a month, and owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,280.

Prices here sit far below the Detroit suburbs, so the dollar cost of transfer tax and other percentage-based charges is lower even though the rates match. Only 136 building permits were issued during 2025, which tells you new construction is not flooding the market.

Recording and transfer tax stamps belong to the county that holds the parcel. Mason, Lake, Newaygo and Muskegon counties adjoin Oceana on land, so make sure the property lies in Oceana before you send a deed here. US 31 follows the western side through Hart and Pentwater, and M-20 crosses the south toward Hesperia.

Recording fees

State law, at MCL 600.2567, fixes recording at $30 for any document regardless of length. A charter county may set a different schedule by ordinance, so phone the Oceana office for the price list before you mail a check.

Fees a Michigan register of deeds may charge
ServiceAmount
Record one document$30.00
Each extra instrument covered by an assignment or discharge$3.00
Page of a copy$1.00
Certification of a recorded document$5.00
Grantor/grantee search, each year covered$0.50, with a $5.00 floor
Filing or looking up any other paper$1.00

Pay when you hand over the document. Electronic submissions have one business day after receipt, and the statute gives government agencies and tax foreclosure filings separate payment schedules.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Oceana County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How much transfer tax applies to a sale?

Two Michigan acts tax a deed's value: MCL 207.505 covers the county share and MCL 207.526 the state share. Transfers worth $100 or more owe both. The county takes 55 cents per $500 block and the state takes $3.75 per block, and any partial block counts as a full one. The seller or grantor is the taxpayer, so plan for it on your side of the closing statement.

The fraction rule matters on odd prices. A price that ends a little past a $500 mark still pays for the whole next block. Swapping two properties triggers tax on each deed, measured by the true value of what each deed conveys.

  • State the full consideration on the deed, or file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit alongside it.
  • The affidavit costs nothing to file, but the deed must say it is being filed.
  • Write any exemption you claim on the instrument.
  • A parcel lying in two counties pays each county on its share of the price.

Rules a deed must meet

Oceana's register posts a recording checklist drawn from MCL 565.201 and nearby sections. Miss one item and the paper comes back unrecorded, which can push a closing date, so run through it before anyone signs.

  • Signatures are originals, and typed, stamped or printed names appear below them.
  • Notary names match the signature names exactly.
  • A grantee address, by street or post office box, appears on each deed or assignment.
  • The drafter's name and address are on the document.
  • A Michigan judge, court clerk or notary acknowledges anything that conveys or burdens real estate.
  • A survivor clause needs a certified death certificate or other proof of death.
  • Court orders arrive certified and sealed by the court clerk.

The page layout has its own checks. Keep the top 2.5 inches of the first sheet blank and half an inch clear on every other edge. Print in black on white stock that weighs 20 pounds or more, in type of 10 points or larger, and use sheets between letter and legal size. The first line of print must name the recordable event in a single statement.

Electronic recording

Oceana County accepts e-recording through Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile or Indecomm Global Services. Sign up with one provider to begin. The register answers e-recording questions at (231) 873-4158.

E-recording is usually the quickest route for a house sale, since the title company submits the deed from its own office and the county never handles a paper original. Ask your closing agent at the start which provider they use, and whether the transfer tax is paid through the same submission.

A title company closing your sale can tell you whether it files through one of these services. For a family transfer or a paper deed, deliver the original to the courthouse or mail it with the fee and a return envelope.

Getting a deed recorded step by step

For a typical sale the title company handles everything, and you only sign. If you are doing a family transfer or a sale without a title company, the path is short.

  • Confirm the parcel lies in Oceana County.
  • Check the deed against the format rules above, including the blank top margin and the grantee address.
  • Put the full price on the deed, or attach the valuation affidavit.
  • Enclose the recording fee and the transfer tax, with a stamped return envelope.
  • Add a daytime phone number so staff can call if something needs fixing.

A cash buyer needs the same recording and pays the same fees. The deed still has to meet every formatting point, and the transfer tax still falls on the seller. Calling the office before you mail anything is the cheapest way to avoid a returned document. Keep copies of what you send, and keep the recorded original when it comes back, since it is your proof that title passed to the buyer.

Frequently asked questions

What number reaches the Oceana County Register of Deeds?

(231) 873-4158. The office sits in the Hart courthouse, and the post office box is 111, Hart, MI 49420.

Will the register accept a deed sent by post?

Yes, with enough fees enclosed. Add a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, and a phone number so staff can resolve any question about the paperwork.

What does recording one document cost in Oceana County?

State law sets $30 per document, whatever the page count. Because a county schedule can differ, confirm the figure with the office before you send payment.

Is there a fee to file the transfer valuation affidavit?

No. The deed has to state that the affidavit is being filed, and the affidavit has to disclose the total consideration.

Who owes the Michigan transfer tax when an Oceana County house sells?

The seller or grantor does. The county levy is 55 cents and the state levy is $3.75, each applied to every $500 of value.

Where the recording office is

You will find the Register of Deeds one floor up from the front door of the main courthouse, at 301 W. Upton Avenue in Reed City, MI 49677. Call (231) 832-6113, fax (231) 832-6115, or write register@osceolacountymi.gov. Counter hours are 9 to 5 Monday through Friday, except holidays, and the public computers shut off fifteen minutes early, at 4:45.

Reed City became the seat in 1927, yet the office still holds books from 1853. Besides taking deeds, it maintains a tract index that sorts every parcel by legal description, and the register also leads the county Plat Board. Staff will not draft a deed or give legal advice. If you need a document prepared, hire an attorney or ask the title company handling your closing.

Recording fees and copy costs

Recording a deed runs a flat $30 whether it is one page or twenty. The counter takes cash, cards, checks and money orders, and checks should name Register of Deeds as payee. Paying by card adds a processing charge.

Osceola County Register of Deeds fees
ServiceCharge
Recording a deed or mortgage$30.00 flat
Releasing or assigning several instruments in one paper$3.00 for each beyond the first
Photocopy of a recorded paper$1.00 a page
Certifying a copy$5.00 more
Plat copy$2.00 a page
Treasurer's tax certificate$5.00 for five descriptions, then $0.20 each
Document sent by email$7.00
Staff name search$5.00 a name plus $0.50 a year
Staff search of the tract index$50.00 an hour

The treasurer's certificate fee rides along in the same payment to the register, so a closing agent writes one check for both.

Transfer tax on a sale

The county publishes the combined rate as $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state. Behind those numbers sit MCL 207.504 (55 cents per $500) and MCL 207.525 ($3.75 per $500). Either the deed states the sale price or an affidavit of value goes in with it. If a sale bundles furnishings with the house, list the two values apart so only the real property is taxed.

The two taxes carry different exemptions, and the state list is longer. These are the ones Osceola sellers run into most:

  • Gifts of a home down the family line, such as parent to child, skip the state tax only.
  • A deed from a lender after foreclosure, or in lieu of it, escapes the state tax, and escapes the county tax too if the loan was government backed.
  • A price below $100 owes neither tax.
  • A court-ordered transfer owes neither tax unless the court sets a price.
  • A land contract is not taxed until title passes with the last payment.

List any exemption on the face of the deed. The register at (231) 832-6113 can tell you how the office likes it phrased.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Osceola County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Why a deed gets rejected

The register applies the format rules of MCL 565.201 at the counter, and failing any one sends the deed back to you. Check each of these first:

  • Margins: leave 2.5 inches empty at the head of page one and half an inch on the other edges.
  • Print: black ink in 10-point type or larger, on white paper of 20-pound weight, letter to legal size.
  • Names: print each signer under the signature, spelled the way the notary's block spells it.
  • Addresses: the grantee's street address, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • Privacy: mask the first five digits of any Social Security number.

Tax proof is a separate hurdle. For warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of those contracts, the County Treasurer must issue a certificate first. MCL 211.135 sets what it confirms: no liens, and taxes paid for the prior five years. A quitclaim without covenants of warranty skips it.

Searching Osceola land records yourself

The county's online search covers 1988 forward, and images of every document can be called up by liber and page back to 1853. Handwritten grantor and grantee books run to 2003, and courthouse terminals show names from 1988. Browsing names is free.

Searching by legal description through the tract index costs $50 an hour, a rate the Board of Commissioners set, and staff do not do title or mineral searches. Mailed search requests are worked in as time allows, with three days as the target. If you need an answer the same day, call a title company.

The county's Fraud Notify service emails you when anything is recorded under your name. That helps an owner of a vacant, inherited or seasonal house spot a forged deed early. GIS parcel maps are linked from the same page.

What order to line up the paperwork

A sale in Osceola County moves faster when the courthouse steps happen in a sensible order. A seller working with a buyer from outside the area can hand this sequence to the closing agent:

  1. Look up the current deed through the online search or the public terminal in Reed City and check the legal description against the parcel map.
  2. Order the treasurer's certificate first, since no warranty deed gets recorded without it.
  3. Have the deed drafted on compliant paper with the sale price or an affidavit of value.
  4. Work out both transfer taxes, and print any exemption you claim on the deed itself.
  5. Bring or mail one payment payable to Register of Deeds covering the $30 recording charge, the tax and the treasurer's fee.
  6. Enroll in Fraud Notify, which sends you an email about later filings in your name.

If something is wrong, the register's staff will usually phone before returning a document, so leave a number that you answer. Mail adds days, and a returned deed adds more, which is why many sellers simply drop the paperwork at the Reed City counter during the 9 to 5 weekday hours.

Most of these steps cost little, and the Reed City counter can take care of nearly all of them in one visit.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Osceola County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Osceola County housing context

Osceola County is a Northern Michigan county of rolling hills, with Evart and Reed City as the cities and Hersey, LeRoy, Marion and Tustin as villages. US 10 and US 131 are the main roads. Population is estimated at 23,516. Typical home value is $155,400, 83.7% of homes are owner occupied, and rent is $807 a month. No building permits were issued in 2025, so the housing supply is mostly older stock.

Get a payoff figure from the Osceola County Treasurer before you pick a closing date, because the certificate has to exist before a warranty deed can record. Selling for cash does not change this. The buyer still takes the same deed, and the same tax certificate and transfer tax apply, but there is no lender timeline, so this paperwork often sets the closing date.

Frequently asked questions

Does page count change the Osceola County recording fee?

No. It is $30 per document, with $3 added for each extra instrument that one paper releases or assigns.

Will Osceola County email a recorded deed?

Yes, for $7.00. Counter copies run $1.00 a page, and a certified copy adds $5.00.

Does a quitclaim deed need the treasurer's certificate?

Usually not. It is aimed at warranty deeds and land contracts, and MCL 211.135 excuses conveyances without warranty covenants.

Which Osceola County transfer tax exemptions help a seller?

A family transfer down a generation skips the state tax, and a price below $100 owes neither. The exemption must be written on the deed.

What is the register's phone number?

Call (231) 832-6113 or email register@osceolacountymi.gov. The courthouse address is 301 W. Upton Avenue, Reed City.

Where and how to file a deed in Mio

Oscoda County has one office for both the Clerk and the Register of Deeds. It works out of the Government Administration Building at 311 South Morenci Avenue in downtown Mio, MI 48647. Phone 989-826-1110, fax 989-826-1136, or email countyclerk@oscodacountymi.com. Mailed items go to PO Box 399.

Doors are open on weekdays from half past eight until half past four, with a break at noon for an hour, and the office shuts on most federal holidays. Walk-ins are fine. Documents arrive in three ways:

  • Over the counter in Mio.
  • By regular mail to the box, with a stamped return envelope so the original comes home.
  • By courier, UPS or FedEx, to the street address.

Title agents based elsewhere can send files through CSC Ingeo, EPN (E-Recording Partners) or Simplifile. Certified court documents and death certificates cannot go that route, so ask first.

Recording fees

The numbers below come from the state schedule in MCL 600.2567. Phone 989-826-1110 for the exact total, including any card or vendor surcharge, before a check goes in the mail.

Recording fees for Oscoda County documents
ServiceFee
Entering and recording a document of any length$30.00
Each added instrument released or assigned by the same paper$3.00
Copy of a record$1.00 a page
Certifying a recorded paper$5.00

Copies are handed out on paper only, and phone photos of records are not allowed.

Transfer tax on a Mio-area sale

Two taxes ride on every deed. The state charges $3.75 per $500 of price (MCL 207.525), and the county charges 55 cents per $500 (MCL 207.504). A part-block rounds up. The price must be shown on the deed itself or in an attached affidavit.

Exemptions the two laws share, and one they do not:

  • Price under $100.
  • Transfers ordered by a court with no price attached.
  • Boundary straightening with no money paid.
  • Quitclaims that only repair a flaw in title already held.
  • Family deeds from parent to child or grandchild, which excuse the state tax and nothing more.

Put the exemption in writing on the deed. The seller is normally the party who bears the tax, so ask your closing agent to show it as a line on your side of the settlement statement.

Land records and fraud protection

Anything from 1985 forward is electronic, and older material is on microfiche. New filings show up online within five days. Each one is time stamped, checked, numbered, indexed and scanned.

All real estate records are public, and anyone may search them in the office or online. Searches go by the property owner's name, and several public computers sit in the office. Staff do not run title searches. They send people to a title company or a private searcher. Ownership follows whatever documents the office has recorded, so a seller holding an old unrecorded deed should file it before listing.

Online tools come in three kinds. Fidlar Laredo is a subscription program with a software download, popular for heavy searching. Fidlar Tapestry bills as you go and spans several Michigan counties. A free direct search link also exists on the county page.

Title fraud is a real risk on vacant and seasonal property, where nobody sees the mail. Alerts are worth setting up before you list, and again after closing if you keep other land in the county.

Property Fraud Alert costs county landowners nothing and starts at 1-800-728-3858 or propertyfraudalert.com/mioscoda. It alerts you right away when a paper is recorded against your parcel. The Youngblood Law, House Bills 5598 and 5599, signed in November 2024, makes filing a fraudulent document with any Michigan register of deeds a felony.

What a deed must show before Mio accepts it

The office drafts nothing and keeps no legal forms. Staff recommend an attorney or title company, and for do-it-yourselfers they name MichiganLegalHelp.org and eforms.com as starting places. They cannot say how a deed should be prepared.

MCL 565.201 governs the page itself: dark ink signatures with printed names, the grantee's address, the drafter's name and address, and a 2.5 inch clear top margin on the first page. MCL 211.135 governs tax proof. Before a warranty deed records, the county treasurer certifies that no liens or tax titles are held and that five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim without warranty covenants is excused. Get the certificate from the Oscoda County Treasurer and carry it with the deed to Mio.

Selling a house in Oscoda County

Oscoda County is the only county in Michigan with no incorporated city or village, so the county offices in Mio are the nearest local government for every parcel. Mio, the seat, sits in the Au Sable River valley where M-33 and M-72 meet, and the south half of the county lies in the Huron National Forest.

The population is estimated at 8,723, up 6.1% from the 2020 count of 8,219. The middle home value is $125,500, owner occupancy is 87.2%, and monthly rent is $681. Housing units total 7,792 against 3,788 households, which shows how many homes sit empty or are used seasonally. Only 24 building permits were issued in 2025. If you are selling a seasonal cabin, expect a buyer pool of out-of-area owners, and confirm internet service at the address for remote-work buyers.

Before listing a cabin or woodland home, search the owner's name at the register and ask the county treasurer for the tax certificate, since both steps affect closing speed.

Closing steps for a cabin or home sale

A sale here follows a short, predictable path. The title company or your attorney prepares the deed, and the register only records it.

  1. Search the owner's name at the register to confirm every earlier deed is recorded.
  2. Request the treasurer's certificate if the deed carries warranty covenants.
  3. Put the price on the deed or attach the affidavit, and write any transfer tax exemption on the face of the deed.
  4. Send the original by mail, courier, e-recording or hand delivery, with the recording fee.
  5. Enroll in Property Fraud Alert so a later filing against your parcel reaches you.

A cash buyer needs the same recording and pays the same fees. The savings come from skipping lender approval and appraisal, not from skipping any county step. Keep the recorded original or a copy of it with your closing papers. Call 989-826-1110 if you are unsure which of these applies to a family transfer.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Oscoda County register's office?

It is at 311 South Morenci Avenue in Mio, MI 48647. Letters go to PO Box 399, and the main number is 989-826-1110.

Does Oscoda County take deeds by mail?

Yes. Send the original to the PO Box, or ship by UPS or FedEx to the street address, and include a self-addressed stamped envelope for the return.

Which e-recording vendors does Oscoda County use?

CSC Ingeo, EPN and Simplifile. Certified court documents and death certificates are excluded, so call before sending one.

How is transfer tax figured on an Oscoda County sale?

The state charges $3.75 and the county charges 55 cents for every $500 of price, if no exemption fits. A partial $500 block counts as a full one, so a price just over a block boundary adds to the bill.

Does the Mio office search titles?

No. It is a recording office and refers people to title companies or private searchers, though you may search names yourself in the office or online.

Who records property documents

The Otsego County Register of Deeds is at 225 W Main Street, Gaylord, MI 49735. Call 989-731-7550 or fax 989-731-7519. The office holds every record of a transfer or encumbrance of land in the county.

Staff time stamp each paper, assign liber and page numbers and index it on computer. The computerized index and images start on March 5, 1864, and any record can be pulled and copied in the office within minutes. Images are also sold online.

The office works with the county Equalization Department to keep ownership current, using tax identification numbers or owner names. It does not run searches for the public. If you want a search done for you, call a title insurance company or a land records data company, or sit at the Gaylord counter and look for yourself.

Recording fees in Gaylord

The office charges $30 for each document it records, with every page included. That rate has applied since October 1, 2016.

Otsego County Register of Deeds fees
ServiceFee
Recording a document, all pages$30
Each extra instrument a document assigns or discharges$3
Copies of recorded instruments$1 per page
Certification of a document$5
Real estate record search$5 per name
State or federal tax lien certificate$3 per name
U.C.C.-11 certificate$6 per name

Of the recording fee, $4 goes to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund. That share is skipped for fixture filings, state, federal and MESC liens, state deeds and plats. For mailed copy orders, phone 989-731-7551 first so staff can fix the page count and price. Payment is due when the service is performed, and checks are made out to Otsego County Register of Deeds.

Transfer tax and exemptions

Transfer tax is collected at the moment of recording, under MCL 207.505(5) and MCL 207.526(6). Either print the full consideration on the deed or file a real estate transfer valuation affidavit, which costs nothing. An exempt transfer should say so on its face.

The rates are $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county per $500 or fraction, from MCL 207.525 and MCL 207.504. Because a fraction counts as a whole block, a price that lands just past a $500 mark costs a little more than you might expect. Budget for the tax on your side of the closing statement.

Exemptions that matter to homeowners:

  • Consideration below $100 removes the tax under both acts.
  • A deed from a mortgage foreclosure skips the state tax, and one given on a government-backed loan skips both. The state exemption does not carry over to the lender's later sale of the property.
  • Deeds within a family, parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, are exempt from the state tax only.
  • A land contract owes nothing until the buyer finishes paying and legal title passes.
  • A deed that moves a boundary line with no money paid is exempt from both.

Mineral rights transfers and leases are exempt too, but they come up rarely in a house sale.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Otsego County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

E-recording and online records

Otsego County offers electronic recording for people who file many documents at once. It is a secure, verified-user service, and you register through an approved provider before you start. Two providers are named: Simplifile, at simplifile.com, and CSC, at cscglobal.com/service/erecording.

Online, the office sells images of recorded documents. Searching the real estate record at the office costs $5 per name, and certificate searches for state tax liens, federal tax liens and U.C.C.-11 filings carry the per-name fees in the fee table.

Freedom of Information requests go on a completed FOIA Request Form sent by email to the county's FOIA coordinator or faxed to 989-731-7529. A deed copy does not need a FOIA request, since recorded instruments are available at $1 per page.

What a deed needs before it reaches the counter

Two statutes apply in Gaylord. MCL 565.201 governs how the paper looks, and MCL 211.135 governs proof that taxes are paid. A deed that misses either can be refused.

  • Legible black or dark blue signatures, with each signer's name printed below and matching the notary's wording.
  • The grantee's mailing address, plus whoever drafted the instrument with a business address.
  • Black type of at least 10 points on white 20-pound paper, between letter and legal size, and a clear 2.5 inches at the top of page one.
  • A single opening line naming the one recordable event, such as a warranty deed or a mortgage discharge.
  • Social Security numbers masked down to the last four digits, unless a law demands more.

With a covenant of warranty in the deed, the county treasurer must certify there are no tax liens or titles on the parcel and that five prior years of taxes are paid. A city, village or township treasurer certifies the local side. A quitclaim deed without warranty covenants, a sheriff's deed and a deed made under a court judgment are excused.

Otsego County housing context

Otsego County is in Northern Michigan. Gaylord is the only city and the seat, and Vanderbilt is the lone village. Water shapes the housing stock: the county has more than 370 lakes, mostly in the south, and Otsego Lake is the largest at 1,972 acres. I-75 bypasses Gaylord on the west and M-32 runs east and west through it.

Population is estimated at 26,080, a gain of 3.9% since the 2020 count of 25,091. The middle home value is $219,700, owner occupancy is 77.2%, and monthly rent is $1,008. The county has 14,976 housing units but 11,231 households, so units outnumber households by about 3,700, which points to a lot of second homes and cabins. Building permits numbered 25 in 2025.

Owners of lake or woodland parcels can ask the Equalization Department for the parcel's tax identification number, and the Treasurer for the tax certificate, before choosing a closing date. A buyer who works remotely should confirm internet service at the address.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Otsego County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Step by step: recording a sale

Your title company normally handles recording, but the sequence is worth knowing, especially for a family or cash transfer.

  1. Get the parcel's tax identification number from the Equalization Department.
  2. Ask the county treasurer for the tax certificate if the deed has warranty covenants.
  3. Prepare the deed to the paper, margin and signature rules above.
  4. Print the price on the deed or attach the free valuation affidavit, and note any exemption.
  5. Deliver the deed with the $30 fee and the transfer tax, in person at 225 W Main Street or through an e-recording provider.

A cash buyer follows the same steps and pays the same charges. What a cash sale skips is the lender's appraisal and underwriting, not the recording. Call 989-731-7550 if a question comes up about a document before you send it.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Otsego County recording fee?

Gaylord charges $30 a document with all pages included, and adds $3 for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges.

Is there a filing fee for Otsego County's transfer valuation affidavit?

None. The county collects nothing for the affidavit, which you can use instead of printing the value on the deed.

How far back do Otsego County's computer records go?

They start on March 5, 1864. The office keeps both the index and the images on computer from that date to the present.

What do Otsego County copies cost?

Each page is $1, and a certification adds $5. For mail orders, ring the office first for an exact quote.

Will Gaylord staff search a title for me?

No. The office does not provide search services and points people to a title insurance company or a land records data company. You can search the records in person at the Gaylord office.

Ottawa County runs its recording desk from West Olive, at 12220 Fillmore Street, West Olive, MI 49460. The building has a recording office in Room 146 and a combined vital records and deeds counter in Room 130, so phone ahead at (616) 994-4510 to learn which window takes your deed. The email is register@miottawa.org and the fax is (616) 994-4521.

A second site, the Research Library, is at 414 Washington Avenue, Room 115, in Grand Haven, the county seat. Its direct line is (616) 846-8109. Weekday service at both sites starts at 8 am and ends at 5 pm, though Grand Haven shuts for an hour after noon. On the third Monday of each month the vital records and deeds offices close from 8:00 to 9:30 am.

The Clerk and Register of Deeds operates five locations. Only West Olive and Grand Haven handle deeds, while Holland and Hudsonville are vital records sites.

How recording works

Ottawa County records and returns a document within one to two days of receipt, as long as it meets the recording requirements. A fax or photocopy of a deed is turned away, because only originals with live signatures are accepted. Court papers must be certified by the court, and a death certificate must be certified by the Clerk's office before it can be recorded.

Professional filers use electronic recording. The county's software lets it record warranty deeds and other documents that need a tax stamp, and it accepts submissions from four approved companies, including Indecomm, Corporation Service Company and Simplifile. Contact each firm about eligibility and pricing. The county collects only the fees set by state and local law, and vendors may add processing charges.

A one-time filer can use the Consumer E-Recording portal for affidavits, liens, certificates of trust, mortgages, discharges, lis pendens, notices of commencement and releases. Deeds and other ownership transfers, UCC documents and foreclosure papers are barred from the consumer portal, so a seller has to deliver the deed in paper or through a title company.

At the counter you can pay in cash, by check or by card. Recording by card adds a 3% convenience fee, and copy orders can also draw on an escrow account.

Recording and copy fees

Michigan sets the base amounts in MCL 600.2567, and Ottawa County adds its own online and card terms. Searching the index is free, and the county asks $1 per page, plus a convenience fee, to view, print or save an image.

Ottawa County recording and copy fees
ServiceAmount
Recording one document, any length$30
Extra instrument assigned or discharged in the same document$3 each
Searching the online indexNo charge
Viewing, printing or saving an image online$1 per page plus a convenience fee
Certified copy$5 under the state schedule
Card payment when recording3% added

Copies are not obtained through Freedom of Information requests, since every record in the office is public or covered by statute and copy fees are fixed by state law. Anyone can get a copy of your deed once it is recorded.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Ottawa County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax for the seller

Two statutes stack here: MCL 207.525 levies $3.75 per $500 for the state, and MCL 207.504 levies 55 cents per $500 for the county, the rate for any county under 2,000,000 people. Any remainder under $500 is treated as a full block. The deed needs to show the value or carry an affidavit, and the seller is the party who owes the tax.

The median owner-occupied home in Ottawa County is valued at $323,400, so for a typical sale the tax is a real line item on the settlement statement. Ask your title company for the figure before you set a net-proceeds target.

You can often avoid the tax with an exemption written on the deed. The common ones for homeowners are:

  • Consideration under $100.
  • Mortgage foreclosure deeds, including deeds in lieu, under the state act.
  • Gifts down the family line, parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, which the state act alone excuses.
  • A spouse's deed that makes or ends a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A deed whose only job is to cure a flaw in title the grantee already holds.

The Document Recording page on the county site links both a County Exemptions sheet and a State Exemptions sheet.

Preparing a deed for recording

The office does not draft documents, supply forms or give legal advice, and it does not furnish abstracts of title. Use an attorney, title company or real estate agent for help. The office cannot say when a house was built or whether a survey exists either, since it only holds land records, and most property has never had a survey recorded.

A state law effective April 1, 1997 requires 2.5 inches at the top and half an inch on the other sides, to leave room for recording stamps. MCL 565.201 contains that rule. Witnesses are no longer required on documents, though most documents still need a notary.

Papers that need a tax certificate from the Treasurer's office:

  • Warranty deeds.
  • Land contracts and assignments of land contracts.
  • Master deeds and amendments to master deeds.

MCL 211.135 backs that requirement and excuses quitclaim deeds without covenants of warranty. If a house is in mortgage foreclosure, the Register of Deeds takes redemption payments, though you may redeem straight through the lender or its lawyer. After the redemption period runs out, only the lender can help.

The county also offers Property Fraud Alerts. Owners sign up to be told when a document is recorded that affects their property.

Selling a house in Ottawa County

Ottawa County is in West Michigan on 24 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline. Holland is the largest city, and the others include Zeeland, Hudsonville, Coopersville and Ferrysburg. Grand Valley State University is in Allendale and Hope College is in Holland, which keeps demand for rentals and starter homes steady near both campuses.

Population is estimated at 308,459, up 4.1% from the 2020 count of 296,200. The median home value is $323,400, the owner-occupied rate is 79.3%, median gross rent is $1,211 and median household income is $90,502. Building permits numbered 1,411 in 2025, so new construction competes with resale listings.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Ottawa County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Recording steps for a sale

Most sellers never visit the recording office, because the title company handles it. If you are closing without one, work through this order.

  1. Confirm the deed carries original signatures and a notary acknowledgment.
  2. Check the margins, the grantee address and the drafter's name.
  3. Ask the Treasurer's office for the tax certificate if the deed is a warranty deed or land contract.
  4. Write the value or an exemption on the deed.
  5. Bring the original to West Olive or Grand Haven, with the $30 fee and the transfer tax.

A cash sale uses the same steps. It skips the lender, so the recording timeline of one to two days often sets the closing date. Call (616) 994-4510 if you are unsure which window to use.

Frequently asked questions

Where does a deed get recorded in Ottawa County?

Bring it to the recording office at 12220 Fillmore Street in West Olive, or let a title company e-record it. Phone (616) 994-4510 to confirm the room. The Washington Avenue site in Grand Haven is the research library.

Can I record a photocopy or fax of a deed in Ottawa County?

No. Staff record only papers bearing original signatures.

How quickly does Ottawa County record a deed?

The county records and returns a document within one to two days of receipt when it meets the recording requirements. A title company or lender decides when the original reaches you.

Can I use the Ottawa County consumer e-recording portal for my deed?

No. The portal excludes deeds and other documents that transfer ownership, as well as UCC documents and foreclosure papers. It handles items like mortgages, discharges and notices of commencement.

Who pays Ottawa County transfer tax on a sale?

The seller does. The state charges $3.75 and the county charges 55 cents for each $500 of value, unless an exemption written on the deed applies.

Where to take a deed in Roscommon County

Take it to the Roscommon County Register of Deeds, 500 Lake Street in the village of Roscommon, ZIP 48653. The office number is 989-275-5931 and the fax is 989-275-8640. Call ahead for counter hours, especially if you are driving in from Houghton Lake, Prudenville or St. Helen.

The county's Online Services page links a public record search, a separate sign-in for title companies and law offices, BS&A parcel and tax data, and a GIS parcel map. Pull the prior deed and the legal description there before anything is drafted.

Parcels here are spread out, with lakefront lots around Houghton Lake and Higgins Lake and woodland near the Au Sable State Forest. Interstate 75 clips the northeast, US 127 follows the western edge of both lakes, and M-18 and M-55 cross near the middle, so a trip to the counter is easy from most of the county.

Recording charges

Filing is a flat $30 for each document, whether it is a deed, a mortgage or a lis pendens. If one document releases or assigns several earlier instruments, add $3 for each additional one. The register's fee page lists these extras:

  • Photocopies at $1 a page, plus $5 when certified.
  • Faxed copies at $2 plus $1 a page.
  • Mailed copies at $5.
  • Emailed copies at $2 plus $1 a page.

E-recording is limited. The county takes no certified documents electronically except death certificates, so a signed deed arrives at the counter or by post. Ask the office how the check should be made out and whether to enclose a prepaid return envelope.

Documents that need a treasurer's certificate first

The register will not file a warranty deed, a deed with any warranty covenant, a land contract, an assignment of a land contract, a condominium master deed or a covenant deed until the County Treasurer has issued a tax certificate. The treasurer's fee is a separate $5 payment for up to 25 parcel descriptions, with 20 cents for every description after that, made out to the County Treasurer.

The rule comes from MCL 211.135. A certificate has to show no tax liens or tax titles on the parcel and that the preceding five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim deed with no warranty falls outside the section, and that is why many family transfers skip it.

Roscommon County sale paperwork
StepOfficeCost or timing
Tax certificate for a warranty deedCounty Treasurer$5 for up to 25 descriptions
State transfer tax, when it appliesCounty TreasurerDue within 15 days of delivery
Recording the deedRegister of Deeds$30 for the document
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Roscommon County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who owes transfer tax on a sale?

The seller carries this tax, and the treasurer's office takes the payment. Under the state act the money falls due a little over two weeks after the deed changes hands, and it attaches to deeds and sale contracts made for consideration (MCL 207.523). A county levy of $0.55 for each $500 band of value also applies where the population is below two million (MCL 207.504). The deed has to show its full value on its face, or an affidavit giving that value is attached. A deed that mixes real and personal property can state the two values separately so only the land is taxed.

Plenty of conveyances owe nothing. The state act exempts transfers under $100, deeds to a son, daughter or grandchild, transfers by foreclosure or deed in lieu, court orders that name no price, and quitclaim deeds that fix a defect in title (MCL 207.526). A seller who paid and later decides the sale qualified can ask the Department of Treasury for a refund.

How a recorded sale changes the tax bill

Two notices reach the assessor. The office passes recorded transfers to local assessing officers at least monthly, and the buyer sends the assessor a transfer form no later than 45 days after closing. After a transfer, the taxable value is reset to state equalized value for the following year (MCL 211.27a). A cabin held since the 1970s can therefore carry a much higher bill under its next owner.

The county has 23,069 housing units for 23,459 residents, and 50.5% of those units are vacant, the mark of a seasonal market. Owners occupy 81.5% of the homes that have year-round residents.

Assessing is done by the townships and the village, so valuation questions belong with the local assessor named on the bill. The county treasurer issues certificates and takes transfer tax, and the Register of Deeds files the instrument itself.

Land contracts and long chains of title

The county grew fast after the war, from 2,055 residents in 1930 to 16,374 in 1980 and a peak of 25,469 in 2000. Parcels with long chains of deeds are common, so a title search can run back many owners.

Where a property was bought on a land contract, remember that the contract and the later deed are separate instruments. A land contract needs the treasurer's certificate, and under MCL 211.27a its taxable value resets for the year after the contract is signed, with no second reset once the deed is on file.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Roscommon County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to check before closing

Start with the parcel record on the county's search page, and confirm the owner of record, the legal description and any open mortgage. Then run through this list:

  • Decide whether the deed will carry a warranty covenant, because that triggers the certificate.
  • Request the certificate and the transfer tax amount from the treasurer ahead of closing.
  • State the full value on the deed, or prepare the valuation affidavit.
  • Phone 989-275-5931 for counter hours and how to submit the original.

Plan the order of events so nothing waits on another office. The treasurer's certificate has to exist before the register can file a warranty deed, and the transfer tax is due soon after the deed is delivered. If the buyer is paying with a loan, the lender will want the recorded deed back quickly, so ask the title agent how it plans to deliver the original and which office it expects to visit first.

Keep every receipt. The treasurer's payment, the recording fee and the transfer tax each come from a different step, and your closing statement should show all three so you can match them later.

A buyer's title agent will flag any lien, prior mortgage or unreleased discharge that shows in the record search, so clear those first. A cash buyer needs the same certificate, deed and tax payment. What a cash sale skips is lender underwriting, so closing can move faster once the treasurer's paperwork is in hand.

Frequently asked questions

What is the fee to file a deed in Roscommon County?

It is $30 per document, with $3 more for each extra instrument that one document assigns or discharges. Copies cost $1 a page and certification adds $5.

Is a treasurer's certificate needed for a quitclaim deed here?

Usually not, since a quitclaim deed with no warranty is outside MCL 211.135. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds and land contracts need the certificate from the County Treasurer.

Can a Roscommon County deed be e-recorded?

Mostly no. The county accepts no certified documents electronically apart from death certificates, so deeds go to the counter or through the mail.

Whose job is the transfer tax on a Roscommon County sale?

The seller covers it, and the county treasurer takes the payment inside the same short window. Conveyances to a son, daughter or grandchild, foreclosures and transfers under $100 are exempt.

Which phone number reaches the Roscommon County Register of Deeds?

Call 989-275-5931, or fax 989-275-8640. The office is at 500 Lake Street in Roscommon.

Address, hours and what the office does

The Register of Deeds is in the courthouse at 111 S. Michigan Avenue, Saginaw, MI 48602. Staff work weekdays from 8:00 until a quarter to five, with holidays off. Call (989) 790-5270 to reach the counter, or send a fax to (989) 790-5278. Counter hours can shift, so a quick phone call before you drive downtown is cheap insurance.

The register is an elected keeper of every real property record in the county. The office maintains the index and holds the original subdivision plats, and cities and townships call on it for liber and page references. Drafting and legal questions are off the table. The quitclaim deed form page says so plainly, so line up an attorney or title agent to write your deed.

For context, the 2020 census put the county at 190,124 people and 85,953 housing units, with 8.7% of the units vacant and 70.5% of occupied homes lived in by their owners.

Recording fees

The recording charge is $30 a document under MCL 600.2567, however many pages it runs. An assignment or discharge that reaches several instruments picks up $3 per extra instrument. The rest of the fee schedule looks like this:

  • Page copies at $1, with a $5 certification per document.
  • Counter searches at $5 apiece.
  • A free public workstation inside the office.
  • Tax certification, which the County Treasurer handles.

The counter takes cash, check, money order, American Express, Discover, Mastercard or Visa, and card payments add a fee. The Treasurer's certificate costs $5 for the first five parcel descriptions, then $1 more per description. Before you stand in line at the register, stop at the Treasurer in Room 107 to learn whether your instrument needs one.

Formatting rules that cause rejections

The county posts a long checklist built on Michigan's recording statutes. Each line carries a statute number, and a paper that fails any of them may come back unrecorded. The lines below apply to deeds signed after April 1, 1997.

Saginaw County recording checklist
RequirementWhat the checklist asks for
Paper and typeWhite paper of at least 20 pounds, legible, in 10-point type or larger
Page sizeAt least 8.5 by 11 inches and no larger than 8.5 by 14
Margins2.5 inches clear at the top of page one and half an inch on every other side
Title lineFirst line names the single recordable event the paper evidences
SignaturesOriginal, in black or dark blue ink, with the name printed beneath
Notary blockDated acknowledgment, printed notary name and commission expiration
Legal descriptionPlat caption and lot number, or quarter section, section, town and range if unplatted

More lines follow. A street or post office address for the grantee is required, and so is the drafter's name and address. Anyone signing after September 12, 2017 must black out the first five digits of a Social Security number, and foreign-language text needs a translation stapled behind it.

Transfer tax on a Saginaw County deed

The checklist states a rate of $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. Either the deed itself shows total consideration or a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit goes in with it. Where nothing is owed, the deed cites the exemption instead.

State law makes the seller responsible, with payment to the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery (MCL 207.523). MCL 207.526 exempts a handful of transfers, among them a land contract that leaves title with the vendor, a boundary line adjustment with no payment, a mineral rights conveyance, and a spouse's conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entirety.

Treat the transfer tax line as a closing cost you plan for, not a surprise. Your title company or closing attorney will usually calculate it from the contract price and deduct it from your proceeds. If you think your deal qualifies for an exemption, tell them before closing so the right statute gets cited on the deed.

A few papers need extra proof. If a deed names a survivor, the death certificate must be certified and either recorded separately or cited by liber and page. A court order arrives certified and sealed by the clerk. A release or assignment points back to the original liber and page or document number.

Working with three offices

The sequence usually runs like this. The assessor values the parcel, the treasurer collects what is owed and certifies the status, and the register records the deed and indexes it for anyone searching later. A seller who knows which desk answers which question wastes less time. Michigan leaves assessing and building permits with cities and townships, so a Saginaw County buyer or seller often deals with three offices: the township or city assessor, the county treasurer and this register. Each has its own counter and its own phone number. Parcels also sit in one of about twenty school districts, so name the district in your listing.

What the Treasurer adds to a deed transfer

Tax questions go to Room 107 in the same courthouse, open weekdays from eight to five. That office takes over delinquent real property tax, manages the Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund, and its head chairs the Land Bank Authority that handles tax foreclosed parcels. Without the certificate, state law keeps most warranty deeds off the record (MCL 211.135).

Back taxes can be paid at the counter, mailed to 111 S. Michigan Avenue or paid on the web around the clock. The web payment runs through an outside vendor that adds an access fee on the total. A card payment that is later reversed voids the payment, and the fees and interest reapply back to the original date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Saginaw County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a seller should prepare to file

Work through these steps in order:

  1. Look up the current deed and legal description on the office workstation.
  2. Learn from the Treasurer whether a certificate applies, and pay for it apart from recording.
  3. Show the price on the deed or prepare the valuation affidavit, and carry the tax payment.
  4. Compare margins, ink, notary block and grantee address with the checklist.
  5. Phone ahead about card fees and counter hours, and carry $30 per document.

After closing, the register passes transfers along to local assessors, and the buyer files a separate form with the assessor inside 45 days. Taxable value then resets to the state equalized value for the next year (MCL 211.27a). A cash buyer who closes quickly still needs every item above, because the checklist does not bend for speed. Paperwork prepared in advance is what lets a short closing stay short.

If the house is an inherited property, bring the certified death certificate and any court order so staff can see how the chain of title runs from the prior owner to you.

Frequently asked questions

What does recording cost at the Saginaw office?

Thirty dollars a document, plus $3 for every extra instrument one document assigns or discharges. Copies run $1 a page and certification costs $5.

Will staff draft my deed?

No. Staff cannot prepare documents or offer legal advice. The quitclaim deed page sells access to a blank form for $5 plus an access fee, and sends owners to an attorney for legal help.

How is the Saginaw County transfer tax stated?

The checklist gives $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. Sellers owe it, and an exempt transfer cites its exemption on the instrument.

Who issues the tax certificate?

The Saginaw County Treasurer issues it, and the register does not. The fee is $5 for up to five descriptions and $1 per description past that.

What number do I call for the register?

Call (989) 790-5270. The office is in the courthouse at 111 S. Michigan Avenue, and faxes go to (989) 790-5278.

Who records deeds in Sanilac County

Any paper that changes or burdens title to land in this county is filed with the recorder in Sandusky. Deeds, mortgages, land contracts, easements, liens, plats, surveys and court orders about real estate all get indexed there, using one uniform system and fees fixed by state law.

Drafting is outside the office's job. Staff will not write a deed or give legal advice, so have an attorney or title agent prepare yours. Once a document exists, the office answers practical questions at (810) 648-2313, and the county's department page links to forms, fee schedules and requirements.

A weekly land transfer list is posted on the same site, naming the parties and the section and township for each deed that cleared that week. Browsing a few weeks of it shows what land is moving near yours. Bring the legal description from your current deed when you visit or call, so any question about your parcel can be answered quickly.

Recording fees and transfer tax

Plan on $30 to put a deed on record, plus $8.60 in transfer taxes per $1,000 of price. These are the charges a seller meets most often.

Sanilac County charges around a sale
ChargeAmount
Base fee to record a deed or mortgage (MCL 600.2567)$30, whatever the length

Ask your closing agent to total these before the closing date so the figure on your settlement statement holds no surprises.

Who pays the transfer tax

The seller does. State law puts the tax on the grantor and gives 15 days after delivery of the deed to pay the county treasurer, though at the Sanilac counter it is collected as the deed is recorded.

Put the full value of the land on the face of the deed, or attach an affidavit stating it. A sale that bundles a house with furniture or equipment is taxed on the real estate alone when the two values are written separately.

Some deeds owe no tax. The state exemptions include:

  • a transfer for under $100;
  • family transfers from a parent to a child and from a grandparent to a grandchild;
  • a court-ordered transfer with no price set by the order;
  • a land contract, until title actually passes.

The county act has no family exemption, so a gift deed can skip the state share and still owe the county share. A deed with neither a price nor an exemption cited is returned.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Sanilac County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Formatting a deed for acceptance

MCL 565.201 sets the intake checklist, and the county reposts it on its real estate information page. In short, signatures need dark ink with printed names beneath them, the grantee's address and the drafter's details belong on the page, and page one needs a 2.5 inch clear top margin and a first line naming the type of recordable event.

Social Security numbers must be cut back to their last four digits, and non-English text needs a translation attached. A deed that clears every point cannot be refused for its content, while one that misses a point is sent back and the closing waits.

Have the drafter read the checklist against the finished deed before anyone signs. Fixing a margin on a draft costs nothing, and fixing it after a notary has signed means starting over.

Do warranty deeds need a tax certificate?

A warranty deed does. The treasurer must certify the property's tax status first for $5. Land contracts, assignments of them and any deed containing a warranty covenant follow the same path.

The county's schedule lists no such step for a plain quit claim deed. A quit claim hands over whatever the grantor owns with no promise about title, which suits relatives and estate cleanups but leaves a paying buyer exposed, so market-price buyers usually ask for a warranty deed.

Median home value in the county is $168,300, so the transfer tax on a typical sale is a real number to subtract when you compare offers.

Paying and searching records

The office takes cash, checks, money orders and debit or credit cards, with checks payable to the Sanilac County Register of Deeds. Card payers at the counter show photo ID, and an online payment location exists for remote payers.

Searching costs nothing at rod.sanilaccounty.net, where guest users can look through an index that begins in 1801. Page images come as PDFs at $1 a page, with a $5 charge on every order.

The office also runs a free property fraud alert. Enroll a parcel and the owner is told whenever something new is recorded against it, which helps with a farm field or lake cabin that nobody checks for weeks.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Sanilac County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Forms for sellers

The forms page carries three downloads: a warranty deed form, a quit claim deed form and an agricultural property affidavit form. The affidavit matters on farmland, where a buyer may need to state that qualified agricultural property will stay qualified agricultural property after the sale.

A separate packet covers manufactured homes. A seller whose home is a mobile or manufactured unit on owned land should ask the office about the Affidavit of Affixture, which the county lists beside the recording requirements and the transfer tax exemption statutes.

The same office is a U.S. passport acceptance facility, so a family selling a house and moving abroad can handle a passport application in the same trip. Hours and appointment rules change, so phone (810) 648-2313 before driving to Sandusky.

Selling in Sanilac County

Sanilac County fronts Lake Huron in the Thumb, and at 963 square miles of land it is the largest Lower Peninsula county by that measure. The 2020 population was 40,611. There are 17,516 households and 21,972 housing units, a gap of roughly 4,450 homes that fits a county of lakeshore cottages and houses left empty after a death or a move to town. Owners live in 82.6 percent of homes, and monthly owner cost with a mortgage is $1,226 against a median rent of $807.

Local families and lake-home shoppers make up much of the buyer pool, and an inland farmhouse reaches a different audience than a cottage at the shore. Level, rich soil keeps farming at the center of many parcels, so a buyer may care more about acreage and drainage than about the house itself. The four cities are Sandusky, Croswell, Marlette and Brown City, and Lexington, Port Sanilac and Carsonville see seasonal visitors.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Sanilac County Register of Deeds?

The office is in Sandusky, the county seat, and its phone number is (810) 648-2313. It records deeds and mortgages and does not prepare documents.

How much does a deed cost to record in Sanilac County?

The base charge is $30 for each document. A warranty deed adds a $5 treasurer's certificate, and transfer tax runs $8.60 per $1,000 of price, paid by the seller.

Can I search Sanilac County land records without an account?

Yes. The guest login at rod.sanilaccounty.net searches the index at no cost, and page images are $1 each plus a $5 order fee.

Which forms does the county offer for a farm or family sale?

The forms page lists a warranty deed, a quit claim deed and an agricultural property affidavit. Have an attorney check any form against your facts before you sign.

How far back do the online land records go?

The index at rod.sanilaccounty.net starts in 1801. Searching is free for guests, and image copies are $1 per page plus a $5 fee per order.

What the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds does

Corunna's courthouse holds the land records for every parcel in the county. Incoming papers are checked against the state recording act, numbered, timed and indexed, and the originals are stored for safekeeping. A question about who owns a given parcel gets answered from this office's books.

Shiawassee's books start in 1836. From 1954 on, records are scanned into the computer system, and all of it can be searched by liber and page. The address is the Circuit Courthouse, 208 N. Shiawassee Street, first floor, Corunna, MI 48817. Phone 989-743-2216 or write rod@shiawassee.net.

Office hours and payment

The counter is staffed on weekdays, 8:00 a.m. until noon, then 1:05 p.m. until 5:00 p.m. The search room closes a little earlier in each half of the day. On county holidays the office asks visitors to phone and book an appointment, so call ahead before carrying in a closing package.

Recording is paid in cash or by check made out to the Register of Deeds. Card payment covers copies and searches, with a $1.00 convenience fee when you print from the website.

What it costs to record a deed

Recording one instrument costs $30.00. A deed that carries a warranty clause also needs a $5.00 tax certificate under MCL 211.135. The treasurer issues it from the second floor of the courthouse (989-743-2224). Land contracts, their assignments and condominium master deeds need the same certificate.

Shiawassee County Register of Deeds fees
ServiceFee
Recording one instrument$30.00
Mortgage discharge or assignment, each added liber and page$3.00
Tax certificate$5.00
Plat, fixture filing (real estate only) or UCC$30.00 each
Copies$1.00 a page, $5.00 more to certify

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Shiawassee County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Michigan transfer tax in Shiawassee County

Recording a sale deed triggers a county tax under MCL 207.505 and a state tax under MCL 207.526. Shiawassee's schedule gives multipliers of .0075 for the state and .0011 for the county and tabulates the amounts in $500 bands. The first band, $100.00 up to $500, shows $3.75 state and $0.55 county.

  • Liability rests with the grantor.
  • The deed face shows total consideration and any claimed exemption.
  • A parcel crossing a county line splits the price between the two counties.
  • Stamps are sold only in the county of the land.
  • A Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit carries no filing fee.

Transfers that are exempt from the tax

The exemption list in MCL 207.505 excuses transfers priced under $100, mortgages and other security papers, leases, and spousal deeds that create or end a tenancy by the entireties. Relatives retitling a house commonly look at two items on that list: a corrective quitclaim, and a joint tenancy formed with someone who already owned the land. Ask the staff which subsection belongs on your deed.

What makes a Shiawassee County deed recordable?

The office posts a piece of Act 103 of 1937 (MCL 565.201) with its acceptance tests. Staff need the original paper with original signatures, a typed name under each signature, the grantee's address, a 2.5 inch blank band at the top of page one, and the drafter's name and address. The first five digits of any Social Security number must be removed.

A deed of unplatted land must also repeat the right-to-farm statement from MCL 560.109, warning that nearby farms may produce noise, dust and odors. When a spouse dies, the survivor brings a certified death certificate. No replacement deed is issued, since the office only records.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Shiawassee County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Sheriff's sales and other county offices

Sheriff's sales are held Wednesday mornings at 10:00 a.m. in the 35th Circuit Court lobby, and bidders need a certified check for the full opening bid. The office also links a property fraud alert service. Michigan leaves assessing and zoning to cities and townships, and the County Equalization department (989-743-2263) works across the county's 21 units of local government, fielding questions on valuation, millage and exemption status.

The county seat is Corunna, and Owosso is the largest city. Durand, Laingsburg, Perry and part of Ovid are the other cities. I-69 enters near the southwest corner and leaves east of Durand, and M-21 serves Corunna and Owosso.

Home values and ownership in the county

The 2025 estimate is 67,681 residents, against 70,648 in 2010. For 2020 through 2024 the county had 28,126 households, and owners occupy 80.1 percent of homes. The median value for a home lived in by its owner is $171,600. Median rent is $899, and median household income is $67,404.

At 128 people per square mile, most parcels sit outside a city street grid. A seller of rural land should expect the right-to-farm statement on the deed and may need extra time to gather a legal description.

Other county pages that help a seller

The Register of Deeds site links several pages worth reading before a closing:

  • A property fraud alert signup.
  • Sheriff sale information.
  • The county transfer tax exemption excerpt and the state exemption form.
  • The Michigan Homeowner Assistance Fund program at MSHDA, a starting point for owners who are behind on a mortgage.

The county treasurer collects and distributes tax roll levies for schools, townships, cities and villages, and its site includes a page for paying delinquent taxes online. Ask the treasurer for the balance on your parcel before you sign a purchase agreement, since the tax certificate on a warranty deed depends on those taxes being current.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Getting a deed ready for closing

Give the title company or attorney your current deed and parcel details early. They draft the new deed with the full consideration or the exemption statute, add the drafter's name and address, and make sure the original signatures and notary are in place. For a warranty deed, the treasurer certification comes first. Then the signed original goes to the Corunna office, with the $30.00 fee, the $5.00 certificate and the transfer tax. A cash sale skips the lender, so the recording step is often the last thing between you and your funds. Ask the title company to confirm the transfer tax figure and the recording total in writing before the signing, and keep your recorded copy once the office returns it with the recording details stamped on it.

Frequently asked questions

What will it cost me to put a sale deed on record in Corunna?

The filing charge is $30.00 per paper. If the deed has a warranty clause, add the $5.00 certificate from the treasurer next door, plus the state and county transfer taxes calculated on the price.

Is the buyer or the seller responsible for transfer tax in Shiawassee County?

The seller carries it. The county's posted schedule applies .0075 for the state and .0011 for the county against the price on the deed.

Will the office accept a scanned or photocopied deed?

No, it wants the signed original. Once it is on record, anyone can order a plain copy at $1.00 a page or a certified copy for an extra $5.00.

If my husband or wife died, do I receive a fresh deed?

No. Take a certified death certificate and the filing fee to the courthouse so the record shows the deceased owner is off the title. Your existing deed continues to apply.

How do I reach the Shiawassee County deeds office?

Go to the first floor of the Circuit Courthouse at 208 N. Shiawassee Street, Corunna, MI 48817, or dial 989-743-2216. On county holidays the office asks visitors to book an appointment.

Where to take a deed or mortgage for recording

The Register of Deeds is in Suite 400 of the Purdy Building, 125 W. Lincoln Street, Caro, MI 48723. It opens at 8:00 a.m. and closes at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, with a lunch closure from noon until 1:00 p.m., and it shuts for holidays. Call 989-672-3840 or write to registerofdeeds@tuscolacounty.org.

You can walk a document in or send it by mail. A mailed packet needs the exact fee and a stamped return envelope. Cash, money orders and checks are all taken. Checks must print both the account holder's name and the bank's name and address, and they cannot be stale-dated. A wrong amount gets the whole request rejected, so count twice before sealing the envelope.

Caro is the county seat, and the county lies in Michigan's Thumb. Recording is the final step of a sale, so confirm with your title company who is carrying the deed to the counter and when.

Recording charges

A single $30.00 charge covers entering and recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, certified copy or other instrument. Papers that discharge or assign several older records add to it.

Tuscola County recording and copy fees
ServiceCharge
Recording one instrument (deed, mortgage, lis pendens and similar)$30.00 flat
Every extra liber and page assigned, discharged, indexed or posted$3.00 extra
Photocopy, real estate record$1.00 a page
Certifying a copy$5.00 a document
Tax lien search certificate, state or federal$3.00 a name

Four dollars of every recording fee funds the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation program. Fixture filings, lien documents, state deeds, plats and tax reversion papers skip that portion. Copies are paid for at the time of purchase, and a mailed order must give the liber and page. Fixture filings are recorded here at $30.00, while UCC filings go to the Secretary of State instead of Caro.

Why a warranty deed visits the Treasurer first

State law (MCLA 211.135) requires proof that taxes are paid before some papers reach the recorder. Three types go to the Tuscola County Treasurer first: warranty deeds, land contract assignments with a warranty clause, and condominium master deeds. The Treasurer's certification costs $5.00 per document.

When the stamped document comes back, send it on to Caro in recording order with the exact fee. The Treasurer, at the same street address, answers certification questions at 989-672-3890.

Sellers carrying unpaid tax feel this step most. Settle early with your title company or closing attorney, who will order the certificate, since each mailed round trip adds days to a closing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tuscola County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Paperwork mistakes that get a recording returned?

Staff check each submission against the Recording Requirements list, which starts from MCL 565.201. A document that misses any item goes back to the sender.

  • Original signatures, each with the signer's name typed or printed beneath it. Fax and photocopy versions are refused.
  • An acknowledgement by a notary, judge or court clerk on any paper that conveys or burdens Michigan land.
  • A mailing address for every grantee, plus the name and address of whoever drafted the paper.
  • Black print of 10 points or larger on white paper between letter and legal size, leaving a blank 2 1/2 inches atop page one and 1/2 inch on other margins.
  • No more than four sequential Social Security digits anywhere on the page.
  • One recordable event per instrument, named on the first line of print.

Court orders and death certificates are recordable only as certified copies, and a survivor deed needs the death certificate recorded or referenced by liber and page. Staff do not draft deeds, answer legal questions or hand out blank forms, so use an attorney or title company for wording.

Transfer tax on a recorded deed

Recording a sale brings two charges. The county's is in MCL 207.504: 55 cents per $500 of value, with any leftover under $500 counted as a full unit, for counties below 2,000,000 people. The state's is in MCL 207.525, at $3.75 for each $500 or fraction.

Value must appear on the face of the deed or in an attached affidavit. The whole consideration is taxed unless the paper cites a valid exemption.

  • Both acts exempt consideration under $100, security instruments, leases and certain land contracts.
  • The state act, MCL 207.526, adds conveyances from an individual to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, plus foreclosure transfers.
  • The county act's list, MCL 207.505, lacks the family exemption. Ask the office how the county share applies when a parent deeds a house to a child.

Searching and monitoring land records

Online indexes start in December 1988, and the vault holds land records back to 1852 for visitors. Every index is by grantor and grantee name. There is no search by street address or parcel number, and the office keeps land records only, so it cannot tell you a build date.

Copies of recorded documents are open to anyone, since recording makes them public. Residents can sign up for Property Alert, an email notice whenever a paper under their name is recorded. It works as a heads-up, and a common name will trigger false alarms. If an alert shows a document you do not recognize, phone the office.

Staff run only simple searches for a small fee and cannot say who owns a parcel. An attorney or title company reaches that conclusion.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tuscola County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling when the property taxes are behind

The Tuscola County Treasurer works with delinquent owners to head off foreclosure and lays out three paths: keep the property, sell it, or let foreclosure proceed. Forfeiture comes first and is not foreclosure. During it, the county adds a title search fee of at least $175 plus recording costs, and interest climbs to 18% a year (1.5% monthly), reaching back to the start of the delinquency.

A year after forfeiture, foreclosure follows. The owner's interest and every lien are wiped out, redemption ends, and the parcel is prepared for auction. Listings usually appear in early August for the August and October auctions. For a bill you dispute, or for a Principal Residence, veteran or hardship exemption, call your township assessor.

Selling before forfeiture is the cheaper route. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff, pay it from proceeds at closing, and the Treasurer's certificate can issue so the warranty deed records on schedule. A cash sale works the same way and can close fast, as long as the payoff is settled.

Homeownership in the county is high at 86.4%, and the median owner-occupied value is $149,500.

Frequently asked questions

What will a Tuscola County recording cost me?

Expect $30.00 flat per instrument, with $3.00 more for each extra liber and page. Transfer tax comes on top, figured on the total consideration unless the document states an exemption.

Does a Tuscola County warranty deed need a tax certificate first?

Yes. Send the document to the Tuscola County Treasurer first with the $5.00 certification fee, then submit the stamped document to the Register of Deeds with exact recording fees. The Treasurer's phone is 989-672-3890.

Can a Tuscola County deed be found by street address?

No. Indexing is by name only. Search by grantor or grantee, or bring the liber and page. Online indexes start December 1, 1988.

Who may order a copy of a Tuscola County deed?

Anyone may. Each page costs $1.00, certifying a copy adds $5.00 per document, and a mailed order needs a self-addressed stamped envelope.

Which transfer tax rates apply to a Tuscola County sale?

The county charges 55 cents and the state $3.75, each for every $500 of value. The value comes from the instrument or an attached affidavit.
