Where to take a deed in Van Buren County

Paperwork for Van Buren County land goes to the Register of Deeds in Suite 102 at 219 E. Paw Paw Street, Paw Paw. The counter is open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 5:00 in the afternoon and closed on holidays. Call (269) 657-8242 with questions.

The office accepts originals bearing real signatures and court papers that carry a certification. Photocopies and faxes are refused.

Clerks read each paper against state requirements, scan and index it, then hand the original back to the sender. The county promises a turnaround of one to two days for a compliant paper. When a title company runs your closing, that company gets the original first, so ask them when it will be passed along to you.

Recording charges

A single flat price covers any length of deed or mortgage, and the figures match MCL 600.2567.

Van Buren County Register of Deeds charges
ServicePriceNotes
Record a deed or mortgage$30.00Pages do not change the price; $4.00 of it funds the state survey and remonumentation program

Walk-in and mailed recording payments must be cash or a check written to Register of Deeds. A card is accepted only for copies bought online. Mail a stamped return envelope with your package so the original finds its way back.

When a deed needs the treasurer's stamp first

Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments that carry a warranty promise must arrive with a county treasurer's tax certificate. The rule traces to MCL 211.135, which wants proof that five years of taxes before the instrument date are paid and a statement on tax liens or tax titles. Quitclaim deeds without warranty covenants escape it.

  • Get the certificate before you head to Paw Paw, because the recording desk will refuse a warranty deed without it.
  • Budget $5.00 for it in addition to the $30.00 recording price.
  • Any unpaid tax usually comes out of your proceeds, so ask the county treasurer for the figure early enough to plan the closing date.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Van Buren County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How does transfer tax work on a house sale?

The seller pays when value reaches $100.00. The county rate is $0.55 and the state rate is $3.75, each applied to every $500 or fraction of $500, under MCL 207.504 and MCL 207.525.

Show the full price on the deed or file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit, which is free. For swaps, each deed is taxed on its own property's real value. A parcel that straddles county lines needs a price per parcel and a payment to each county.

Delivery of the deed starts a 15-day clock for paying the county treasurer under MCL 207.523. A sale later found exempt can be refunded through the state Treasury, provided the form goes in within four years of payment.

Some transfers are exempt under MCL 207.526, such as these:

  • Gifts from a parent to a child, stepchild or adopted child.
  • Gifts from a grandparent to a grandchild.
  • Corrective deeds that confirm title the buyer already has.
  • Court orders that move property with no stated price.

What the office asks for by document type

Every paper needs a date and a legal description. Beyond that, the requirements differ by document type, and two stand out for sellers dealing with a distressed property.

  • A sheriff's sale or foreclosure by advertisement comes with the auction sale amount, a signed and notarized auctioneer statement, a Soldiers and Sailors affidavit if it applies, the newspaper publication notice, an affidavit of posting, a redemption period statement and an affidavit of redemption.
  • A tax deed or similar paper carries the $5.00 treasurer certificate.
  • Releases and assignments cross-reference the original by liber and page.
  • A land patent must be an original or certified copy.

General rules track MCL 565.201. Names are typed under signatures and match the notary block, every party's address appears, the drafter is identified and the notary acknowledgment is complete. Leave 2 1/2 inches clear at the top of page one, use 10-point type or bigger and keep sheets to 8.5 by 14 inches at most. Wrong fees, missing drafter names, handwritten names and partial notary certificates are the usual causes of rejection.

A certified death certificate must back any deed that names a survivor. The office cannot draft documents or give legal advice, so see a lawyer or title agent for wording.

Searching deed records

The Register of Deeds portal at deeds.vanburencountymi.gov lets anyone search the index and buy images one document at a time. A BS&A property search from the county site also lists the liber and page in each legal description, and the sale history section can fill in gaps.

Paying for an older record depends on its volume. Liber 924 or lower is paid through the county's GovPayNow link. Liber 925 and higher is bought from the searchable index and downloads right after payment. Online copy orders may take up to two working days, and big orders on the portal may take up to 48 hours. Recorded papers are public, so anyone can request a copy of any deed.

Selling a home in Van Buren County

The county covers 1,090 square miles, 482 of them water, with farmland, small towns and lakeshore making up the rest. Paw Paw is the seat. Bangor, Gobles, Hartford and part of South Haven are cities, while Decatur, Lawton, Mattawan, Lawrence, Bloomingdale and Paw Paw are villages. Antwerp and Almena townships, beside Kalamazoo County, are turning suburban.

Many inland lakes are ringed by year-round homes and cottages, and Lake Michigan beaches, Van Buren State Park and the Kal-Haven Trail draw visitors. Highways include I-94, I-196, US 31 and M-40, and an Amtrak Pere Marquette stop serves the county.

Of 30,622 households, 80.6 percent own. Owner-occupied homes are valued at $206,500 at the median, and gross rent runs $870. Zoning and building permits come from the township or city, so call the local hall about those before you list.

Plan the paperwork backward from closing day: order the treasurer's certificate, confirm the transfer tax with the title agent, and make sure the deed meets the format rules above. A cash buyer closes quickly, but the recording desk works at the same pace either way.

Frequently asked questions

What is the recording price in Van Buren County?

$30.00 per instrument, whatever the page count. Add $3.00 for each further instrument assigned or discharged. Certified copies and treasurer tax certificates cost $5.00, and photocopies cost $1.00 a page.

Does the Van Buren County Register of Deeds take credit cards?

Only for copies ordered online. Anything you file, along with the transfer tax, must be paid in cash or by check made out to Register of Deeds.

Who owes transfer tax on a Van Buren County sale?

The seller, when the property's value is $100.00 or more. County tax is $0.55 and state tax is $3.75 for each $500 or fraction of $500.

How fast does the Van Buren County office record a deed?

Within one to two days of receipt, if the paper meets the requirements. Wrong fees, missing drafter names, handwritten names and incomplete notary certificates get it sent back.

Is a treasurer's certificate needed for a Van Buren County quitclaim deed?

No. Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments with a warranty covenant need it. A quitclaim deed without warranty covenants is excused under MCL 211.135.

What the Washtenaw County deed office holds

Land research in Washtenaw County runs through the Register of Deeds. Its files include deeds, mortgages and foreclosure records, along with other real and personal property papers. The register works inside the joint Clerk / Register of Deeds department, and inspection is open to all comers.

The office's main page links to recording rules, record searches and requests, eRecording, a fee schedule and a transfer tax explainer. Copies bought through the online land record search need a login.

Recording finishes a sale, because the buyer is shielded from later claimants only once the deed is on file. Closings usually pass the signed deed to a title company, which can tell you the recording date and supply a recorded copy for your files.

Can a deed be filed electronically?

Yes. Approved vendors carry electronic filings to the Register of Deeds, and lenders and title agents depend on that route. An owner who signs outside a title closing typically files on paper, by mail or at the Ann Arbor counter.

Before sending a deed, read the recording requirements page, because a paper with layout defects is returned unrecorded. The fee schedule page shows the county's price for each service.

  • Keep the original signed deed in hand until the county accepts it.
  • Ask which payment types the office takes for your kind of filing.
  • Request your recorded deed before listing, so the buyer's title agent has the legal description early.

Recording fees and transfer tax rates

State law sets the starting figures for every Michigan register of deeds, and Washtenaw applies them. The table pairs each charge with its section number. The statute text is on the Michigan Legislature site.

Statutory charges on a Washtenaw County deed filing

Who pays transfer tax, and what avoids it

The tax lands on the seller. MCL 207.523 makes the grantor liable and sets a 15-day window, running from delivery of the deed, for payment to the county treasurer. The county's explainer adds a rule that trips people up. Collection is automatic unless the deed qualifies and states the reason on its face.

So any exemption you intend to use has to be written into the deed. MCL 207.526 lists the categories, including:

  • Spouses creating or ending a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A parent or grandparent deeding to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild.
  • A boundary line correction where no money changes hands.
  • A joint tenancy in which one co-owner already holds title.
  • A deed given through foreclosure or as a substitute for it.

A payer who later learns that an exemption applied can request a refund from the state Treasury department under subsection (4) of the section on liability.

Does a warranty deed need a tax certificate?

Usually. MCL 211.135 has registers of deeds ask for treasurer certificates whenever a deed or land contract is presented. They disclose tax liens or tax titles and confirm that the five years of tax before the instrument date were paid.

A quitclaim deed carrying no warranty covenants gets a pass, and so do sheriff's deeds and a handful of other types. If you are signing an ordinary warranty deed, line up the certificate first.

When back tax is owed, the county treasurer will quote a payoff. Pay it by closing and the certificate follows, which lets the deed go to the recorder without delay.

Deed formatting rules

Format rules are in MCL 565.201, and a register must refuse any paper that breaks them. Check these before anyone signs.

  • Line one of the printed text names the one recordable event, for instance warranty deed.
  • Black ink on white stock of 20-pound weight or heavier, with type no smaller than 10 points.
  • 2 1/2 inches blank above the text on page one and half an inch on every remaining edge.
  • A mailing address for each grantee, and the drafter's name with a business address.
  • Social Security numbers trimmed to the final four digits.
  • A stapled English translation on any paper written partly in another language.

The office also enrolls people in Fraud Guard alerts, which warn you when a paper is recorded under your name. It is a sensible precaution while a house sits listed or vacant. Two other county pages cover older paperwork: discharging prohibited deed restrictions, such as covenants that discriminated by race or religion, and the Michigan Construction Lien Act, which matters if contractors recently worked on the house.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Washtenaw County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

A seller's checklist for recording

  1. Ask the title company whether your deed is a warranty or a quitclaim, since that decides whether a treasurer's certificate is needed.
  2. Get a payoff figure from the Washtenaw County Treasurer if any tax is owing.
  3. Decide whether an exemption applies and make sure the deed states the reason on its face.
  4. Check the format rules before signing, with the first line naming the recordable event.
  5. Pay transfer tax to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed if the closing agent is not collecting it.
  6. Ask for the recorded copy so your own files show the recording date.

A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but not the recording steps, so the same list applies. Bring the parcel number and the legal description to any call with the office, since staff will ask for one or the other. If the title company is handling everything, ask for a short written timeline that shows who files the deed and who pays the tax, and keep it with your closing papers.

Washtenaw County homes and local offices

Ann Arbor is the county seat. Chelsea, Dexter, Manchester, Saline, Ypsilanti and the northern slice of Milan are the other cities, with Barton Hills a village and Whitmore Lake a census community. Main roads are I-94, US 23, US 12, M-14, M-17 and M-52.

The county has 165,103 housing units, and owners occupy 61.6 percent of homes. The middle owner-occupied value is $374,100. Typical household income is $89,180 and typical gross rent is $1,463. Zoning, building permits and assessing belong to local units, so ask the city or township about any open permit before you list.

Frequently asked questions

Does Washtenaw County take electronic deed filings?

Yes, through eRecording vendors the Register of Deeds has approved. Lenders and title companies use that route most often.

Who is responsible for transfer tax in a Washtenaw County sale?

The seller owes it. Counting both levels, that is 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state on each $500 of value, and the county treasurer wants payment within 15 days of the deed being delivered.

Does my Washtenaw County deed have to name a transfer tax exemption?

Yes. The county collects unless the deed is exempt and says why on its face, so spell out the statutory reason before you sign.

What tax paperwork goes with a Washtenaw County warranty deed?

A county treasurer's certificate that shows no tax liens or titles and five earlier years of paid tax. A quitclaim deed without warranty covenants does not need one.

Where can I confirm the Washtenaw County recording fee?

Check the Register of Deeds fee schedule page, which covers recording, copies, searches, transfer tax and tax certificates. State law sets the starting recording charge at $30.00 per document.

Where to take a deed for recording

Recording happens at the Wayne County Register of Deeds, 400 Monroe, 7th floor, in the Greektown neighborhood of downtown Detroit. The Treasurer's deed certification desk is in that building too, on the 5th floor.

Since October 1, 2025 the office no longer takes walk-ins. Service is by appointment, and nobody can wait on the floor for a cancellation. The day's first slots begin at 8:00 AM and the last begin at 3:50 PM. A 20 minute slot handles up to five documents, while a 45 minute slot is reserved for high volume customers filing five to 25. One person per appointment may enter. The scheduling help line is 313-224-5860, and the recording help line is 313-224-5851.

Mailing documents in is also allowed. Recorded papers come back the way they arrived. An agent who hand delivered them must collect them in person, and mailed ones return to the address typed on the document, which is often the attorney's or the title agent's, not the buyer's.

Recording fees

The fee schedule changed on January 1, 2026, the first rise since 1996. For a deed, mortgage or similar instrument the charge is $26.00 plus a $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee, which adds up to $30.00 for each document no matter how many pages it runs.

Wayne County Register of Deeds and Treasurer charges
ServiceCharge
Recording a deed or mortgage$26.00 plus $4.00 state fee
Property search at the office$5.00 (waived for your own home with proof)
Search by mail$15.00 per address
Copies$2.00 per page
Certifying a recorded document$10.00 each
Online account, 15 minutes$6
Online account, 60 minutes$24
Treasurer's deed certification$5.00 per document, up to 25 parcel numbers

Wayne County's charges differ from other counties, so a figure you hear elsewhere may not apply here.

How the county collects transfer tax

The Register states the formula: $0.55 per $500 of consideration for the county, $3.75 per $500 for the state, which the office also expresses as $8.60 per $1,000. The tax is collected when the deed is filed unless an exemption is noted on it, and accepted forms are cash, check or money order, payable to that office.

Exemptions are listed in MCL 207.526 and, for the county tax, MCL 207.505. A deed claiming one must cite the statute and subparagraph. Typical examples seen in a house sale:

  • consideration below $100
  • a gift deed running down to a son, daughter or grandchild
  • a deed issued in foreclosure or instead of foreclosure
  • a land contract whose title has not yet passed to the buyer
  • a court order with no stated price

Sellers who held a principal residence exemption should also read subsection (u) of the state act. It excuses certain arm's-length sales where the state equalized value never rose above the first value set after the home was built or bought, and a refund can be requested when tax was paid on such a sale.

What payment does the counter accept?

Debit and credit cards work at the counter when the cardholder shows matching ID. So do money orders, cashier's checks, certified checks, corporation checks and law firm checks. Two card brands, American Express and Discover, are refused. Personal checks are turned away at the window yet welcome in the mail, and cards cannot be used for mailed filings.

Each document needs its own check for fees plus any tax. The office is strict about amounts:

  • Underpaying returns both document and check.
  • An overpayment above $25.00 also returns everything.
  • An overpayment of $25.00 or less is kept and not refunded.
  • Several documents on one check travel as a group, and if one fails, all come back.

Title companies handle this routinely. If you are recording a family transfer on your own, work out the exact figure first.

What a deed needs to be accepted

The county posts a checklist and a list of common rejection reasons. The main points are original signatures with names typed, printed or stamped under them, a notary acknowledgment on any real estate deed signed in Michigan, plus the preparer's name and address.

  • Pages meet the office's size, margin, ink and type rules, with a deep blank top margin on page one.
  • The document's title sits on the first line, and the parcel number and street address are shown.
  • A full legal description appears, including plat liber and page or condominium details where they apply.
  • Any Social Security number has its first five digits removed or hidden.
  • A death certificate is an original certified by the clerk, and a court order is certified and sealed.

The register does not furnish blank forms and cannot give legal advice. An attorney is the office's recommendation for drafting.

Why the Treasurer certifies a deed first

MCL 211.135 bars the register from recording until a treasurer's certificate shows the parcel's taxes current for the prior five years. Wayne County requires the Treasurer's stamp on warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts and their assignments.

Only originals can be certified. Make a separate appointment with the Treasurer, or send the original by UPS, FedEx or USPS with a check payable to the Wayne County Treasurer and a stamped return envelope. The Treasurer sends it back and you forward it for recording. A document listing more than 25 parcels pays $5.00 plus 20 cents per extra parcel.

Unpaid tax is the usual snag. A bill left unpaid at the local office past the end of February is delinquent from March 1 and then payable only to the county. After a full year it is forfeited, the interest climbs to 1.5% a month, and a $175 foreclosure fee plus $30 in recording charges join the balance.

Booking and timing in a large county

The office calls itself the library of land records for nearly 900,000 parcels, filed by liber and page back to 1703. Wayne County has 814,793 housing units, and 64.8% of homes are owner-occupied. The median value of an owned home is $178,500.

At that volume, appointments fill up. Reserve one early when a closing depends on a recorded deed, and ask the title company which of your documents need Treasurer certification beforehand.

How can you find or copy a recorded deed?

You can use the land records website, visit the office, or request a search by mail. The website is open around the clock. A free name search shows a list of recorded documents by grantor or grantee but not the documents themselves. A paid On-Demand Account adds searches by address, legal description, parcel number or liber and page, and printing costs $2 per page. Certified copies are not sold online.

Lobby kiosks allow self-service searching. Current and former service members can get a search of their own property and its copies at no charge with credentials, though businesses are excluded. A mailed request needs a short description, a check payable to the Wayne County Register of Deeds, and the address 400 Monroe, 7th Floor, Detroit, MI 48226. Ask the office which years of images your search needs before you buy an online session.

Frequently asked questions

What does Wayne County charge for one recorded document?

The charge is $30.00, made up of $26.00 plus the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee. A warranty deed also needs Treasurer certification at $5.00. The current schedule began January 1, 2026.

Can I just show up at 400 Monroe to record a deed?

No. Since October 1, 2025 service is by appointment only. Choose record, search or kiosk on the county's calendar, or call 313-224-5860 for help booking.

How much transfer tax does Wayne County print per $500?

The county prints $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, or $8.60 per $1,000. The seller pays at recording unless the deed cites an exemption.

Will the Register of Deeds write my deed for me?

No. The office provides no blank documents and may not give legal advice. It points owners to an attorney who can prepare a deed that meets the recording rules.

What gets a Wayne County deed sent back?

A photocopied signature, no stated price or exemption, wrong margins or type size, a thin legal description, or no treasurer certification. Rejected papers return with the check so you can fix and refile.

Selling in Wexford County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Office location and mailing

The Wexford County Register of Deeds is at 437 E. Division St., Cadillac, on the second floor of the older section of the courthouse. The main entrance and parking lot are behind the building. Mail goes to P.O. Box 303, Cadillac, MI 49601, and the phone is (231) 779-9455.

To drive in from downtown Cadillac, head east on Harris Street, go four blocks, and look to the left.

You can mail a filing. Send it with the fees and a stamped, self-addressed envelope for the return. State law does not allow recording a photocopy, so the sheet you send must be the original with original signatures.

Recording fees and extra charges

Every document costs $30.00 to record, however many pages it has. That amount includes the Michigan remonumentation fee and the Register's automation fee, and it has been the statewide figure since October 1, 2016. The office takes cash, checks and credit cards. Make checks payable to Register of Deeds.

  • Tax certification, $5.00, is required on every warranty deed and land contract.
  • A discharge or assignment that covers several instruments adds $3.00 per instrument beyond the base $30.00.
  • A fixture filing costs $30.00.
  • Copies run $1.00 a page, and certifying a document is $5.00.
  • Name searches cost $5.00 each plus $0.50 per year. UCC searches are $6.00 a name, and state, federal, MESC or judgment searches are $3.00 a name.
  • A track index request is $50 an hour, or $25 for half an hour.
  • Emailing a request adds a $3.00 convenience fee.

The counter also sells fill-in-the-blank quit claim, warranty and mineral deeds and non-construction liens for $5.00 each. Staff do not draft legal papers or advise on wording, and the office suggests hiring an attorney for any deed.

Transfer tax on a sale

The county prints a table that splits each $500 price band into a state share and a county share. One check payable to the Wexford County Register of Deeds can cover transfer tax, tax certification and recording together.

Opening price bands of the Wexford County transfer tax table
Sale price bandState taxCounty taxTotal
$100.01 to $500$3.75$0.55$4.30
$500.01 to $1,000$7.50$1.10$8.60
$1,000.01 to $1,500$11.25$1.65$12.90

Each further $500 band repeats the same pair of amounts. The printed table stops at $100,000, so for a typical home price, ask the counter staff for the exact tax before you write the check. If the sale is exempt, the exemption must be cited on the deed itself: MCL 207.505 for the county tax and MCL 207.526 for the state tax.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wexford County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What a deed must contain to be recorded

The county posts seventeen numbered rules with statute citations, and every deed is checked against them. The ones that trip people up most:

  • Names typed or printed under the original signatures must match the names in the notary's acknowledgment.
  • Each deed or assignment gives the grantee's street or post office address and the drafter's name and address.
  • Page one leaves 2.5 inches blank at the top, and every page keeps a half inch around the other edges. Ink is black, type is at least 10 point, and the paper is white, at least 20 pound, and between letter and legal size.
  • The first line of print says what the paper does, such as a warranty deed.
  • If the deed claims survivorship, a certified death certificate or proof of death is already recorded or referenced by liber and page.
  • A court order carries the clerk's certification and seal.

Unplatted land needs two more statements. One says whether the right to make further divisions under the Land Division Act is being conveyed. The other is the Michigan right to farm notice about nearby agricultural operations.

Electronic recording

Most paper types can be e-recorded. Court certified documents and anything needing tax certification are excluded, so warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, their assignments, plats and condominium documents must still be filed on paper.

E-recording is processed from 8:30 A.M. to 4:30 P.M., Monday to Friday, except county holidays. Payment goes by ACH under vendor agreements. Only fees set by state and local statute reach the county, and vendors can add their own charges. A submission that breaks the Michigan Recording Act can be rejected, and a filer who violates the state's e-recording standards is cut off until further notice. The vendors in use are CSC eRecording, Simplifile, ePN and Indecomm.

Records affected by the 2024 cyber incident

A cyber incident on November 5, 2024 kept the office from recovering under 5% of documents first recorded between August 14, 2024 and October 30, 2024. If you sent papers for recording in that stretch, call the office to learn whether yours survived or must be recorded again. A seller who closed in those months should make that call before listing.

The online land records search is hosted through the county website, and the office's holdings go back to 1864. Duplicate microfilm sits in underground storage in Grand Rapids. Once a document is recorded, anyone may request a copy for $1.00 a page. The office will fax prepaid copies but will not email them.

The office also runs a Fraud Notify service that watches for recordings under a name or business name. Ask the office how to enroll.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wexford County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Taxes, deeds and closing

MCL 211.135 keeps a warranty deed from being recorded until a treasurer's certificate shows the prior five years of tax paid. That is what the $5.00 certification line buys. Any balance owed on the parcel has to be settled by closing, so check with the treasurer early if you think something is outstanding.

Family situations come up often. If a spouse dies and both names were on the deed, bring a certified death certificate and the fee. No new deed is issued, because the office only records. A paid-off mortgage produces a discharge from the lender, not a deed. Adding or removing a name affects divorce, borrowing, taxes and probate, so talk to an attorney first. Once the sale closes, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor a transfer notice (MCL 211.27a).

A cash sale does not change any of this. The deed still needs the same signatures, the same tax certification and the same fees, but it skips lender paperwork and the delays that come with underwriting.

Local housing context

Wexford County sits in the Northern Lower Peninsula and holds much of the Manistee National Forest. Population is 34,445, with 16,924 housing units. About 80.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, the middle value of an owned home is $170,400, and median household income is $61,085. Many parcels are rural, so the land division and farm notice statements above come up more often here than they would on a platted city lot.

Frequently asked questions

What is the per-document recording charge in Wexford County?

It is $30.00, which includes the Michigan remonumentation and Register of Deeds automation fees. Warranty deeds add $5.00 for tax certification, and discharges covering several instruments add $3.00 for each.

Can a warranty deed go through e-recording in Wexford County?

No. Warranty deeds and land contracts need tax certification, so they go in on paper: the original, with original signatures, delivered or mailed with fees and a stamped return envelope.

Will Wexford County staff advise me on wording my deed?

No. The office prepares no legal documents and gives no legal advice. It sells blank fill-in forms for $5.00 and recommends an attorney.

How can I find the owner of a Wexford County parcel?

Ask the County Equalization Department or the assessor for the city, township or village. They can give the name on the tax roll, which may differ from the owner, and that name opens a search of the Register's records.

Do I get a new deed after paying off a Wexford County mortgage?

No. The lender sends a discharge, release or satisfaction of mortgage to be recorded. Your deed remains the one from purchase, and a recorded copy costs $1.00 per page.
